definition_zh: 系统地；有条理地；按既定步骤逐一地
definition_en: in a way that follows a fixed method or plan, step by step, so that nothing is left to chance
core_image: 一张按编号逐格填满的清单，每一格都对应一个固定步骤，格子依次被勾掉
scene: The team systematically checked every plot for signs of the disease.
sceneCN: 这里 systematically 指「系统地」（第 1 个义项：按既定方法一步一步执行）；句意：团队系统地检查了每一块样地有无该病害的迹象。图中可辨识物件：编号样方、记录板、逐格勾选的清单。

pos.zh: 系统地；有条理地；按部就班地（由形容词 systematic 加 -ally 构成，修饰动作的执行方式）

collocations.zh: 一贯地无视；成体系地忽视

forms.label: 易混形容词
forms.form: systemic（系统的；全身的；体制层面的，见 similar 第一组）

derivatives.zh: 系统的；有条理的；按计划的
系统的；全身的；体制性的（与 systematic 不同，见 similar）

senses.title: By Fixed Method
senses.titleCN: 按既定方法：一步一步来
senses.definition: in a way that follows a fixed method or plan
senses.definitionCN: 按既定方法或计划地；有步骤地
senses.example: The samples were systematically labelled before any test began.
senses.exampleCN: 任何测试开始之前，样品都被系统地贴上了标签。
senses.why: Systematic work follows a system, that is, a set of steps kept in the same order each time. The adverb -ally says the action is carried out in exactly that order.
senses.whyCN: systematic 的工作遵循一个 system，也就是每次顺序相同的一套步骤；副词词尾 -ally 表示动作正是按这个顺序执行的。

senses.title: Covering Everything
senses.titleCN: 全面的：一处不漏
senses.definition: in a way that covers every part of a set, leaving nothing out
senses.definitionCN: 全面地；无遗漏地覆盖每一部分
senses.example: She systematically searched every drawer for the missing key.
senses.exampleCN: 她把每个抽屉都系统地搜了一遍，寻找丢失的钥匙。
senses.why: If you go through all the members of a set in order, the set is covered. The word then carries the force of 'nothing skipped', which is why it pairs naturally with search, check and review.
senses.whyCN: 如果按顺序走遍一个集合的所有成员，这个集合就被覆盖了。此时该词带有「一处未漏」的力量，因此常与 search、check、review 搭配。

senses.title: As a Settled Policy
senses.titleCN: 一贯地：成体系地（常含贬义）
senses.definition: as a repeated, deliberate pattern, often with disapproval
senses.definitionCN: 作为反复而蓄意的做法，常带批评语气
senses.example: The report was systematically ignored by the department.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告被该部门一贯地无视。
senses.why: A repeated pattern that looks planned rather than accidental is called systematic. The adverb then accuses someone of doing the same thing on purpose, again and again.
senses.whyCN: 一种看起来经过安排、而非偶然的重复模式，就叫 systematic；这个副词因此是在指责某人一次又一次地故意这么做。

senses.title: Across a Whole System
senses.titleCN: 从系统整体看：整体存在差异
senses.definition: with respect to a whole system rather than one of its parts
senses.definitionCN: 相对于整个系统而言，而非某个局部
senses.example: The two lakes differ systematically in depth and temperature.
senses.exampleCN: 这两个湖在深度与温度上存在系统性的差异。
senses.why: Here the comparison is between whole systems. The difference is not a local accident but a property of each system taken together, so systematically marks the level of comparison.
senses.whyCN: 这里的比较发生在两个完整系统之间：差异不是局部的偶然，而是各系统整体所具有的性质，因此 systematically 标出的是比较的层次。

senses.title: In Ordered Arrangement
senses.titleCN: 按体系排列：遵循分类秩序
senses.definition: in an ordered arrangement, especially one based on a classification
senses.definitionCN: 按有秩序的安排，尤指依据分类体系
senses.example: The specimens were systematically arranged by family.
senses.exampleCN: 标本按科系统地排列。
senses.why: A system can also be an order of classes or ranks. To arrange systematically is to follow that order rather than to place things by chance.
senses.whyCN: system 也可以指类别或等级的次序；按体系排列，就是遵循这个次序，而不是随手摆放。

senses.title: By Research Procedure
senses.titleCN: 按科研规程：系统综述与系统抽样
senses.definition: by the fixed procedures of systematic inquiry
senses.definitionCN: 按系统研究的固定规程
senses.example: The authors systematically reviewed forty trials before concluding.
senses.exampleCN: 作者在得出结论前系统地综述了四十项试验。
senses.why: Names such as systematic review and systematic sampling fix a procedure in advance. The adverb points to those procedures rather than to a general habit of tidiness.
senses.whyCN: systematic review、systematic sampling 这类名称事先就把规程固定下来；这个副词指向的是这些规程，而不只是一般的整齐习惯。

senses.title: According to a Prior Plan
senses.titleCN: 按事先计划：先定后做
senses.definition: according to a plan decided before the action
senses.definitionCN: 按照行动之前就已决定的计划
senses.example: They systematically cleared the site before the rain arrived.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在雨来之前按计划清理了场地。
senses.why: When the steps are decided in advance, the doing follows the plan. The adverb marks that the plan, not the impulse of the moment, guided the work.
senses.whyCN: 当步骤事先定好，执行就是跟着计划走；这个副词标出的是计划——而不是一时冲动——在指挥这项工作。

senses.title: As a Regular Routine
senses.titleCN: 有规律地：固定套路
senses.definition: in a regular, repeated routine
senses.definitionCN: 以有规律、反复的日常程序
senses.example: He systematically checks the gauges at the start of every shift.
senses.exampleCN: 每次上班开始时，他都按固定流程检查仪表。
senses.why: A routine repeats the same order each time, so it behaves like a small system. The adverb presents the habit as such a working order, neither accidental nor dramatic.
senses.whyCN: 日常程序每次都重复同一顺序，运行起来就像一个小系统；这个副词把该习惯呈现为这样一套工作秩序，既非偶然，也不夸张。

intro.en: Systematically is the adverb of systematic, which was built on system. System goes back through Latin systema to Greek systēma, a whole put together from parts. The date of the English adverb is given approximately.
intro.cn: systematically 是 systematic 的副词，而 systematic 建立在 system 之上。system 经拉丁 systema 上溯到希腊 systēma，指由各部分合成的一个整体。英语副词的首见年代为约数。

items.en: Greek syn- meant 'together' and histanai meant 'to make stand, to set up'. Combined they produced synistanai, 'to put together, to combine'. The root of histanai is the same *sta- that gives English stand and stable.
items.cn: 希腊语前缀 syn- 意为「一起」，动词 histanai 意为「使立起、安置」。两者合成 synistanai，意为「组合、放在一起」。histanai 的词根与英语 stand、stable 同出 *sta-。

items.en: The noun systēma named an organized whole, whether a musical scale, a body of troops or a philosophical arrangement. The accent on 'organized' is already present in Greek.
items.cn: 名词 systēma 指有组织的整体，可以是一段音阶、一支部队，也可以是一套哲学安排。「有组织」这一重心在希腊语里就已存在。

items.en: Latin borrowed systema from Greek and used it mainly for a whole composed of parts. English took the word in the early seventeenth century, first in learned and theological writing.
items.cn: 拉丁语从希腊语借入 systema，主要用来指由部分组成的整体。英语于十七世纪初借入该词，最早见于学术与神学写作。

items.en: Systematic entered English in the seventeenth century from the Latinized Greek adjective systematicus. Adding -al + -ly produced systematically. The exact first citation is uncertain, so the date is approximate.
items.cn: systematic 于十七世纪经拉丁化的希腊形容词 systematicus 进入英语，再加 -al 与 -ly 构成 systematically。确切的首见书证不确定，故年代为约数。

items.en: Both adjectives derive from system but split in meaning. Systematic describes a method that follows ordered steps. Systemic describes a property of the whole system, as in systemic disease or systemic risk. The two are not interchangeable.
items.cn: 两个形容词都出自 system，但意义不同。systematic 描述遵循有序步骤的方法；systemic 描述整个系统的属性，如 systemic disease（全身性疾病）、systemic risk（系统性风险）。二者不可互换。

items.en: Modern statistics and evidence-based research fix phrases such as systematic error, systematic sampling and systematic review. In these names the adverb keeps its oldest force: the same procedure applied to every unit.
items.cn: 现代统计学与循证研究固定了 systematic error（系统误差）、systematic sampling（系统抽样）、systematic review（系统综述）等说法。在这些名称里，副词保留最古老的力量：同一套程序施加于每一个单位。

note.en: The first group separates two adjectives that both come from system but mean different things. The second group holds near-synonyms that stress order, procedure or repetition.
note.cn: 第一组区分两个都出自 system、但意义不同的形容词；第二组是强调秩序、程序或重复性的近义词。

entries.definition: Describes a method that follows ordered steps. It answers the question 'how is the work done', not 'what does the whole consist of'.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，指遵循有序步骤的方法；回答的是「工作怎么做」，而不是「整体由什么构成」。

entries.definition: Describes something that affects or belongs to a whole system, such as the whole body or the whole economy. It is not a synonym of systematic.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，指影响或属于整个系统的，如整个身体或整个经济体；它并非 systematic 的同义词。

entries.definition: The adverb of systemic: 'in a way that affects the whole system'. It contrasts with systematically as whole-system does with methodical.
entries.definitionCN: systemic 的副词，意为「以影响整个系统的方式」；它与 systematically 的对立，正如「整体系统」与「讲究方法」的对立。

entries.definition: In an orderly way, following a method. It stresses calm sequence rather than complete coverage.
entries.definitionCN: 有条不紊地、按方法地；强调从容的顺序，而不强调覆盖全部。

entries.definition: In the same way on every occasion. It stresses repetition of a standard, not the internal order of steps.
entries.definitionCN: 每次都以同样方式地；强调标准的一致性，而非步骤的内部次序。

entries.definition: So thoroughly that nothing remains. It is stronger than systematically on coverage and says nothing about method.
entries.definitionCN: 彻底到不留余地地；在覆盖面上比 systematically 更强，但不涉及方法。

entries.definition: As an ordinary repeated practice. It stresses habit and frequency rather than designed procedure.
entries.definitionCN: 作为日常惯例地；强调习惯与频率，而非设计好的程序。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: system + -atic + -ally: doing something as a small system of ordered steps.
normal.cn: system + -atic + -ally：把一件事当作一套有序步骤的小系统来做。

normal.en: The family runs system, systematic, systematically, systematize, systematics, systemic and subsystem.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 system、systematic、systematically、systematize、systematics、systemic、subsystem。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the method: systematic review, systematic sampling, systematic error, systematic search.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出方法义：系统综述、系统抽样、系统误差、系统搜索。

normal.en: systematic is about method; systemic is about the whole body or the whole system.
normal.cn: systematic 讲方法，systemic 讲整个身体或整个系统。

normal.en: A checklist is the everyday picture of this word: every line gets a tick in turn.
normal.cn: 清单是这个词的日常画面：每一行都依次被勾掉。

abstract.en: Picture a librarian walking every shelf from left to right, touching each spine once.
abstract.cn: 想象一位图书管理员从左到右走遍每一排书架，每一本书脊都碰一次。

abstract.en: Picture a machine that cannot skip a step, even when the step seems pointless.
abstract.cn: 想象一台机器不会跳步，哪怕那一步看起来毫无必要。

abstract.en: Picture a pattern of footprints that repeats at exactly the same distance, so it must have been planned.
abstract.cn: 想象一串间距完全相同的脚印，因此它必然是事先安排好的。

examples.en: Before drawing conclusions, the researchers systematically coded every interview.
examples.cn: 在下结论之前，研究者把每一份访谈都系统地编码。

examples.en: The fault was not random: errors appeared systematically at low temperatures.
examples.cn: 这个故障并非随机：误差在低温下系统性出现。

examples.en: A government that systematically suppresses complaints will eventually lose its sources of information.
examples.cn: 一贯压制投诉的政府，最终会失去信息来源。

dict_mnemonic.text: system（系统）+ atic + ally（以……方式）→ 以系统的方式 → 系统地、有条理地

root: 希腊 syn-「一起」+ histanai「使立起」（*sta-「站立」）→ systēma「由部分组成的整体」→ 拉丁 systema → 英语 system → systematic → systematically。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses rest on one picture, a fixed order of steps, and apply it to different objects: a method, a complete coverage, a deliberate pattern, a whole system, a classification, a research procedure, a prior plan and a daily routine.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都建立在同一幅画面上——一套固定的步骤次序——只是施加的对象不同：方法、全面覆盖、蓄意模式、整个系统、分类体系、科研规程、事先计划与日常流程。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: numbered steps in a fixed order, each box ticked in turn.
core.cn: 核心意象：按固定次序编号的步骤，每个格子依次被勾掉。

branches.en: METHOD AND COVERAGE: the same ordered path is used, and it is used until the set is finished.
branches.cn: 方法与覆盖：走同一条有序路径，并且走到整个集合完毕。

branches.en: INTENTION: when the same path recurs, observers stop calling it accidental and start calling it policy.
branches.cn: 意图：当同一条路径反复出现，旁观者就不再称之为偶然，而称之为既定做法。

branches.en: WHOLE AND ORDER: the system can be an entire object under comparison or a ranked scheme of classes.
branches.cn: 整体与秩序：system 既可以指被比较的完整对象，也可以指分等级的分类体系。

branches.en: PROTOCOL AND PLAN: research fixes the path in advance, and so does a plan made before the action.
branches.cn: 规程与计划：科研事先固定路径，行动之前订好的计划也是如此。

branches.en: ROUTINE: a habit that repeats the same order behaves like a small system running every day.
branches.cn: 日常流程：重复同一顺序的习惯，就像每天运行的一个小系统。

intro.en: Systematically is a Greek-derived noun turned adjective and then adverb: a prefix of union, a root of standing, an adjective ending and an adverb ending.
intro.cn: systematically 是希腊来源的名词，先变形容词、再变副词：表示「结合」的前缀、表示「站立」的词根、形容词词尾与副词词尾。

latinIntro.en: Systema reached Latin from Greek and supplied system, systematic, systematize and systematics. Latin also has its own verb stare 'to stand', a cognate from the same Indo-European root rather than a source of the Greek word.
latinIntro.cn: systema 由希腊语进入拉丁语，衍生出 system、systematic、systematize、systematics。拉丁语本身另有动词 stare「站立」，它与希腊词同出同一个印欧词根，但并非希腊词的来源。

items.example: The files were systematically sorted by date.
items.exampleCN: 文件按日期系统地整理过。

items.example: The survey used a systematic sample of households.
items.exampleCN: 该调查使用了住户系统抽样。

items.structure: systema < Greek systēma (a whole put together)
items.example: The drainage system covers the whole valley.
items.exampleCN: 排水系统覆盖整个山谷。

items.meaning: to reduce to an ordered system
items.example: She systematized the archive over one summer.
items.exampleCN: 她用一个夏天把档案系统化了。

items.meaning: the act of arranging into a system
items.example: The systematization of records took three years.
items.exampleCN: 档案的系统化用了三年。

items.meaning: the study of classification, especially of living things
items.meaningCN: 分类学，尤指生物分类学
items.example: Molecular systematics reshaped the tree of birds.
items.exampleCN: 分子分类学重塑了鸟类的演化树。

items.meaning: affecting the whole system or body
items.meaningCN: 影响整个系统或全身的
items.example: The infection became systemic within a week.
items.exampleCN: 感染在一周内变为全身性的。

items.meaning: a system contained within a larger one
items.meaningCN: 包含在更大系统内的子系统
items.example: The braking subsystem failed first.
items.exampleCN: 制动子系统最先失效。

latinEntries.structure: stare (verb, first conjugation); cognate with Greek histanai, not borrowed from it

definition_zh: 理论的；理论上的；假设的；以理论推理为依据的
definition_en: based on general principles and reasoning rather than on practice, observation or direct experiment
core_image: 黑板上推演到一半的公式，与现实车间里尚未造出的机器隔着一段距离
scene: Theoretical physics often runs decades ahead of experiment.
sceneCN: 这里 theoretical 指「理论的」（第 1 个义项：依据原理与推理、而非实践与实验）；句意：理论物理学往往比实验领先数十年。图中可辨识物件：写满推演的黑板、尚未装配的仪器草图。

pos.zh: 理论的；理论上的；假设的（与 practical、experimental、applied 相对）

forms.label: 同义形容词变体
forms.form: theoretic（理论的，较少用，多见于学术复合词）

derivatives.zh: 理论的（多见于 theoretic framework 等学术搭配）
定理（与 theory 同出希腊 theōrēma「所观之物」）

senses.title: Based on Theory
senses.titleCN: 理论的：依据原理而非实践
senses.definition: based on ideas and general principles rather than on practice or experiment
senses.definitionCN: 依据观念与一般原理，而非实践或实验的
senses.example: Theoretical physics often runs decades ahead of experiment.
senses.exampleCN: 理论物理学往往比实验领先数十年。
senses.why: Greek theoria named looking and contemplating. The adjective marks knowledge reached by reasoning about principles, not by handling the thing itself.
senses.whyCN: 希腊 theoria 指观看与沉思。这个形容词标出的是通过对原理的推理而获得的知识，而不是亲手处理事物得来的知识。

senses.title: Hypothetical
senses.titleCN: 假设的：只为推理而设想
senses.definition: imagined or supposed for the purpose of reasoning, not actual
senses.definitionCN: 为推理而设想或假定，并非实际存在
senses.example: Let us take a theoretical case in which nobody pays tax.
senses.exampleCN: 让我们设想一个没人缴税的理论情形。
senses.why: A case built to test an argument is not observed anywhere. It exists only inside the reasoning, so the adjective shifts from 'about theory' to 'merely supposed'.
senses.whyCN: 为检验论证而构造的情形并不在任何地方被观察到，它只存在于推理之中；于是这个形容词从「关于理论的」滑向「仅仅假设的」。

senses.title: Predicted but Unseen
senses.titleCN: 理论预言的：尚未观测到
senses.definition: predicted by theory but not yet observed
senses.definitionCN: 由理论预言、但尚未被观测到的
senses.example: The theoretical particle would leave only a tiny trace in the detector.
senses.exampleCN: 这种理论粒子只会在探测器中留下极微小的痕迹。
senses.why: Theory can name something before any instrument sees it. The adjective marks that priority of reasoning over observation, which is common in particle physics.
senses.whyCN: 理论可以在任何仪器看见某物之前先给它命名；这个形容词标出的正是推理先于观测，这在粒子物理中很常见。

senses.title: Of the Theory Branch
senses.titleCN: 理论分支的：学科的理论侧
senses.definition: belonging to the branch of a subject that studies principles rather than applications
senses.definitionCN: 属于研究原理而非应用的那个学科分支
senses.example: She holds a chair in theoretical computer science.
senses.exampleCN: 她担任理论计算机科学方向的教授。
senses.why: Disciplines split into theory and application. The adjective labels the theory side, where the aim is to prove what is possible, not to ship a product.
senses.whyCN: 学科会分成理论与应用两侧；这个形容词标出理论一侧，其目标是证明什么在原理上可行，而不是交付产品。

senses.title: Idealized Model
senses.titleCN: 理想化模型的：删去复杂细节
senses.definition: belonging to an idealized model that leaves out complicating details
senses.definitionCN: 属于省略了复杂细节的理想化模型
senses.example: The theoretical model assumes a perfectly smooth sphere.
senses.exampleCN: 这个理论模型假定球体完全光滑。
senses.why: A model is made by leaving things out. The word marks that the object is a construction, so its predictions hold only as far as the omissions are harmless.
senses.whyCN: 模型是靠删减造出来的；这个词标出该对象是一种构造物，因此其预测只在删减无碍的范围内成立。

senses.title: Possible in Principle
senses.titleCN: 原则上可能的：逻辑容许
senses.definition: possible according to reasoning, whether or not it can be done in practice
senses.definitionCN: 按推理是可能的，不论实践中能否做到
senses.example: A theoretical solution exists, but nobody can build it yet.
senses.exampleCN: 理论上存在解法，但暂时没人能把它造出来。
senses.why: If the reasoning permits something, it is theoretically possible. The barrier lies in materials or cost, not in logic, which is why the two words 'theoretical' and 'practical' so often face each other.
senses.whyCN: 如果推理容许某件事，它就是理论上可能的；障碍在材料或成本，而不在逻辑，所以 theoretical 与 practical 常常成对出现。

senses.title: Abstract, Not Applied
senses.titleCN: 抽象的：带不务实的意味
senses.definition: concerned with abstract reasoning, often with a hint of impracticality
senses.definitionCN: 关心抽象推理，常暗示不切实际
senses.example: His answer was theoretical and ignored the cost of the plan.
senses.exampleCN: 他的回答是理论性的，忽略了该计划的成本。
senses.why: When reasoning ignores real conditions, the same word turns mildly critical: correct in the abstract and useless in this room. The tone comes from context, not from the root.
senses.whyCN: 当推理无视现实条件，同一个词就带上轻微批评：抽象上正确，在这间屋子里却没用。这一语气来自语境，而非词根。

senses.title: Consistent within a Theory
senses.titleCN: 理论体系内的：内部自洽
senses.definition: consistent with the definitions and assumptions of a given theory
senses.definitionCN: 与某一理论的定义和假定保持一致
senses.example: The objection is theoretical: the two claims cannot both hold.
senses.exampleCN: 这一反对是理论层面的：两项主张不能同时成立。
senses.why: Inside a theory, statements must fit its own rules. A theoretical objection attacks that fit rather than the data, so it can be settled by argument alone.
senses.whyCN: 在一个理论内部，陈述必须符合它自己的规则；理论性反对攻击的正是这种吻合，而不是数据，因此仅凭论证就能解决。

intro.en: Theoretical descends from Greek theōria 'a looking, contemplation', through Latin theoreticus. The Greek noun is usually traced to theoros 'spectator', but the details of the earliest formation are debated.
intro.cn: theoretical 经拉丁 theoreticus 上溯希腊 theōria「观看、沉思」。这个希腊名词通常追溯到 theoros「观看者」，但最早构词细节仍有争议。

items.en: The noun thea is generally taken to mean 'a view, a sight', and horan means 'to see'. Together they are thought to give theoros, 'one who looks on', especially a spectator at a festival or an envoy consulting an oracle.
items.cn: 名词 thea 一般认为是「景象、观看」，horan 意为「看见」；两者合成 theoros，即「观看的人」，尤指节庆上的观众或去求神谕的使者。此说一般认为是，细节并不完全确定。

items.en: From theoros came the noun theōria, 'the act of looking on, contemplation, a spectacle'. Philosophy borrowed it for the mind's disinterested viewing of truth, away from action.
items.cn: 由 theoros 产生名词 theōria，意为「观看的行为、沉思、景象」。哲学借它指心灵不带功利地观看真理，与行动保持距离。

items.en: Latin took the adjective theorēticus from Greek theoretikos, 'of contemplation'. The Latin form kept the philosophical sense of knowledge pursued for understanding rather than for use.
items.cn: 拉丁语从希腊 theoretikos 借入形容词 theorēticus，意为「沉思的」。拉丁形式保留了哲学含义：为理解而非为实用而追求的知识。

items.en: English theoretical appears in the seventeenth century beside the older theoretic. The -al form became the everyday adjective, while theoretic survived mainly in fixed academic phrases. The first citation is uncertain.
items.cn: 英语 theoretical 于十七世纪出现，与更早的 theoretic 并存。-al 形式成为日常形容词，theoretic 主要残留在固定的学术搭配中。确切首见书证不确定。

items.en: The modern contrast between theoretical and practical is older than English: Greek already opposed theōria to praxis. The pair therefore marks a division of labour, not a judgement that one side is useless.
items.cn: 现代 theoretical 与 practical 的对立比英语更古老：希腊语已用 theōria 对 praxis。因此这一对词标出的是分工，而不是判定某一侧无用。

note.en: The first group traces one Greek family whose members are easily confused. The second holds near-synonyms that sit at different distances from reality.
note.cn: 第一组梳理同一个希腊词族中容易混淆的成员；第二组是距现实远近不同的近义词。

entries.definition: A body of principles that explains a field. It is the thing a theoretical argument is built inside, not the adjective describing the argument.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，指解释某一领域的一套原理；理论论证是在它内部进行的，而它不是描述论证的形容词。

entries.definition: A person who builds or studies theory. It names the human agent, so it never replaces theoretical before a noun.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，指建构或研究理论的人；它命名的是人，因此不能替代名词前的 theoretical。

entries.definition: An older adjective of the same meaning, now mostly confined to phrases such as theoretic framework. It is not a different concept.
entries.definitionCN: 同义的较旧形容词形式，如今多限于 theoretic framework 一类搭配；它并非另一个概念。

entries.definition: Imagined as a premise. It stresses that the case is not real, while theoretical may still describe a well-founded body of reasoning.
entries.definitionCN: 作为前提被设想出来的；强调情形不真实，而 theoretical 仍可指有根据的推理体系。

entries.definition: Concerning concepts or mental categories. It says the work happens with ideas, not that it is unproven.
entries.definitionCN: 关于概念或心智范畴的；它说的是工作以观念为材料，并不表示未经证实。

entries.definition: General and detached from concrete cases. It can be neutral or critical, but it does not imply a formal theory.
entries.definitionCN: 一般性的、脱离具体个案的；可中性也可带批评，但不暗示存在形式化的理论。

entries.definition: Based on conjecture with little evidence. It is more negative than theoretical, which can be rigorous.
entries.definitionCN: 基于猜测而证据不足的；比 theoretical 更负面，因为 theoretical 可以是严谨的。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: theoria 'a looking' + -al: knowledge from viewing principles with the mind.
normal.cn: theoria「观看」+ -al：用心灵观看原理而得到的知识。

normal.en: The family runs theory, theorist, theorize, theoretic, theoretical, theorem.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 theory、theorist、theorize、theoretic、theoretical、theorem。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the use: theoretical framework, theoretical physics, theoretical model, theoretical possibility.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出用法：理论框架、理论物理学、理论模型、理论上的可能性。

normal.en: The opposite pair is theoretical and practical, or theoretical and experimental.
normal.cn: 对立搭配是 theoretical 与 practical，或 theoretical 与 experimental。

normal.en: theorem is a proved statement; theory is the whole system that contains it.
normal.cn: theorem 是被证明的命题；theory 是包含它的整个体系。

abstract.en: Picture a map drawn years before anyone walks the ground it describes.
abstract.cn: 想象一张地图，在任何人走过它所描述的地面之前许多年就已画好。

abstract.en: Picture a model ship in a bottle: exact in shape, unable to carry a single passenger.
abstract.cn: 想象瓶中船：形状精确，却载不了一位乘客。

abstract.en: Picture two people arguing about whether a door can open, without ever trying the handle.
abstract.cn: 想象两个人争论一扇门能不能开，却从不去拧门把手。

examples.en: The paper offers a theoretical explanation, but no experiment has tested it.
examples.cn: 这篇论文给出了一种理论解释，但尚无实验检验它。

examples.en: In theoretical terms the plan is sound; in practice it needs money nobody has.
examples.cn: 从理论上说这个计划是成立的；实践中它需要没人拿得出的资金。

examples.en: Students often find theoretical courses dry until they meet a real problem.
examples.cn: 学生常觉得理论课程枯燥，直到遇上一个真实问题。

dict_mnemonic.text: theory（理论）+ etical（形容词词尾）→ 属于理论的 → theoretical 理论的

root: 希腊 thea「景象」+ horan「看见」→ theoros「观看者」→ theōria「观看、沉思」→ 拉丁 theoreticus → 英语 theoretical。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses begin with reasoning rather than practice and fan out: a hypothetical case, an unobserved prediction, a branch of a discipline, an idealized model, a logical possibility, an abstract answer and an internal objection.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从「以推理而非实践为本」出发向外展开：假设情形、尚未观测的预言、学科分支、理想化模型、逻辑上的可能、抽象的回答与体系内部的反对。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a formula worked out on a board, separated from the machine it describes.
core.cn: 核心意象：黑板上推演出的公式，与它所描述的机器之间隔着距离。

branches.en: REASONING APART FROM PRACTICE: knowledge from principles, which can look either rigorous or useless depending on the room.
branches.cn: 与实践分离的推理：来自原理的知识，视场合可显得严谨，也可显得无用。

branches.en: THE SUPPOSED AND THE POSSIBLE: a case invented for argument and a solution the reasoning permits.
branches.cn: 假设与可能：为论证而虚构的情形，以及推理所容许的解法。

branches.en: THE UNSEEN: theory may name a particle before any detector records it.
branches.cn: 未见之物：理论可在任何探测器记录之前先为粒子命名。

branches.en: THE BRANCH: a discipline divides into a theory side and an application side.
branches.cn: 分支：一个学科分为理论侧与应用侧。

branches.en: CONSTRUCTION AND CONSISTENCY: a model built by omission must also stay coherent with its own assumptions.
branches.cn: 构造与自洽：靠省略建成的模型，还必须在自身假定内保持一致。

intro.en: Theoretical is a Greek noun of viewing turned into a Latin adjective and then an English one: root words for sight, a noun ending, and an adjective ending -al.
intro.cn: theoretical 是希腊语中表示「观看」的名词，先转为拉丁形容词，再进入英语：表示视觉的词根、名词词尾，以及形容词词尾 -al。

latinIntro.en: Greek theōria produced Latin theoreticus and English theory, theoretical, theorist, theorize and theorem. The same sight-root appears in theater, a place for viewing, though that word reached English by a different route.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊 theōria 产生拉丁 theoreticus，以及英语 theory、theoretical、theorist、theorize、theorem。同一个「观看」词根也出现在 theater（观看的场所）中，但那个词走的是另一条路径。

items.example: The theoretical part of the course comes first.
items.exampleCN: 课程的理论部分排在前面。

items.meaning: an organized body of explanatory principles
items.meaningCN: 有组织的解释性原理体系
items.example: The theory predicts a slow rise in sea level.
items.exampleCN: 该理论预测海平面会缓慢上升。

items.meaning: one who builds or studies theory
items.example: The theorist never visited the site she wrote about.
items.exampleCN: 这位理论家从未到过她所写的那处遗址。

items.meaning: to form or reason with theories
items.example: They theorized about the cause for years.
items.exampleCN: 他们多年来就成因进行理论推测。

items.meaningCN: theory 的较旧形容词形式
items.example: Theoretic work preceded any measurement.
items.exampleCN: 理论研究先于任何测量。

items.structure: theōrēma (a thing viewed, a proposition) + English form
items.example: The theorem holds for every triangle.
items.exampleCN: 该定理对一切三角形都成立。

items.meaning: of the stage; exaggerated as if acted
items.meaningCN: 戏剧的；如表演般夸张的
items.example: His grief was real but theatrical.
items.exampleCN: 他的悲伤是真的，却很戏剧化。

items.example: Theoretically, the bridge can hold twice that load.
items.exampleCN: 理论上，这座桥能承受两倍的荷载。

latinEntries.structure: theōria, -ae (f., first declension, Greek loan in Latin)

latinEntries.meaning: a spectacle; a proposition to be proved
latinEntries.meaningCN: 所见之物；待证明的命题

definition_zh: 理论上；按理说；从原理上讲；在假设情形下
definition_en: according to theory or principle, especially when practice may differ
core_image: 纸上算出的箭头与真实机器里实际走出的轨迹并排摆放，两者并不重合
scene: Theoretically, the bridge can carry twice that load, but nobody has tested it.
sceneCN: 这里 theoretically 指「理论上」（第 2 个义项：按原理推算应当如此，实际未必）；句意：理论上这座桥能承受两倍的荷载，但没人测试过。图中可辨识物件：计算纸带、桥梁受力示意图、未启用的测试装置。

pos.zh: 理论上；按理说；从原理上（由 theoretical 加 -ly 构成，常用于「理应如此，实际未必」的对比）

forms.label: 用法提示
forms.form: 常置于句首或句末作评注副词，如 Theoretically, ... / ..., theoretically.

senses.title: In Theory, Not in Practice
senses.titleCN: 理论上：与实践相对
senses.definition: according to theory rather than practice
senses.definitionCN: 依据理论而非实践
senses.example: Theoretically the method is elegant; in the lab it fails.
senses.exampleCN: 理论上这个方法很优雅；在实验室里它却行不通。
senses.why: The adverb marks the side of the theory-practice pair. It says the statement is judged by principles, leaving open what happens when the method meets real conditions.
senses.whyCN: 这个副词标出「理论—实践」这一对里的理论一侧：它表示该陈述是按原理来评判的，至于方法遇到现实条件会怎样，则留着不说。

senses.title: In Principle
senses.titleCN: 按理说：照原理应当
senses.definition: as reasoning says it should be
senses.definitionCN: 按推理所说应当如此
senses.example: Theoretically, the Bridge can carry twice that load.
senses.exampleCN: 按理说，这座桥能承受两倍的荷载。
senses.why: Here the word invites you to follow the calculation to its conclusion. It is a claim about what the numbers allow, not a report of what has been observed.
senses.whyCN: 这里这个词邀请你顺着计算走到结论；它主张的是数字所容许的范围，而不是报告已经观察到的事实。

senses.title: Under a Supposition
senses.titleCN: 在假设情形下：假定前提成立
senses.definition: within a case that is assumed rather than actual
senses.definitionCN: 在被假定而非实际的情形之中
senses.example: Theoretically, with no friction, the puck would never stop.
senses.exampleCN: 在无摩擦的假设下，冰球理论上永远不会停下。
senses.why: A supposition sets the conditions. The adverb tells the listener that the conclusion holds inside those conditions only, so the missing friction is not an oversight but a premise.
senses.whyCN: 假设先设定条件；这个副词告诉听者，结论只在那些条件之内成立，因此被忽略的摩擦不是疏忽，而是前提。

senses.title: By Abstract Reasoning
senses.titleCN: 从抽象推理上说
senses.definition: by reasoning with abstractions rather than with observed cases
senses.definitionCN: 以抽象概念而非观察到的个案进行推理
senses.example: Theoretically, any language can express any idea.
senses.exampleCN: 从抽象推理上说，任何语言都能表达任何观念。
senses.why: The step here is from particular examples to a general claim. The adverb marks that move, which is legitimate in itself but must be defended on its own terms.
senses.whyCN: 这里的一步是从具体例子推向一般主张；这个副词标出的正是这一步——它本身是正当的，但必须按自身的规则来论证。

senses.title: As Predicted by a Model
senses.titleCN: 按模型推算：模型给出什么
senses.definition: as a model or calculation predicts
senses.definitionCN: 按照模型或计算所预测的
senses.example: Theoretically, the population should double in nine years.
senses.exampleCN: 按模型推算，该种群应在九年内翻倍。
senses.why: A model produces numbers whether or not the world cooperates. The adverb attributes the figure to the model, which protects the speaker if reality disagrees.
senses.whyCN: 模型无论现实是否配合都会给出数字；这个副词把数值归到模型名下，从而在现实不符时保护说话者。

senses.title: Expected but Not Guaranteed
senses.titleCN: 按理论推断：与实际常有落差
senses.definition: as one would expect from theory, often with the hint that reality differs
senses.definitionCN: 按理论推想应当如此，常暗示现实未必
senses.example: Theoretically it should work by Friday; last time it took a month.
senses.exampleCN: 按理论它周五前该能用了；上次却用了一个月。
senses.why: The contrast is supplied by the second clause. The adverb sets up an expectation that the speaker already suspects will not be met, a very common conversational use.
senses.whyCN: 对比由后半句提供；这个副词先立起一个期待，而说话者已怀疑它不会实现——这是口语里极常见的用法。

senses.title: On the Theory Side
senses.titleCN: 就理论分支而言
senses.definition: with respect to the theoretical branch of a subject
senses.definitionCN: 就某一学科的理论分支而言
senses.example: The paper is theoretically strong but empirically thin.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇论文在理论方面很强，实证方面却很单薄。
senses.why: Here the adverb locates a work inside the theory branch and praises or criticizes it by that standard, not by the standard of data collection.
senses.whyCN: 这里这个副词把一项工作定位在理论分支之内，并按那一分支的标准来褒贬，而不是按数据收集的标准。

senses.title: In Idealized Terms
senses.titleCN: 以理想化的方式：删繁就简
senses.definition: in idealized terms that omit complicating detail
senses.definitionCN: 以省略复杂细节的理想化方式
senses.example: Theoretically, the two species never compete; in the field they do.
senses.exampleCN: 理想化地说，这两个物种从不竞争；在野外它们却竞争。
senses.why: Idealization removes friction, weather and history. The adverb flags that the clean result belongs to the simplified picture, which is useful precisely because it can then be tested against the messy one.
senses.whyCN: 理想化删去摩擦、天气与历史；这个副词提示干净的结果属于简化后的图景——它的用处恰恰在于随后可以用杂乱的现实来检验它。

intro.en: Theoretically is theoretical plus -ly, and theoretical descends from Greek theōria 'a looking, contemplation' through Latin theoreticus. The first English use is dated only approximately.
intro.cn: theoretically 由 theoretical 加 -ly 构成，而 theoretical 经拉丁 theoreticus 上溯希腊 theōria「观看、沉思」。英语首见年代仅为约数。

items.en: Theoros is generally explained as 'one who looks on', from thea 'a view' and horan 'to see'. It named a spectator and also an envoy sent to consult an oracle and report what he had seen.
items.cn: theoros 一般解释为「观看的人」，由 thea「景象」与 horan「看见」构成；它既指观众，也指被派去求神谕并回报所见之事的使者。

items.en: The abstract noun theōria meant 'the act of viewing, contemplation'. Philosophy gave it a technical sense: the mind's quiet inspection of eternal truths, in contrast with action.
items.cn: 抽象名词 theōria 意为「观看的行为、沉思」。哲学赋予它专门含义：心灵对永恒真理的安静审视，与行动形成对照。

items.en: Latin theoreticus gave English theoretic in the sixteenth century and theoretical in the seventeenth. Adding -ly produced theoretically. The exact first citation of the adverb is not firmly dated.
items.cn: 拉丁 theoreticus 在十六世纪给出英语 theoretic，十七世纪给出 theoretical；加 -ly 产生 theoretically。副词的确切首见书证没有可靠年代。

items.en: Modern English often uses theoretically at the front of a sentence as a comment adverb, meaning 'judging by theory'. The habit grew with scientific and academic writing.
items.cn: 现代英语常把 theoretically 放在句首作评注副词，意思是「按理论判断」。这一习惯随科学与学术写作而发展。

items.en: The Greek pair theōria and praxis still shapes the English pair theoretical and practical. The adverb therefore always implies a counterpart: some practice against which the reasoning could be checked.
items.cn: 希腊语 theōria 与 praxis 这对概念至今仍塑造英语 theoretical 与 practical 这对词。因此这个副词总暗含一个对应项：某种可以用来检验推理的实践。

note.en: The first group separates the adverb from its adjective and from a different adverb of whole systems. The second holds near-synonyms that hedge in different ways.
note.cn: 第一组区分该副词与其形容词，以及与「整体系统」有关的另一个副词；第二组是不同程度留有余地的近义词。

entries.definition: The adjective describing knowledge based on principles. It modifies a noun, while the adverb modifies the act of judging or speaking.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，描述以原理为基础的知识；它修饰名词，而副词修饰判断或陈述的动作。

entries.definition: In practice, or almost. It occupies the other half of the theory-practice pair and can also mean 'almost'.
entries.definitionCN: 在实践中，或「几乎」；它占据理论—实践这一对的另一半，也可表示「几乎」。

entries.definition: In a way that affects the whole system or body. It is unrelated in meaning to the theory-practice contrast.
entries.definitionCN: 以影响整个系统或全身的方式；与理论—实践这一对立在意义上无关。

entries.definition: As far as the basic rule goes. It is the plain-English equivalent of the second sense and carries the same unspoken 'but'.
entries.definitionCN: 就基本原则而言；它是第 2 个义项的平实英语说法，并且带着同样未说出口的「但是」。

entries.definition: At the level of ideas or definitions. It is about how concepts are formed, not about whether a result can be realized.
entries.definitionCN: 在观念或定义的层面上；它讲概念如何构成，而不讲结果能否实现。

entries.definition: Under an assumed condition. It is more openly fictional than theoretically and invites a conditional sentence.
entries.definitionCN: 在假定条件下；比 theoretically 更坦率地表示虚构，常引出条件句。

entries.definition: According to what something is called, not what it is. It is close to sense 6 but stresses labels rather than reasoning.
entries.definitionCN: 按照名称上所说，而非实际如何；接近第 6 个义项，但强调的是名义标签而非推理。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: theoretical + -ly: judging a thing by principle rather than by trial.
normal.cn: theoretical + -ly：按原理而不是靠试验来评判一件事。

normal.en: The family runs theory, theoretical, theoretically, theorist, theorize, theorem.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 theory、theoretical、theoretically、theorist、theorize、theorem。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the use: theoretically possible, theoretically speaking, theoretically infinite.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出用法：理论上可能、从理论上说、理论上无限。

normal.en: The natural partner is practically: theory says yes, practice says wait.
normal.cn: 天然搭档是 practically：理论说可以，实践说再等等。

normal.en: Sentence-initial Theoretically, ... is a comment on the whole claim that follows.
normal.cn: 句首的 Theoretically, ... 是对后面整个主张的评注。

abstract.en: Picture a straight line drawn with a ruler beside a path that curves around every stone.
abstract.cn: 想象一条用尺画出的直线，旁边是一条绕过每块石头的弯曲小路。

abstract.en: Picture a recipe that works perfectly until the kitchen runs out of one ingredient.
abstract.cn: 想象一份配方完美可行，直到厨房少了一样原料。

abstract.en: Picture a sign that reads 'should be fine' in a building where nothing has been switched on yet.
abstract.cn: 想象一栋还没通电的楼里挂着「应该没问题」的牌子。

examples.en: Theoretically, the reaction needs only a trace of catalyst.
examples.cn: 理论上，这个反应只需要极少量催化剂。

examples.en: Theoretically speaking, no ecosystem can grow without a limit.
examples.cn: 从理论上说，没有哪个生态系统能无限制地增长。

examples.en: The plan is theoretically justified, yet its cost makes it unusable.
examples.cn: 该计划在理论上说得通，但成本使它无法实施。

dict_mnemonic.text: theoretical（理论的）+ ly（以……方式）→ 以理论的方式 → 理论上

root: 希腊 thea「景象」+ horan「看见」→ theoros「观看者」→ theōria「观看、沉思」→ 拉丁 theoreticus → 英语 theoretical → theoretically。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all judge by principle rather than by trial, but the source of the principle varies: theory itself, a calculation, a supposition, abstract reasoning, a model, an expectation, a branch of study or an idealized picture.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都以原理而非试验来评判，但原理的来源各不相同：理论本身、计算、假设、抽象推理、模型、期待、学科分支或理想化图景。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a computed arrow beside the path a real machine actually takes.
core.cn: 核心意象：计算出的箭头与真实机器实际走出的轨迹并排摆放。

branches.en: THE THEORY SIDE: the adverb either contrasts with practice or locates a work inside the theoretical branch.
branches.cn: 理论一侧：该副词或与实践相对，或把一项工作定位在理论分支之内。

branches.en: WHAT THE RULE ALLOWS: a calculation or a model states what follows from its own assumptions.
branches.cn: 规则容许什么：计算或模型陈述的是从其自身假定推出的结果。

branches.en: CONDITIONS AND IDEALIZATION: a supposition or a simplified picture sets the boundary inside which the claim holds.
branches.cn: 条件与理想化：假设或简化图景设定了主张成立的边界。

branches.en: THE ABSTRACT STEP: moving from examples to a general claim, which must be argued in its own terms.
branches.cn: 抽象的一步：从例子推向一般主张，而这一步必须按自身规则论证。

branches.en: THE GAP: the adverb often raises an expectation the speaker already expects reality to break.
branches.cn: 落差：这个副词常立起一个期待，而说话者已料到现实会打破它。

intro.en: Theoretically is a Greek-derived adjective with an English adverb ending: a sight-root, a noun of contemplation, an adjective suffix and -ly.
intro.cn: theoretically 是希腊来源的形容词加英语副词词尾：一个「观看」词根、一个表示沉思的名词、一个形容词后缀，以及 -ly。

latinIntro.en: Greek theōria gave Latin theoreticus and English theory, theoretical, theoretic, theoretically, theorist and theorem. The sight-root also appears in theater, which arrived by another route.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊 theōria 给出拉丁 theoreticus，以及英语 theory、theoretical、theoretic、theoretically、theorist、theorem。同一个「观看」词根也见于 theater，但那个词走的是另一条路径。

items.example: Theoretically, the tank holds a thousand litres.
items.exampleCN: 理论上，这个罐子能装一千升。

items.example: The theoretical gain was never measured.
items.exampleCN: 理论上的增益从未被测量。

items.example: The theory explains why the two curves cross.
items.exampleCN: 该理论解释了这两条曲线为何相交。

items.example: The theorist works mostly with pencil and paper.
items.exampleCN: 这位理论家主要用纸笔工作。

items.meaning: to reason in terms of theory
items.example: They theorized long before any data arrived.
items.exampleCN: 他们早在任何数据到来之前就做了理论推想。

items.example: The theorem follows from two simple axioms.
items.exampleCN: 该定理由两条简单公理推出。

items.example: Theoretic debate filled the early journals.
items.exampleCN: 早期的期刊充满理论争论。

items.example: The lighting gave the hall a theatrical air.
items.exampleCN: 灯光给大厅带来一种舞台气氛。

latinEntries.structure: theōria, -ae (f., first declension, Greek loan in Latin)

latinEntries.meaning: a thing viewed; a proved proposition
latinEntries.meaningCN: 所见之物；已证明的命题

definition_zh: 转变；改造；转型；（数学）变换；（生物）转化
definition_en: a thorough change in form, nature or appearance, or the result of such a change
core_image: 同一团黏土在手中被重新塑成完全不同的形状，材质未变而形态全非
scene: The city underwent a complete transformation after the harbor was rebuilt.
sceneCN: 这里 transformation 指「转变」（第 1 个义项：形态或性质发生根本变化）；句意：港口重建之后，这座城市经历了彻底的转变。图中可辨识物件：新旧街区对照图、起重机、被重新规划的岸线。

pos.zh: 转变；改造；转型；变换；转化（可数，指一次具体变化；也可不可数，指变化过程）

forms.label: 形容词形式
forms.form: transformative（有变革作用的）；transformational（转换的；变革的）

derivatives.zh: 有变革作用的；起改造作用的
转换的；变革的（transformational grammar 转换语法）

senses.title: Radical Change of Form
senses.titleCN: 转变：形态或性质的根本改变
senses.definition: a thorough change in the form or nature of something
senses.definitionCN: 事物形态或性质发生的彻底变化
senses.example: The city underwent a complete transformation after the harbor was rebuilt.
senses.exampleCN: 港口重建之后，这座城市经历了彻底的转变。
senses.why: Trans- means 'across' and forma means 'form'. The noun names a crossing from one form to another, and the prefix promises that the distance travelled is large, not a small adjustment.
senses.whyCN: trans- 意为「跨越」，forma 意为「形状」。这个名词命名的是从一种形态跨到另一种形态，而前缀保证跨越的距离很大，不是小修小补。

senses.title: The Changed Result
senses.titleCN: 变化后的形态：转变的产物
senses.definition: the new form that results from such a change
senses.definitionCN: 这种变化所产生的新形态
senses.example: Her final transformation into a singer surprised the whole family.
senses.exampleCN: 她最终转变为一名歌手，让全家人都感到意外。
senses.why: The same noun can name either the journey or the place arrived at. Context decides which is meant, and English often uses 'a transformation' for the resulting new state.
senses.whyCN: 同一个名词既可指旅程，也可指到达之处；语境决定所指，而英语常用 a transformation 来指变化后的新状态。

senses.title: Mathematical Mapping
senses.titleCN: 数学变换：点与点之间的对应
senses.definition: a rule or mapping that carries each point or value to another
senses.definitionCN: 把每个点或数值对应到另一个点或数值的规则
senses.example: A rotation is a transformation that preserves distance.
senses.exampleCN: 旋转是一种保持距离不变的变换。
senses.why: Mathematics borrows the word for a change of position or representation that follows a rule. Nothing physical changes; only the coordinates do, which is why the term is so useful.
senses.whyCN: 数学借这个词表示按规则进行的方位或表示方式变化；没有任何实物改变，变的只是坐标——这正是该术语极其有用的原因。

senses.title: Genetic Transformation
senses.titleCN: 遗传转化：细胞接纳外源基因
senses.definition: the introduction of foreign DNA into a cell so that it takes up the new genes
senses.definitionCN: 把外源 DNA 引入细胞，使其接纳新基因
senses.example: The lab used transformation to insert a resistance gene into the bacteria.
senses.exampleCN: 实验室用转化把一段抗性基因插入细菌。
senses.why: In biology the change is a lasting alteration of the cell's inherited material. The general sense of 'form changed from outside' narrows into 'genome changed from outside'.
senses.whyCN: 在生物学里，变化是对细胞遗传物质的持久改动；「由外部改变形态」的一般含义收窄为「由外部改变基因组」。

senses.title: Syntactic Rewriting
senses.titleCN: 语言学转换：句式的重写
senses.definition: a rule that rewrites one sentence structure into another with the same meaning
senses.definitionCN: 把一种句式改写成另一种同义句式的规则
senses.example: The passive sentence is derived by transformation from the active one.
senses.exampleCN: 被动句由主动句经转换生成。
senses.why: Transformational grammar treats a sentence as passing through rule-governed rewrites. The word is apt because the meaning survives while the shape of the sentence changes.
senses.whyCN: 转换语法把句子看作经过一系列规则化改写；这个词用得很贴切，因为句子的意义保留下来，而句子的外形改变了。

senses.title: Personal Change
senses.titleCN: 人的转变：性情或处境改观
senses.definition: a deep change in a person's character, health or circumstances
senses.definitionCN: 一个人性格、健康或处境的深刻变化
senses.example: Years of care brought about a slow transformation in him.
senses.exampleCN: 多年的照料使他慢慢发生了转变。
senses.why: The noun is not limited to visible shapes. A person's life can cross from one form to another, and the word then carries hope or moral weight rather than geometry.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词并不限于可见的形状；一个人的生活可以从一种形态跨到另一种，此时该词承载的是希望或道德分量，而不是几何意味。

senses.title: Energy Conversion
senses.titleCN: 能量转换：从一种形式到另一种
senses.definition: the change of energy from one form into another
senses.definitionCN: 能量由一种形式变为另一种形式
senses.example: A turbine converts heat into motion through a series of transformations.
senses.exampleCN: 涡轮通过一连串能量转换把热变成运动。
senses.why: Physics uses the oldest literal sense: the energy is the same quantity but appears in a new form. The prefix trans- is exact here, since the amount is conserved while its dress changes.
senses.whyCN: 物理学用的是最古老的字面义：能量总量不变，只是以新形式出现；这里 trans- 非常准确，因为总量守恒，改变的只是它的「外衣」。

senses.title: Structural Overhaul
senses.titleCN: 结构性改造：体制或产业重构
senses.definition: a far-reaching reorganization of an institution, economy or system
senses.definitionCN: 机构、经济或体制的深远重组
senses.example: The transformation of the postal service took a decade.
senses.exampleCN: 邮政系统的改造用了十年。
senses.why: When the object is an organization, the change is in its structure rather than its surface. The word then belongs to policy and management talk, where it signals depth and scale.
senses.whyCN: 当对象是组织机构时，改变的是结构而非表面；此时该词属于政策与管理话语，标出的是深度与规模。

intro.en: Transformation comes from Late Latin transformatio, built on the verb transformare, itself trans- 'across' plus forma 'form'. It reached English through Old French, so the exact first date is approximate.
intro.cn: transformation 出自晚期拉丁 transformatio，它建立在动词 transformare 之上，而 transformare 即 trans-「跨越」加 forma「形状」。该词经古法语进入英语，确切首见年代为约数。

items.en: Latin forma named a shape, a mould and, by extension, a pattern or beauty. Its family reaches English in form, formal, format, formula, uniform and reform.
items.cn: 拉丁 forma 指形状、模子，并引申指样式或美。其词族以 form、formal、format、formula、uniform、reform 等进入英语。

items.en: Transformare joined trans- 'across' to formare 'to shape', giving 'to shape across, to change the form of'. Classical Latin used it for changing appearance as well as for metamorphosis.
items.cn: transformare 把 trans-「跨越」与 formare「塑造」结合，意为「跨形塑造、改变形状」。古典拉丁既用它指改变外观，也指变形。

items.en: The action noun transformatio named the act of changing form. The -tio suffix marks a completed act viewed as a thing, which is why English -ation nouns so often feel like events.
items.cn: 动作名词 transformatio 指改变形状的行为。-tio 后缀把完成的动作当作一个事物来看，因此英语 -ation 名词常带有「事件」的质感。

items.en: Transformation entered English around the fourteenth century through Old French transformation. Early uses were mostly religious, for a change of the soul or the body.
items.cn: transformation 约于十四世纪经古法语 transformation 进入英语；早期用法多属宗教语境，指灵魂或身体的改变。

items.en: Mathematics, physics and biology later borrowed the word for rule-bound changes of coordinates, of energy form and of genetic material. The core idea stayed the same: one form crosses into another.
items.cn: 数学、物理学与生物学后来借这个词表示受规则约束的坐标变化、能量形式变化与遗传物质变化；核心观念未变：一种形态跨越到另一种形态。

note.en: The first group separates forms built on the same Latin root or on a neighbouring concept. The second holds near-synonyms that differ in scale, speed or type of change.
note.cn: 第一组区分同出拉丁词根、或概念相邻的形态；第二组是变化规模、速度或类型不同的近义词。

entries.definition: The verb meaning 'to change the form of'. It names the doing, while transformation names the deed or its result.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，意为「改变……的形态」；它表示做的动作，而 transformation 表示这一行为或其结果。

entries.definition: The process of passing from one state to another. It stresses the interval, whereas transformation stresses how different the end state is.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，指从一种状态转到另一种状态的过程；它强调中间那段间隔，而 transformation 强调终态差异之大。

entries.definition: A change of one substance or element into another, historically linked to alchemy. It is narrower and more dramatic than transformation.
entries.definitionCN: 指一种物质或元素变成另一种，历史上与炼金术相关；比 transformation 更狭窄、更具戏剧性。

entries.definition: Any difference from a previous state. It says nothing about depth, so it can describe a swapped label or a remade city.
entries.definitionCN: 任何与先前状态的差异；不涉及深度，因此既可指换了一个标签，也可指重建一座城市。

entries.definition: A change from one use, purpose or system to another, as a barn converted into a house. It stresses function rather than shape.
entries.definitionCN: 从一种用途、目的或制度转为另一种，如谷仓改作住宅；强调功能而非形状。

entries.definition: A complete change of form, especially in an animal's development. It is more vivid and more specific than transformation.
entries.definitionCN: 形态的彻底改变，尤指动物发育过程；比 transformation 更生动、更具体。

entries.definition: A thorough examination and repair of a system or machine. It implies restoring fitness rather than becoming something new.
entries.definitionCN: 对系统或机器的彻底检查与修理；暗示恢复良好状态，而不是变成新事物。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: trans- 'across' + forma 'form' + -ation: a crossing from one shape to another.
normal.cn: trans-「跨越」+ forma「形状」+ -ation：从一种形状跨到另一种形状。

normal.en: The family runs transform, transformation, transformer, transformative, transformational, form, format, formula.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 transform、transformation、transformer、transformative、transformational、form、format、formula。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the domains: digital transformation, economic transformation, genetic transformation, energy transformation.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出领域：数字化转型、经济转型、遗传转化、能量转换。

normal.en: transition is the passage; transformation is the difference between the ends.
normal.cn: transition 是过程，transformation 是两端之间的差异。

normal.en: A transformer in the street changes voltage, a literal child of this family.
normal.cn: 街上的变压器改变电压，正是这个词族的字面后代。

abstract.en: Picture a caterpillar dissolving inside a shell and a winged thing climbing out.
abstract.cn: 想象一条毛虫在壳内溶解，一个有翅的东西爬出来。

abstract.en: Picture the same lump of clay becoming a bowl, then a cup, then a bird.
abstract.cn: 想象同一团黏土先变成碗，再变成杯，再变成一只鸟。

abstract.en: Picture a street that looks the same on the map but is unrecognizable from the pavement.
abstract.cn: 想象一条街在地图上没变，站在人行道上却已认不出来。

examples.en: The transformation of the old mill into a museum took three years.
examples.cn: 把旧磨坊改造成博物馆花了三年。

examples.en: Energy transformation always leaves some heat behind.
examples.cn: 能量转换总会留下一些热。

examples.en: His transformation from clerk to mayor surprised no one who knew him.
examples.cn: 他从职员变成市长，认识他的人都不觉得意外。

dict_mnemonic.text: trans（跨越）+ form（形状）+ ation（名词词尾）→ 跨过原有形状 → 转变、改造

root: 拉丁 trans-「跨越」+ forma「形状、模子」→ transformare「改变形状」→ 晚期拉丁 transformatio → 古法语 transformation → 英语 transformation。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses share the picture of crossing from one form to another, applied to an object, a result, a mathematical rule, a cell, a sentence, a person, energy and an institution.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项共享同一幅画面——从一种形态跨到另一种形态——只是施加于对象、结果、数学规则、细胞、句子、人、能量与机构。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the same clay reshaped into a different figure, material unchanged.
core.cn: 核心意象：同一团黏土被重新塑成另一个样子，材质未变。

branches.en: THE JOURNEY AND THE ARRIVAL: one noun names both the act of changing and the new form that results.
branches.cn: 旅程与抵达：同一个名词既指变化的行为，也指变化所产生的新形态。

branches.en: RULE-GOVERNED REWRITING: points and sentences are carried to new positions or shapes while relations are preserved.
branches.cn: 受规则约束的改写：点与句子被带到新位置或新外形，而关系保持不变。

branches.en: MATERIAL FROM OUTSIDE: a cell takes in foreign genes, so the change enters the inherited substance itself.
branches.cn: 外来物质：细胞接纳外源基因，变化深入到遗传物质本身。

branches.en: INNER AND INSTITUTIONAL: a person or an organization crosses into a new state, and the word gains moral or political weight.
branches.cn: 个人与机构：人或组织跨入新状态，该词由此获得道德或政治分量。

branches.en: CONSERVED QUANTITY: energy changes dress but not amount, the most literal use of trans-.
branches.cn: 守恒的量：能量换了外衣却不改总量，这是 trans- 最字面的用法。

intro.en: Transformation is a Latin action noun: a prefix of crossing, the root for form, a verb-forming suffix and a noun ending that turns the act into a thing.
intro.cn: transformation 是拉丁动作名词：表示跨越的前缀、表示形状的词根、构成动词的后缀，以及把行为变成事物的名词词尾。

latinIntro.en: Latin forma supplies form, formal, format, formula, uniform and reform; transformare adds the crossing prefix and supplies transform, transformation, transformer and transformative.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 forma 衍生 form、formal、format、formula、uniform、reform；transformare 加上跨越前缀，衍生 transform、transformation、transformer、transformative。

items.meaning: the act or result of changing form
items.meaningCN: 改变形态的行为或结果
items.example: The transformation left the outer walls intact.
items.exampleCN: 这次改造保留了外墙。

items.example: New irrigation transformed the valley.
items.exampleCN: 新的灌溉改变了山谷的面貌。

items.meaning: a device or person that transforms
items.example: The transformer stepped the voltage down.
items.exampleCN: 变压器把电压降了下来。

items.meaning: having the power to change something deeply
items.example: The trip was a transformative experience.
items.exampleCN: 那次旅行是一次具有改变作用的经历。

items.example: Transformational grammar rewrites deep structures.
items.exampleCN: 转换语法改写深层结构。

items.example: Water takes the form of its container.
items.exampleCN: 水会呈现容器的形状。

items.example: The walls were painted a uniform grey.
items.exampleCN: 墙壁被刷成统一的灰色。

items.meaning: to shape again, usually for improvement
items.example: The law was reformed in 1998.
items.exampleCN: 该法律于 1998 年得到改革。

definition_zh: 过渡的；过渡期的；转变中的；临时的
definition_en: relating to a period or stage in which something passes from one state to another
core_image: 一条短走廊连接两个房间，人正走在中间，既未到达也未离开
scene: The country is in a transitional period between two economic models.
sceneCN: 这里 transitional 指「过渡期的」（第 1 个义项：处在两种状态之间的阶段）；句意：该国正处于两种经济模式之间的过渡期。图中可辨识物件：连接两室的走廊、尚未拆掉的旧标识、临时指示牌。

pos.zh: 过渡的；过渡期的；转变中的；临时性的（由 transition 加 -al 构成）

forms.label: 同根形容词
forms.form: transitive（及物的；可传递的）；transitory（短暂的）

derivatives.zh: 及物的；可传递的（语法与逻辑术语）
短暂的；临时的（同出 ire「走」，但构词路径不同）

senses.title: Of a Betwixt Period
senses.titleCN: 过渡期的：处于两态之间
senses.definition: relating to a period in which something passes from one state to another
senses.definitionCN: 指某事物从一种状态转入另一种状态的那段时间
senses.example: The country is in a transitional period between two economic models.
senses.exampleCN: 该国正处于两种经济模式之间的过渡期。
senses.why: Transition names the going across; the adjective attaches that going to a period. The emphasis falls on the interval itself, when neither the old nor the new state fully holds.
senses.whyCN: transition 指「走过去」这件事，形容词把这一过程挂到一段时间上；重心落在间隔本身——此时旧状态与新状态都不完全成立。

senses.title: Intermediate in Form
senses.titleCN: 中间形态的：既像这头又像那头
senses.definition: having a form that shares features of two neighbouring stages
senses.definitionCN: 形态上兼有两种相邻阶段的特征
senses.example: The fossil shows a transitional form between walking and swimming limbs.
senses.exampleCN: 该化石显示了介于行走与游泳之间的过渡形态。
senses.why: If a thing sits between two forms, it can show parts of both. The adjective marks that mixture rather than a stable third type.
senses.whyCN: 如果一个事物处在两种形态之间，它就可能同时显出两者的局部；这个形容词标出的是这种混合，而不是一种稳定的第三种类型。

senses.title: Provisional
senses.titleCN: 临时的：只为撑到下一阶段
senses.definition: temporary, existing only until the next stage begins
senses.definitionCN: 临时的，只维持到下一阶段开始
senses.example: They moved into a transitional shelter while the house was rebuilt.
senses.exampleCN: 房子重建期间，他们住进了一个临时住所。
senses.why: A stage that will be left behind cannot be built to last. The word therefore often implies 'do not invest too much here', which is a practical warning as much as a description.
senses.whyCN: 一个终将被离开的阶段不能按永久标准来建；因此这个词常暗示「别在这里投入太多」——这既是描述，也是实用警告。

senses.title: Caretaker Government
senses.titleCN: 过渡政府的：代管性质
senses.definition: relating to a government that holds power only until a permanent one is formed
senses.definitionCN: 指只在正式政府成立前掌权的政府
senses.example: The transitional government set the date for the first free election.
senses.exampleCN: 过渡政府确定了首次自由选举的日期。
senses.why: Politics gives the word an institutional sense: the body is legitimate but limited in time and mandate. Its authority comes from the handover it promises.
senses.whyCN: 政治赋予该词制度含义：这个机构合法，但在时限与授权上都受限制；它的权威来自它所承诺的那次交接。

senses.title: Evolutionary Intermediate
senses.titleCN: 进化过渡型：谱系上的中间环节
senses.definition: describing a species or structure thought to lie between ancestral and later forms
senses.definitionCN: 指被认为位于祖先型与后起型之间的物种或结构
senses.example: Palaeontologists argued over whether the animal was truly transitional.
senses.exampleCN: 古生物学家争论这种动物是否真的是过渡类型。
senses.why: Evolution is continuous, but bones are not. The adjective marks a point on a line, and its use always depends on which two ends the researcher has chosen.
senses.whyCN: 演化是连续的，化石却不是；这个形容词标出线上的一个点，而它的用法总取决于研究者选定了哪两个端点。

senses.title: Blended Zone
senses.titleCN: 过渡地带的：两种环境交叠
senses.definition: relating to a zone where two environments or styles overlap
senses.definitionCN: 指两种环境或风格交叠的地带
senses.example: The transitional zone between forest and grassland is rich in species.
senses.exampleCN: 森林与草原之间的过渡地带物种丰富。
senses.why: Space can also have a between. Where two habitats meet, conditions are neither one nor the other, and the adjective names that mixed band.
senses.whyCN: 空间也可以有「之间」。两种生境相接处，条件既不属于这一种也不属于另一种，这个形容词命名的正是那条混合带。

senses.title: Linking Word
senses.titleCN: 过渡词的：连接前后文
senses.definition: describing a word or phrase that links two parts of a text
senses.definitionCN: 指连接文章两部分的词或短语
senses.example: However and therefore are transitional words.
senses.exampleCN: however 与 therefore 都是过渡词。
senses.why: In writing, a transition carries the reader from one idea to the next. The adjective marks those small hinges, which is a direct extension of the spatial picture.
senses.whyCN: 在写作中，transition 把读者从一个观点带到下一个观点；这个形容词标出的正是这些小铰链，是空间画面的直接延伸。

senses.title: Legal Bridge Clauses
senses.titleCN: 过渡条款的：新旧法衔接
senses.definition: describing legal rules that govern the change from an old law to a new one
senses.definitionCN: 指处理旧法向新法转换的法律规则
senses.example: The statute includes transitional provisions for existing contracts.
senses.exampleCN: 该法规为既有合同设有过渡条款。
senses.why: Laws cannot change overnight without harming people who acted under the old rules. Transitional clauses are the legal form of the corridor between two rooms.
senses.whyCN: 法律不能一夜之间改变而不伤害依旧法行事的人；过渡条款就是两个房间之间那条走廊的法律形态。

intro.en: Transitional is transition plus -al. Transition comes from Latin transitio, built on transire 'to go across', itself trans- 'across' plus ire 'to go'. The English adjective is dated only approximately.
intro.cn: transitional 是 transition 加 -al。transition 出自拉丁 transitio，建立在 transire「走过去」之上，而 transire 即 trans-「跨越」加 ire「走」。英语形容词的年代仅为约数。

items.en: Latin ire meant 'to go'. It is one of the most productive verbs in the family: it yields exit, initial, circuit, ambition and many prefixed forms.
items.cn: 拉丁 ire 意为「走」，是这个词族中最高产的动词之一，衍生 exit、initial、circuit、ambition 以及大量带前缀的形式。

items.en: Transire joined trans- 'across' to ire, giving 'to go across, to pass'. It could describe crossing a river, a border or a period of time.
items.cn: transire 把 trans-「跨越」加到 ire 上，意为「走过去、穿过」，可指渡河、越境，也可指度过一段时间。

items.en: The noun transitio named a going across and, in grammar and rhetoric, a passing from one subject to another. The latter sense is the direct ancestor of the English writing term.
items.cn: 名词 transitio 指走过去，在语法与修辞中也指从一个话题转到另一个话题；后一义正是英语写作术语的直接来源。

items.en: English transition appears in the sixteenth century, first as a rhetorical and then as a general term for passage. Transitional was coined later by adding -al.
items.cn: 英语 transition 于十六世纪出现，先作修辞术语，后泛指过渡；transitional 是后来加 -al 构成的。

items.en: The same Latin verb ire produced transitive, transitory and transient by different formations. They are relatives, not synonyms: transitive concerns carrying an action to an object, transitory and transient concern brief duration.
items.cn: 同一个拉丁动词 ire 经不同构词路径产生 transitive、transitory、transient。它们是亲属而非同义词：transitive 指把动作带到宾语，transitory 与 transient 指持续时间短暂。

note.en: The first group separates relatives built on Latin ire that are often confused. The second holds near-synonyms differing in duration and in how complete the change is.
note.cn: 第一组区分同出拉丁 ire、容易混淆的亲属词；第二组是持续时间与变化彻底程度不同的近义词。

entries.definition: Describing a verb that takes a direct object. It has nothing to do with periods of change, despite sharing the Latin verb ire.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，指带直接宾语的动词；尽管同出拉丁 ire，它与「过渡时期」毫无关系。

entries.definition: Lasting only a short time. It stresses shortness, while transitional stresses position between two states.
entries.definitionCN: 只持续很短时间的；强调短暂，而 transitional 强调处于两种状态之间。

entries.definition: Passing quickly, or a temporary visitor or effect. It often describes what has already gone, not a stage that bridges two others.
entries.definitionCN: 迅速消逝的，或指短暂逗留者与短暂效应；常描述已经逝去之物，而非连接两端的阶段。

entries.definition: Situated between two levels or stages. It is neutral about time, whereas transitional implies that the stage will end.
entries.definitionCN: 位于两个层级或阶段之间的；对时间中性，而 transitional 暗示该阶段会结束。

entries.definition: Arranged for the present because a permanent arrangement is not yet possible. It stresses the temporary authority or arrangement.
entries.definitionCN: 因尚无永久安排而暂定的；强调临时性的授权或安排。

entries.definition: Belonging to the time between two events. It is close to transitional but usually follows nouns such as report, payment or leader.
entries.definitionCN: 属于两件事之间那段时间的；接近 transitional，但常修饰 report、payment、leader 等名词。

entries.definition: Serving to connect two sides. It stresses the link itself rather than the period in which the link exists.
entries.definitionCN: 起连接两侧作用的；强调连接本身，而不是连接存在的时期。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: trans- 'across' + ire 'go' + -tion + -al: the adjective of a going-across period.
normal.cn: trans-「跨越」+ ire「走」+ -tion + -al：表示「走过去那段时间」的形容词。

normal.en: The family runs transition, transitional, transit, transient, transitory, transitive.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 transition、transitional、transit、transient、transitory、transitive。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the use: transitional period, transitional government, transitional zone, transitional provisions.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出用法：过渡期、过渡政府、过渡地带、过渡条款。

normal.en: transition is the corridor; transitional describes whatever belongs to the corridor.
normal.cn: transition 是走廊，transitional 描述属于这条走廊的事物。

normal.en: Do not confuse it with transitive, which is about verbs taking objects.
normal.cn: 不要与 transitive 混淆，后者讲的是动词带宾语。

abstract.en: Picture clothes packed in a suitcase but the wardrobe not yet built.
abstract.cn: 想象衣服已装进行李箱，而衣柜还没做好。

abstract.en: Picture a bridge that is open to walkers but has no railings yet.
abstract.cn: 想象一座已允许行人通行、却还没装栏杆的桥。

abstract.en: Picture a shop sign that still shows the old name under the new one.
abstract.cn: 想象一块招牌，新名字下面还留着旧名字。

examples.en: The transitional period lasted eighteen months.
examples.cn: 过渡期持续了十八个月。

examples.en: Fossils of transitional forms are rare because conditions seldom preserve them.
examples.cn: 过渡形态的化石很罕见，因为条件很少能把它们保存下来。

examples.en: The agreement contains transitional clauses protecting older contracts.
examples.cn: 该协议包含保护旧合同的过渡条款。

dict_mnemonic.text: transition（过渡）+ al（……的）→ 过渡的、过渡期的

root: 拉丁 trans-「跨越」+ ire「走」→ transire「走过去」→ transitio「过渡」→ 英语 transition → transitional。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all describe what belongs to a between: a period, an intermediate form, a temporary arrangement, a caretaker government, an evolutionary link, a blended zone, a linking word and a legal bridge.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都描述属于「之间」的事物：一段时间、中间形态、临时安排、代管政府、演化环节、混合地带、连接词与法律桥梁。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a corridor between two rooms, with the traveller still inside it.
core.cn: 核心意象：连接两个房间的走廊，人还在走廊里。

branches.en: THE INTERVAL AND THE MIXTURE: a period between states, and a form that shows features of both.
branches.cn: 间隔与混合：两态之间的一段时间，以及兼显两者特征的形态。

branches.en: PROVISIONAL ARRANGEMENTS: shelters and caretaker governments exist only to carry people to the next stage.
branches.cn: 临时安排：临时住所与过渡政府只为把人送到下一阶段而存在。

branches.en: LINKS IN TIME AND SPACE: a fossil joins two ends of a lineage, and a zone joins two habitats.
branches.cn: 时间与空间上的连接：化石连接谱系两端，地带连接两种生境。

branches.en: LINKS IN TEXT: a word that carries a reader from one idea to the next.
branches.cn: 文本中的连接：把一个读者从一个观点带到下一个观点的词。

branches.en: LINKS IN LAW: clauses that let old contracts survive the arrival of a new rule.
branches.cn: 法律中的连接：让旧合同在新规则到来后仍能存续的条款。

intro.en: Transitional is a Latin noun of going-across with an English adjective ending: a crossing prefix, the verb 'to go', an action noun suffix and -al.
intro.cn: transitional 是拉丁「走过去」名词加英语形容词词尾：跨越前缀、动词「走」、动作名词后缀与 -al。

latinIntro.en: Latin ire supplies transit, transition, transient, transitory, transitive and transitional. The same verb also underlies exit and initial, where the prefixed forms travelled separate paths.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 ire 衍生 transit、transition、transient、transitory、transitive、transitional；同一动词也支撑 exit 与 initial，其带前缀形式各自走了不同的路径。

items.meaning: belonging to a passage between states
items.example: The transitional stage is the hardest for patients.
items.exampleCN: 过渡阶段对病人来说最艰难。

items.meaning: a passage from one state to another
items.meaningCN: 从一种状态到另一种状态的过渡
items.example: The transition from spring to summer was sudden.
items.exampleCN: 春到夏的过渡很突然。

items.meaning: the act of passing; public transport
items.example: The goods were damaged in transit.
items.exampleCN: 货物在运输途中受损。

items.meaningCN: 迅速消逝的；短暂逗留者
items.example: The pain was transient and soon faded.
items.exampleCN: 疼痛是短暂的，很快就消退了。

items.example: Fame of that kind is transitory.
items.exampleCN: 那种名声是转瞬即逝的。

items.meaning: carrying the action to an object
items.example: Break is transitive in 'break the glass'.
items.exampleCN: 在 break the glass 中，break 是及物的。

items.meaning: to go out; a way out
items.example: The rear exit leads to the yard.
items.exampleCN: 后出口通向院子。

items.example: The initial estimate was far too low.
items.exampleCN: 最初的估计低得离谱。

definition_zh: 传输；播送；传动装置；传播；传承；透射
definition_en: the act or process of sending something from one place or person to another, or the thing so sent
core_image: 一排中继塔把同一束信号接力送向地平线，信号在中途被放大后继续前行
scene: The transmission of the signal across the valley required three relay towers.
sceneCN: 这里 transmission 指「传输」（第 1 个义项：把信号从一处送到另一处）；句意：把信号传过山谷需要三座中继塔。图中可辨识物件：中继塔、抛物面天线、山谷剖面。

pos.zh: 传输；播送；传动装置；传播；传承；透射（作「传动装置」时可指汽车变速器）

collocations.zh: 无线电播送；无线电发射

forms.label: 形容词形式
forms.form: transmissible（可传播的）；transmissive（传输的；透射的）

derivatives.zh: 任务；使命；传教（同出 mittere「送」，但前缀不同）

senses.title: Sending a Signal
senses.titleCN: 信号传输：把信息送到远处
senses.definition: the sending of signals or data from one point to another
senses.definitionCN: 把信号或数据从一点送到另一点
senses.example: The transmission of the signal across the valley required three relay towers.
senses.exampleCN: 把信号传过山谷需要三座中继塔。
senses.why: Mit- in Latin mittere means 'to send'. trans- adds 'across'. The noun therefore names a sending that crosses a distance, and the distance is the point of the word.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 mittere 的词根 mit- 意为「送」，trans- 再加「跨越」；因此这个名词命名的是跨过一段距离的发送，而这段距离正是词的重点。

senses.title: A Broadcast
senses.titleCN: 播出的节目：电台送出的一档内容
senses.definition: a programme or message that is broadcast
senses.definitionCN: 被播送出去的节目或讯息
senses.example: We heard the transmission at midnight on a shortwave radio.
senses.exampleCN: 我们在午夜用短波收音机听到了那段广播。
senses.why: The product of sending can be named by the same noun as the sending. Radio made this sense common: a transmission is what came out of the transmitter.
senses.whyCN: 发送的产物可以用与发送行为相同的名词来指称；无线电使这一义项普及：a transmission 就是从发射机里出来的东西。

senses.title: Gearbox
senses.titleCN: 传动装置：把动力传到车轮
senses.definition: the mechanism that carries power from an engine to the wheels
senses.definitionCN: 把动力从发动机传到车轮的机械装置
senses.example: The car's transmission slipped when it climbed the hill.
senses.exampleCN: 汽车爬坡时变速器打滑了。
senses.why: A machine also sends power across a gap, from engine to road. Mechanics borrowed the same noun, and the whole gearbox came to be called the transmission.
senses.whyCN: 机器也要把动力跨过一段距离送出，从发动机到路面；机械学借用了同一个名词，整个变速箱于是被称为 transmission。

senses.title: Spread of Disease
senses.titleCN: 疾病传播：病原从一个宿主到另一个
senses.definition: the passing of a disease from one person, animal or place to another
senses.definitionCN: 疾病从一个人、动物或地点传到另一个
senses.example: Mosquitoes are the main route of transmission for the virus.
senses.exampleCN: 蚊子是该病毒的主要传播途径。
senses.why: An infection is something carried, so the sending image fits exactly. Public health fixed phrases such as transmission route and transmission rate around this sense.
senses.whyCN: 感染是可以被携带的东西，所以「送出」的意象完全吻合；公共卫生围绕这一义项固定了 transmission route（传播途径）、transmission rate（传播率）等说法。

senses.title: Handing Down Knowledge
senses.titleCN: 传承：把知识与传统交给下一代
senses.definition: the passing on of knowledge, customs or traditions to later generations
senses.definitionCN: 把知识、习俗或传统交给后代
senses.example: Oral transmission kept the stories alive for centuries.
senses.exampleCN: 口耳相传让这些故事存续了数百年。
senses.why: What is sent need not be physical. Stories and skills cross from one generation to the next, and the word marks that continuity rather than the content.
senses.whyCN: 被送出的不必是实物；故事与技艺从一代跨到下一代，这个词标出的是延续性，而不是内容本身。

senses.title: Passage Through Matter
senses.titleCN: 透射：波穿过介质而不被吸收
senses.definition: the passage of light, heat or sound through a material
senses.definitionCN: 光、热或声穿过某种物质
senses.example: The transmission of light through the glass fell as the coating thickened.
senses.exampleCN: 随着涂层加厚，光透过玻璃的透射量下降了。
senses.why: Physics keeps the spatial core: something travels through a medium rather than stopping at its surface. The contrast pair is reflection or absorption.
senses.whyCN: 物理学保留空间核心：某物穿过介质，而不是停在表面；与它成对的概念是反射或吸收。

senses.title: Message Delivery
senses.titleCN: 讯息发送：从发件方到收件方
senses.definition: the sending of a message or document to its recipient
senses.definitionCN: 把讯息或文件发送给收件方
senses.example: Automatic transmission of the report failed twice.
senses.exampleCN: 报告的自动发送失败了两次。
senses.why: Digital systems made this everyday: an email is complete only when transmission succeeds. Here the noun is almost a technical synonym for delivery.
senses.whyCN: 数字系统让这一用法日常化：一封邮件只有在 transmission 成功时才算完成；此时该名词几乎是 delivery 的技术同义词。

senses.title: Inheritance of Genes
senses.titleCN: 基因传递：性状随遗传递到子代
senses.definition: the passing of genetic material from parents to offspring
senses.definitionCN: 遗传物质由亲代传给子代
senses.example: The transmission of the trait followed a simple dominant pattern.
senses.exampleCN: 该性状的传递遵循简单的显性规律。
senses.why: Genetics uses the word for what crosses from parent to child. The material is microscopic, but the direction and the sending are the same as in radio.
senses.whyCN: 遗传学用这个词指从亲代跨到子代的东西；物质虽显微，方向与「送出」却与无线电相同。

intro.en: Transmission comes from Latin transmissio, built on transmittere 'to send across', made of trans- 'across' and mittere 'to send'. The English word is recorded from the sixteenth century, but the exact date is approximate.
intro.cn: transmission 出自拉丁 transmissio，建立在 transmittere「跨送」之上，由 trans-「跨越」与 mittere「送」构成。英语该词自十六世纪有记录，但确切年代为约数。

items.en: Mittere meant 'to send, let go, release'. Its family is wide: mission, missile, admit, submit, permit, commit, emit and transmit all come from it, each shaped by a different prefix.
items.cn: mittere 意为「送、放出、让走」。其词族很广：mission、missile、admit、submit、permit、commit、emit、transmit 都出自它，各自被不同的前缀塑造成不同含义。

items.en: Transmittere meant literally 'to send across', used for sending a person, a message or a thing over a distance. Classical Latin also used it for handing something over to another's care.
items.cn: transmittere 字面意为「送过去」，用于把人、讯息或物品送过一段距离；古典拉丁也用它指把某物交给他人照管。

items.en: The action noun transmissio named the sending across and the thing handed on. The -sio spelling comes from the past participle stem transmissus.
items.cn: 动作名词 transmissio 指「跨送」这一行为，也指被交送之物；-sio 的拼法来自过去分词词干 transmissus。

items.en: English transmission appears in the sixteenth century, first in legal and religious senses of handing something over. The first precise citation is not certain.
items.cn: 英语 transmission 于十六世纪出现，最初用于法律与宗教语境，指把某物交付出去；确切的首见书证并不确定。

items.en: Telegraphy, radio and later genetics each adopted the word for their own kind of sending. The mechanics of a car borrowed it too, so the same noun now names a gearbox, a broadcast and a hereditary trait.
items.cn: 电报、无线电以及后来的遗传学，各自把这词用在自己那一类「发送」上；汽车机械也借用了它，于是同一个名词如今既指变速器，也指广播节目与遗传性状。

note.en: The first group separates words built on Latin mittere that look similar. The second holds near-synonyms differing in what is carried and how far.
note.cn: 第一组区分同出拉丁 mittere、外形相近的词；第二组是所载之物与传播距离不同的近义词。

entries.definition: The verb meaning 'to send across'. It names the action; transmission names the action as a thing or its result.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，意为「跨送、传输」；它表示动作，而 transmission 把动作当作事物或其结果来命名。

entries.definition: A passage from one state to another, built on ire 'to go', not on mittere 'to send'. It concerns change, not delivery.
entries.definitionCN: 指从一种状态到另一种状态的过渡，出自 ire「走」而非 mittere「送」；它讲变化，不讲投送。

entries.definition: Mission is a sending out with a purpose, from mittere with no crossing prefix. Transmission adds trans- and loses the sense of a commissioned task.
entries.definitionCN: mission 指有目的的派出，出自 mittere 而不带跨越前缀；transmission 加上 trans-，同时失去了「受命任务」的含义。

entries.tag: move from one holder to another
entries.definition: The moving of something from one place, account or person to another. It stresses change of owner or location more than the sending itself.
entries.definitionCN: 把某物从一处、一个账户或一个人转到另一处；比 transmission 更强调所有者或位置的改变。

entries.definition: A sending of a programme to many receivers at once. It is narrower than transmission and implies public reception.
entries.definitionCN: 把节目一次发送给众多接收者；比 transmission 狭窄，并暗示公众接收。

entries.definition: The carrying of something, or a legal deed transferring property. It is formal and rare outside law and transport.
entries.definitionCN: 运送，或指转让财产的法律契据；正式用语，在法律与运输之外少见。

entries.definition: The spreading of something, especially waves, ideas or plants, often with increase in number. It stresses spread, not a single send.
entries.definitionCN: 某物的扩散，尤指波、观念或植物，常含数量增加；强调扩散，而非单次发送。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: trans- 'across' + mittere 'send' + -sion: a sending across.
normal.cn: trans-「跨越」+ mittere「送」+ -sion：跨过距离的发送。

normal.en: The mittere family runs transmit, transmission, transmitter, mission, missile, admit, submit, permit, emit.
normal.cn: mittere 词族包括 transmit、transmission、transmitter、mission、missile、admit、submit、permit、emit。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the fields: data transmission, disease transmission, automatic transmission, cultural transmission.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出领域：数据传输、疾病传播、自动变速器、文化传承。

normal.en: transmission sends something across; transition changes a state; transfer changes hands.
normal.cn: transmission 把东西送过去，transition 改变状态，transfer 更换持有者。

normal.en: A car's gearbox is called a transmission because it sends power to the wheels.
normal.cn: 汽车变速箱叫 transmission，因为它把动力送到车轮。

abstract.en: Picture a line of runners passing one sealed letter from hand to hand until it reaches the last runner.
abstract.cn: 想象一列跑者把一封密封的信逐手相传，直到最后一个跑者手中。

abstract.en: Picture a lamp behind a thick curtain: the glow arrives, but the lamp itself never does.
abstract.cn: 想象厚帘后的一盏灯：光到了，灯本身却从未到达。

abstract.en: Picture a grandmother teaching a song to a child who will teach it to another child.
abstract.cn: 想象祖母把一首歌教给孩子，孩子以后又把它教给另一个孩子。

examples.en: The transmission of the disease slowed once the water was treated.
examples.cn: 水经过处理之后，该疾病的传播变慢了。

examples.en: Engineers measured transmission loss along the new cable.
examples.cn: 工程师测量了新电缆上的传输损耗。

examples.en: The transmission of traditional skills depends on daily practice.
examples.cn: 传统技艺的传承依赖于日常练习。

dict_mnemonic.text: trans（跨越）+ miss（送）+ ion（名词词尾）→ 送过去 → 传输、传播

root: 拉丁 trans-「跨越」+ mittere「送」→ transmittere「送过去」→ transmissio「跨送」→ 英语 transmission。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all send something across a gap: a signal, a broadcast, mechanical power, an infection, a tradition, light through matter, a message and a gene.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都把某物送过一段距离：信号、广播节目、机械动力、感染、传统、穿过物质的光、讯息与基因。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: relay towers passing one signal to the horizon, each one boosting it onward.
core.cn: 核心意象：中继塔把同一束信号接力送向地平线，每一座都把它放大后继续送出。

branches.en: ENGINEERED SENDING: signals and messages cross a designed channel, and success is measured by arrival.
branches.cn: 工程化发送：信号与讯息跨过设计好的通道，成功与否以是否送达来衡量。

branches.en: THE THING SENT: what leaves the transmitter can itself be called a transmission.
branches.cn: 被送出之物：从发射机出来的东西本身也可称为 a transmission。

branches.en: POWER TO THE ROAD: a gearbox carries torque across metal, the mechanical branch of the same image.
branches.cn: 动力到路面：变速箱让扭矩跨过金属传递，是同一意象的机械分支。

branches.en: CARRIERS OF LIFE: infections, traditions and genes are all handed from one bearer to the next.
branches.cn: 生命的载体：感染、传统与基因都由一个携带者交给下一个。

branches.en: THROUGH A MEDIUM: light travels through glass rather than stopping at its face.
branches.cn: 穿过介质：光穿过玻璃，而不是停在它的表面。

intro.en: Transmission is a Latin action noun on the verb 'to send': a prefix of crossing, the send-root, and a noun suffix made from the past participle stem.
intro.cn: transmission 是建立在动词「送」上的拉丁动作名词：跨越前缀、表示「送」的词根，以及由过去分词词干构成的名词后缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin mittere supplies mission, missile, admit, submit, permit, commit, emit, transmit and transmission. The prefix decides the direction of each: out, in, under, through or across.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 mittere 衍生 mission、missile、admit、submit、permit、commit、emit、transmit、transmission；前缀决定各自的方向：向外、向内、向下、穿过或跨越。

items.meaning: a sending across; the thing sent
items.example: The transmission reached the coast by morning.
items.exampleCN: 信号到早晨已抵达海岸。

items.example: The station transmits on two frequencies.
items.exampleCN: 该电台用两个频率播送。

items.example: The transmitter was mounted on the ridge.
items.exampleCN: 发射机安装在山脊上。

items.example: The strain proved highly transmissible.
items.exampleCN: 该毒株被证明极易传播。

items.example: The film is transmissive in the infrared.
items.exampleCN: 该薄膜在红外波段可透射。

items.meaning: a sending out with a purpose
items.example: The team was sent on a rescue mission.
items.exampleCN: 该队被派出执行救援任务。

items.meaning: to send out, as light or sound
items.example: The diode emits a narrow beam.
items.exampleCN: 该二极管发出一束窄光。

items.meaning: to send under; to yield or present
items.example: Please submit the form by Friday.
items.exampleCN: 请在周五前提交表格。

latinEntries.meaning: a sending across; a handing over

definition_zh: 可变性；变异性；变动幅度；（统计）离散程度
definition_en: the quality or degree of being changeable, or the extent to which values differ from one another
core_image: 同一块地的十次收成排成一列，高低差别明显，尺子量出的正是这些差别
scene: Rainfall variability makes farming risky in this region.
sceneCN: 这里 variability 指「变动幅度」（第 1 个义项：随时间或个案变化、不稳定）；句意：降水量的变动使该地区的农业风险很大。图中可辨识物件：逐年降水柱状图、干裂的田块、蓄水池。

pos.zh: 可变性；变异性；变动幅度；（统计）离散程度（多为不可数，也可用 variabilities 指多种变异）

senses.title: Changeability
senses.titleCN: 可变性：会变的性质
senses.definition: the quality of being changeable
senses.definitionCN: 容易发生变化的性质
senses.example: Rainfall variability makes farming risky in this region.
senses.exampleCN: 降水量的变化使该地区的农业风险很大。
senses.why: Varius in Latin meant 'diverse, spotted, changeable'. The noun -ability turns that quality into a measurable thing: not 'it changes' but 'how much it changes'.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 varius 意为「多样的、有斑点的、易变的」。名词后缀 -ability 把这种性质变成可度量之物：不是「它变」，而是「它变得有多少」。

senses.title: Statistical Spread
senses.titleCN: 统计离散：数值彼此差多少
senses.definition: the extent to which values in a set differ from one another
senses.definitionCN: 一组数值之间相互差异的程度
senses.example: The variability of the scores was low, so the class was evenly matched.
senses.exampleCN: 分数的离散程度很低，说明这个班水平相当。
