senses.why: Statistics needs a word for difference rather than average. Variability measures how far the members scatter, which is why it pairs with standard deviation and range.
senses.whyCN: 统计学需要一个词来表示「差异」而不是「平均」；variability 量的是成员分散得多远，因此它与标准差、极差等概念搭配。

senses.title: Biological Variation
senses.titleCN: 生物变异：同种个体间的差异
senses.definition: the range of differences among individuals of a species
senses.definitionCN: 同一物种个体之间的差异范围
senses.example: Genetic variability gives a population a chance to survive a new disease.
senses.exampleCN: 遗传变异让一个种群有机会熬过新的疾病。
senses.why: Evolution depends on differences, not on uniformity. Here variability is a resource: the wider the spread, the more likely some member fits a changed world.
senses.whyCN: 演化依赖差异而非整齐划一。此时 variability 是一种资源：分布越宽，越可能有某个成员适应改变了的世界。

senses.title: Climate Fluctuation
senses.titleCN: 气候波动：年际起伏
senses.definition: the degree to which climate conditions differ from year to year or place to place
senses.definitionCN: 气候条件在年际或地点之间的差异程度
senses.example: Natural variability hides the slower trend for decades.
senses.exampleCN: 自然波动会在数十年里掩盖较慢的趋势。
senses.why: A trend is a direction; variability is the noise around it. Climate science separates the two, because a wet year says nothing about a warming century.
senses.whyCN: 趋势是方向，变率是围绕方向的噪声。气候科学要把两者分开，因为一个多雨的年份说明不了整个世纪在变暖。

senses.title: Measurement Noise
senses.titleCN: 测量波动：同一对象反复测出的差别
senses.definition: the differences between repeated measurements of the same thing
senses.definitionCN: 对同一对象反复测量所得结果之间的差异
senses.example: The variability between the three readings came from the old balance.
senses.exampleCN: 三次读数的波动来自那台旧天平。
senses.why: Instruments never repeat perfectly. The noun names that scatter, and a low value is a sign of a trustworthy method rather than of a stable world.
senses.whyCN: 仪器从不完美重复；这个名词命名的正是那种分散，而数值低说明方法可信，并不说明世界稳定。

senses.title: Beat-to-Beat Range
senses.titleCN: 心率变异性：逐次心跳的间隔差
senses.definition: the variation in the time between heartbeats
senses.definitionCN: 心跳之间时间间隔的变化
senses.example: High heart rate variability is usually a sign of a healthy nervous system.
senses.exampleCN: 较高的心率变异性通常意味着神经系统健康。
senses.why: Medicine uses the statistical sense on a living signal. A perfectly regular pulse can be a warning, so variability here is not noise but information.
senses.whyCN: 医学把统计义用在活体信号上；完全规律的脉搏反而可能是警讯，因此这里的变异性不是噪声，而是信息。

senses.title: Genetic Range
senses.titleCN: 遗传变异度：基因库里的多样性
senses.definition: the amount of genetic difference carried within a group
senses.definitionCN: 一个群体内部所携带的遗传差异总量
senses.example: The island population lost much of its genetic variability.
senses.exampleCN: 这个岛屿种群失去了大部分遗传变异。
senses.why: Small populations lose variants by chance. The word then measures a store of options, which conservation biology treats as something to protect.
senses.whyCN: 小种群会因偶然丢失变体；此时这个词量的是选项的储备，保护生物学把它当作需要保护的对象。

senses.title: Inconsistency of Quality
senses.titleCN: 质量波动：好坏不稳
senses.definition: the unevenness of quality or performance over time
senses.definitionCN: 质量或表现在时间上的不均衡
senses.example: Customers complained about the variability of the product.
senses.exampleCN: 顾客抱怨该产品的质量波动。
senses.why: In manufacturing, variability is the enemy of trust: two units of the same model should behave alike. The word shifts from description to a defect to be reduced.
senses.whyCN: 在制造业，变异性是信任的敌人：同一型号的两件产品应当表现一致。此时该词从描述变成一种应当被降低的缺陷。

intro.en: Variability is formed from variable plus -ity, and variable comes from Latin variabilis, from variare 'to change', from varius 'diverse, spotted'. The origin of varius itself is uncertain, and the first English date is only approximate.
intro.cn: variability 由 variable 加 -ity 构成；variable 出自拉丁 variabilis，来自 variare「变化」，而 variare 又来自 varius「多样的、有斑点的」。varius 本身的来源不确定，英语首见年代仅为约数。

items.en: Varius meant 'of various kinds, spotted, mottled, changeable'. Its deeper origin is uncertain: some connect it with a root for 'to weave or vary', but no source is agreed.
items.cn: varius 意为「多种多样的、有斑点的、斑驳的、易变的」。它更深的来源不确定：有人把它与表示「编织、变化」的词根联系起来，但没有公认的来源。此处标注为来源不确定。

items.en: The verb variare meant 'to diversify, to change, to alternate'. It was used for colouring, for altering a plan and for taking turns.
items.cn: 动词 variare 意为「使多样、改变、交替」，可用于上色、改变计划，也可指轮流。

items.en: Variabilis meant 'changeable, inconstant'. Latin built it with the suffix -bilis, 'able to be', which English keeps in -able.
items.cn: variabilis 意为「可变的、不恒定的」。拉丁语用后缀 -bilis「能够被……」构成它，英语以 -able 保留了这个后缀。

items.en: English variable appears in the fifteenth century from Old French. Variability followed later, adding -ity to make the quality into a noun. Exact first citations are uncertain.
items.cn: 英语 variable 于十五世纪经古法语出现；variability 稍后加上 -ity，把这种性质变成名词。确切的首见书证不确定。

items.en: In the nineteenth and twentieth centuries variability acquired a technical sense in statistics and biology: the measurable spread of a set of observations. The old idea of changeability became a number.
items.cn: 十九与二十世纪，variability 在统计学与生物学中获得专门含义：一组观测值可测量的离散程度。古老的「易变」观念由此变成了一个数字。

note.en: The first group separates nouns and adjectives of the same Latin family that are easy to mix. The second holds near-synonyms from statistics and everyday speech.
note.cn: 第一组区分同出拉丁词族、容易混淆的名词与形容词；第二组是统计学与日常用语中的近义词。

entries.definition: A particular change or difference, or the act of varying. It counts differences; variability measures how large the differences are.
entries.definitionCN: 指某一具体变化或差异，或变化的行为；它数差异的个数，而 variability 量差异的大小。

entries.definition: In statistics, the average squared deviation; in law, a permission to depart from a rule. It is a precise quantity, not a general quality.
entries.definitionCN: 统计学中指离差平方的平均值；法律中指对规则适用的例外许可。它是精确的量，不是一般的性质。

entries.definition: The adjective 'changeable' or the noun for a quantity that can take different values. The noun names the thing that varies, not the amount of varying.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词「易变的」，或指可取不同值的量；该名词命名的是会变的东西，而不是变化的幅度。

entries.definition: An irregular rising and falling, as of prices. It stresses movement up and down rather than the spread of values.
entries.definitionCN: 不规则地上下起伏，如价格；强调上下运动，而不是数值的分散。

entries.definition: A tendency to change or become unbalanced. It carries more risk and less measurement than variability.
entries.definitionCN: 倾向于变化或失衡；比 variability 含更多风险意味，更少测量意味。

entries.definition: The presence of many different kinds. It counts variety of types, while variability measures differences within a measure.
entries.definitionCN: 存在许多不同种类；它数类型的多样，而 variability 量同一度量内的差异。

entries.definition: The spreading of values around a centre. It is a technical near-synonym of variability in statistics.
entries.definitionCN: 数值围绕中心散布；在统计学中是 variability 的技术性近义词。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: varius 'varied' + -able 'able to' + -ity: the quality of being able to vary.
normal.cn: varius「多样的」+ -able「能够」+ -ity：能够变化的性质。

normal.en: The family runs vary, variable, variability, variation, variance, variant, various.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 vary、variable、variability、variation、variance、variant、various。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the fields: climate variability, genetic variability, heart rate variability, measurement variability.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出领域：气候变率、遗传变异度、心率变异性、测量波动。

normal.en: variability is how much things differ; variation is a particular difference.
normal.cn: variability 是差异有多大，variation 是某一处具体的差异。

normal.en: Low variability in a factory is good; high variability in a gene pool is good.
normal.cn: 工厂里变异性低是好事，基因库里变异性高是好事。

abstract.en: Picture a row of ten identical cups, then a row where every cup is a different height.
abstract.cn: 想象一排十只一模一样的杯子，再想象一排每只高度都不同的杯子。

abstract.en: Picture a ruler laid across a scatter of dots to show how far they wander from the middle.
abstract.cn: 想象一把尺横放在散乱的点上，用来显示它们离中心有多远。

abstract.en: Picture a heartbeat that is never exactly on time, and a doctor smiling at the irregularity.
abstract.cn: 想象一颗从不准时的心跳，而医生对这种不规则微笑。

examples.en: The study measured the variability of response times across four groups.
examples.cn: 该研究测量了四组反应时间的波动程度。

examples.en: High variability in rainfall forces farmers to store water.
examples.cn: 降水的剧烈变动迫使农民储水。

examples.en: Reducing variability is the first aim of any production line.
examples.cn: 降低波动是任何生产线的首要目标。

dict_mnemonic.text: variable（可变的）+ ility（性质）→ 可变的程度 → 可变性、变异性

root: 拉丁 varius「多样的、有斑点的」（来源不确定）→ variare「变化」→ variabilis「可变的」→ 英语 variable → variability。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all measure how much something differs: a general quality, a statistical spread, biological difference, climate noise, instrument scatter, heartbeat range, genetic variety and uneven quality.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都在量「差异有多大」：一般性质、统计离散、生物差异、气候噪声、仪器散布、心跳间隔、遗传多样与质量起伏。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a row of unequal harvests, and a ruler laid across the differences.
core.cn: 核心意象：一排高低不等的收成，一把尺子横放在这些差异之上。

branches.en: QUALITY BECOMES QUANTITY: a vague property of being changeable turns into a measurable spread.
branches.cn: 性质变成数量：模糊的「易变」性质变成了可测量的离散度。

branches.en: VARIATION AS RESOURCE: genetic differences give a population options, and a narrow pool is a risk.
branches.cn: 变异作为资源：遗传差异给种群提供选项，而狭窄的基因库是一种风险。

branches.en: NOISE VERSUS TREND: year-to-year wobble can hide a slow direction for decades.
branches.cn: 噪声与趋势：年际抖动可以在数十年里掩盖缓慢的方向。

branches.en: READING A SIGNAL: in instruments the scatter means error, while in a heartbeat it can mean health.
branches.cn: 读取信号：在仪器上散布意味着误差，在心跳上却可能意味着健康。

branches.en: QUALITY CONTROL: identical products should behave alike, so variability becomes a defect to reduce.
branches.cn: 质量控制：相同产品应当表现一致，因此变异性成为需要降低的缺陷。

intro.en: Variability is a Latin-rooted adjective turned into a quality-noun: a root meaning 'varied', the suffix -able, and the suffix -ity.
intro.cn: variability 是拉丁词根的形容词转化为性质名词：表示「多样」的词根、后缀 -able，以及后缀 -ity。

latinIntro.en: Latin varius and variare supply vary, variable, variability, variation, variance, variant, various and varietas, the ancestor of variety.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 varius 与 variare 衍生 vary、variable、variability、variation、variance、variant、various，以及 variety 的祖形 varietas。

items.example: Variability in the data was greater than expected.
items.exampleCN: 数据的波动比预期更大。

items.meaning: changeable; a quantity that can vary
items.meaningCN: 易变的；可取不同值的量
items.example: Temperature is the key variable in the experiment.
items.exampleCN: 温度是该实验的关键变量。

items.example: Results vary widely between regions.
items.exampleCN: 各地结果差异很大。

items.meaning: a change; a difference in form
items.example: Slight variation in colour is normal.
items.exampleCN: 颜色的轻微差异是正常的。

items.meaningCN: 差异；离差平方的平均值
items.example: The variance of the sample was small.
items.exampleCN: 样本的方差很小。

items.meaning: a different form of the same thing
items.example: A rare variant appeared in the north.
items.exampleCN: 北方出现了一种罕见的变体。

items.example: The shelf held various tools.
items.exampleCN: 架子上放着各种工具。

items.example: The garden grows a wide variety of herbs.
items.exampleCN: 园子里种着多种香草。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 多样的；有斑点的；易变的（更深来源不确定）

definition_zh: 易变的；多变的；不稳定的；（数学与实验中的）变量
definition_en: liable to change, or a quantity, factor or symbol that can take different values
core_image: 同一块仪表上的指针来回摆动，刻度并不停在同一个数字上
scene: Temperature is the key variable in this experiment, so it must be recorded every hour.
sceneCN: 这里 variable 指「变量」（第 2 个义项：可取不同数值、需要被观测或控制的因素）；句意：温度是这个实验的关键变量，必须每小时记录。图中可辨识物件：温度计、记录表、可调加热器。

pos.zh: 易变的；多变的；不稳定的（可比较级 more variable, most variable）
变量；可变因素；可变符号（数学、统计、实验与计算机用语）

senses.title: Liable to Change
senses.titleCN: 易变的：说变就变
senses.definition: likely to change without warning
senses.definitionCN: 容易在没有预警的情况下发生变化
senses.example: The weather here is variable, so carry a coat.
senses.exampleCN: 这里天气多变，带件外套吧。
senses.why: Varius meant 'varied, changeable'. As an adjective the word simply reports that change happens; how much and how often is left to context.
senses.whyCN: varius 意为「多样的、易变的」。作形容词时，这个词只是报告「会变」这一事实；变多少、多久变一次，则交给语境。

senses.title: Mathematical Variable
senses.titleCN: 数学变量：可取不同值
senses.definition: a symbol or quantity that can stand for different values
senses.definitionCN: 可以代表不同数值的符号或量
senses.example: In the equation, x is the variable and 7 is the constant.
senses.exampleCN: 在这个方程里，x 是变量，7 是常量。
senses.why: Mathematics makes the adjective into a noun: the thing that can vary is called a variable. Its opposite, the constant, holds one value throughout.
senses.whyCN: 数学把这个形容词变成名词：会变化的那个东西就叫 variable；与之相反的 constant 则始终只取一个值。

senses.title: Experimental Factor
senses.titleCN: 实验变量：被操控或观测的因素
senses.definition: a factor in an experiment that is controlled, changed or measured
senses.definitionCN: 实验中受控制、被改变或被测量的因素
senses.example: Temperature is the key variable in this experiment, so it must be recorded every hour.
senses.exampleCN: 温度是这个实验的关键变量，必须每小时记录。
senses.why: An experiment works by changing one thing and watching another. Both are variables; the labels independent and dependent record which one is moved and which one answers.
senses.whyCN: 实验的做法是改变一件事、观察另一件事；两者都是变量，而 independent 与 dependent 这两个标签记录的是哪一个被改变、哪一个作出回应。

senses.title: Unreliable, Not Steady
senses.titleCN: 不稳定的：表现时好时坏
senses.definition: not steady in quality or performance
senses.definitionCN: 质量或表现不稳定的
senses.example: His early results were variable, which made reviewers cautious.
senses.exampleCN: 他早期的结果时好时坏，让评审人格外谨慎。
senses.why: Applied to people or outputs, the adjective carries a mild judgement. It does not say 'bad' but 'cannot be relied on to repeat', which is often worse for a reader.
senses.whyCN: 用于人或成果时，这个形容词带轻微评判：它不说「差」，而说「不能指望它重复」，这对读者往往更糟。

senses.title: Programme Variable
senses.titleCN: 程序变量：内存中的具名值
senses.definition: a named storage location in a program whose value can change
senses.definitionCN: 程序中值可以改变的具名存储位置
senses.example: The program stores each score in a variable called total.
senses.exampleCN: 程序把每个分数存入名为 total 的变量。
senses.why: Computing borrowed the mathematical noun and gave it a body: a name attached to a slot in memory. The value may change; the name stays.
senses.whyCN: 计算机借用了数学名词，并给它一个实体：附着在内存槽上的名字。值可以变，名字不变。

senses.title: Biologically Variable
senses.titleCN: 变异大的：个体差异显著
senses.definition: showing noticeable differences among individuals or samples
senses.definitionCN: 个体或样本之间差异明显的
senses.example: The species is highly variable in leaf shape.
senses.exampleCN: 该物种的叶形变异很大。
senses.why: In biology a variable species is not disorganized; it is genetically rich. The adjective describes spread within a group rather than unreliability.
senses.whyCN: 在生物学中，一个 variable 的物种并非杂乱无章，而是遗传丰富；这个形容词描述的是群体内部的分布宽度，而不是不可靠。

senses.title: Statistical Variable
senses.titleCN: 统计变量：被测量的特征
senses.definition: a characteristic that can be measured and takes different values across cases
senses.definitionCN: 可以测量、并在不同个案中取不同值的特征
senses.example: Age was treated as a continuous variable in the model.
senses.exampleCN: 在该模型中，年龄被当作连续变量处理。
senses.why: Statistics names the feature, not the numbers. Because the feature can take many values, the same word serves for income, height and reaction time.
senses.whyCN: 统计学命名的是特征，而不是数字；由于特征可取许多值，同一个词可用来指收入、身高与反应时间。

senses.title: Changeable Cost
senses.titleCN: 可变的（成本）：随产量起伏
senses.definition: changing with output or activity, as a cost does
senses.definitionCN: 随产量或业务量而变，如成本
senses.example: Fuel is a variable cost; rent is fixed.
senses.exampleCN: 燃料是可变成本，租金是固定成本。
senses.why: Business pairs variable with fixed. The word marks what moves when production moves, which is why it matters so much in pricing decisions.
senses.whyCN: 商业语境把 variable 与 fixed 成对使用；这个词标出的是产量变动时会跟着动的那部分，因此它在定价决策中格外重要。

intro.en: Variable comes from Latin variabilis 'changeable', from variare 'to change', from varius 'varied, spotted'. The deeper origin of varius is uncertain; the English word is recorded from the fifteenth century, though the exact date is approximate.
intro.cn: variable 出自拉丁 variabilis「可变的」，来自 variare「变化」，而 variare 又来自 varius「多样的、有斑点的」。varius 的更早来源不确定；英语该词自十五世纪有记录，确切年代为约数。

items.en: Varius meant 'varied, mottled, changeable'. Its own origin is uncertain; suggested links with a root for weaving or bending are not established. The word is best treated as inherited without a known source.
items.cn: varius 意为「多样的、斑驳的、易变的」。它自身的来源不确定；有人提出与「编织」或「弯折」词根的联系，但未获证实。最好把它视为来源不明的承继词。此处标注为来源不确定。

items.en: Variare meant 'to diversify, alter, alternate'. It covered changes of colour, of plan and of turn, and it is the direct source of English vary.
items.cn: variare 意为「使多样、改变、交替」，涵盖颜色、计划与轮次的变化，是英语 vary 的直接来源。

items.en: Variabilis, 'changeable', was formed with -bilis 'able to be'. English keeps this suffix as -able, so the shape of the word still announces its meaning.
items.cn: variabilis「可变的」由 -bilis「能够被……」构成；英语以 -able 保留这个后缀，因此词的形状至今仍在宣告它的含义。

items.en: English variable entered through Old French in the fifteenth century. Early uses were mostly adjectival, for inconstant things, people or fortune.
items.cn: 英语 variable 于十五世纪经古法语进入，早期多用作形容词，指不恒定的事物、人或命运。

items.en: From the seventeenth century onward mathematics used variable as a noun for a quantity that may take different values. Statistics and computing later extended the noun to features and to named storage.
items.cn: 自十七世纪起，数学把 variable 用作名词，指可取不同值的量；统计学与计算机科学后来把这一名词扩展到特征与具名存储。

note.en: The first group separates the adjective from related nouns and from its direct opposite. The second holds near-synonyms that describe change in different ways.
note.cn: 第一组区分该形容词与相关名词及其直接反义词；第二组是以不同方式描述变化的近义词。

entries.definition: The noun for how much something varies. It is a quantity or degree, whereas variable names the thing that varies.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，指某物变化幅度有多大；它是个数量或程度，而 variable 命名的是会变的那个东西。

entries.definition: Means 'several different kinds of'. It counts types and never means 'changeable over time'.
entries.definitionCN: 意为「好几种不同的」；它数的是种类，从不表示「随时间变化」。

entries.definition: Means 'never changing'. It is the direct negation, used for constants, habits and rules without exceptions.
entries.definitionCN: 意为「从不改变的」，是直接否定形式，用于常量、习惯与无例外的规则。

entries.definition: Able or likely to change. It is the everyday equivalent of the first sense and says nothing technical.
entries.definitionCN: 能够或容易改变的；是第 1 个义项的日常说法，不含技术含义。

entries.definition: Moving up and down irregularly. It describes a pattern over time rather than a capacity to differ.
entries.definitionCN: 不规则地上下波动；描述的是随时间呈现的形态，而不是产生差异的能力。

entries.definition: Changing often, especially in loyalty or affection. It is literary and personal, not statistical.
entries.definitionCN: 常变的，尤指忠诚或情感；属文学与个人语境，不用于统计。

entries.definition: Likely to move, fail or fall. It is stronger and more alarming than variable, which merely reports difference.
entries.definitionCN: 容易移动、失效或倒下；比 variable 更强、更令人警觉，因为 variable 只是报告存在差异。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: varius 'varied' + -able: able to vary, and so a quantity that varies.
normal.cn: varius「多样的」+ -able：能够变化的，因而是会变的量。

normal.en: The family runs vary, variable, variability, variation, variance, variant, various, variety.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 vary、variable、variability、variation、variance、variant、various、variety。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the use: dependent variable, independent variable, random variable, variable cost.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出用法：因变量、自变量、随机变量、可变成本。

normal.en: The opposite in mathematics is constant; in business it is fixed cost.
normal.cn: 数学中的反义是 constant，商业中的反义是 fixed cost。

normal.en: A variable is a named slot; its value may change while the name stays.
normal.cn: 变量是一个具名的槽；值可变，名字不变。

abstract.en: Picture a dial that refuses to settle, and a hand writing down each position.
abstract.cn: 想象一个不肯停稳的转盘，一只手把每个位置都记下来。

abstract.en: Picture a box labelled with a name but holding a different number each morning.
abstract.cn: 想象一只贴着名字的盒子，每天早上装的数字都不同。

abstract.en: Picture two plants of one species, one tall and one short, both healthy.
abstract.cn: 想象同一物种的两株植物，一高一矮，却都健康。

examples.en: The researcher changed one variable at a time.
examples.cn: 研究者每次只改变一个变量。

examples.en: Results were variable, so the trial was repeated.
examples.cn: 结果不稳定，因此试验被重复了一次。

examples.en: Rainfall in the region is highly variable from year to year.
examples.cn: 该地区的降水年际变化很大。

dict_mnemonic.text: vary（变化）+ able（能……的）→ 能变化的 → 易变的；可变因素（变量）

root: 拉丁 varius「多样的、有斑点的」（来源不确定）→ variare「变化」→ variabilis「可变的」→ 英语 variable。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all concern something that can take different values or states: weather, an algebraic symbol, an experimental factor, uneven performance, a program slot, a rich species, a measured trait and a cost that moves with output.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都涉及可取不同值或状态的事物：天气、代数符号、实验因素、不稳的表现、程序槽位、变异丰富的物种、被测量的特征，以及随产量起伏的成本。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a needle that will not settle on one number.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根不肯停在同一数字上的指针。

branches.en: CHANGE AS A PROPERTY: weather shifts, and human performance refuses to repeat.
branches.cn: 变化作为性质：天气会变，人的表现也不肯重复。

branches.en: THE SYMBOL: mathematics turns the property into a letter that stands for any value.
branches.cn: 符号：数学把这种性质变成一个可代表任意值的字母。

branches.en: THE MEASURED FACTOR: experiments and statistics name the feature they move or record.
branches.cn: 被测量的因素：实验与统计学为它们改变或记录的特征命名。

branches.en: THE NAMED SLOT: computing gives the variable a memory address and a fixed name.
branches.cn: 具名槽位：计算机给变量一个内存地址和一个固定名字。

branches.en: NATURAL AND FINANCIAL SPREAD: a variable species is rich, and a variable cost rises with output.
branches.cn: 自然与财务上的变动：variable 的物种遗传丰富，variable cost 随产量上升。

intro.en: Variable is a Latin adjective of change with the suffix -able: a root meaning 'varied', a suffix of possibility, and later a noun use.
intro.cn: variable 是拉丁语中表示变化的形容词加 -able：一个意为「多样」的词根、一个表示可能的后缀，后来又有了名词用法。

latinIntro.en: Latin varius and variare supply vary, variable, variability, variation, variance, variant, various and variety. The same root also gives the mathematical variable and the everyday 'variable weather'.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 varius 与 variare 衍生 vary、variable、variability、variation、variance、variant、various、variety；同一词根也给出数学变量与日常的「多变天气」。

items.example: The variable was measured every ten minutes.
items.exampleCN: 该变量每十分钟测量一次。

items.example: Variability rose after the storm.
items.exampleCN: 暴风雨之后波动增大了。

items.example: Prices vary by season.
items.exampleCN: 价格随季节而变。

items.example: The variation between the two prints is slight.
items.exampleCN: 两幅印品之间的差异很小。

items.example: Variance measures squared distance from the mean.
items.exampleCN: 方差衡量的是与均值之差的平方。

items.example: The southern variant is easier to read.
items.exampleCN: 南方的变体更容易读。

items.example: His answer was invariable.
items.exampleCN: 他的回答一成不变。

items.example: The term has been variously defined.
items.exampleCN: 这个术语有过几种不同的定义。

definition_zh: 解剖学；身体结构；解剖；剖析
definition_en: the scientific study of the structure of bodies, or the structure of a body or system itself
core_image: 一具被细心分层的躯干示意图，肌肉、血管与骨骼逐层揭开
scene: Anatomy students spend the first term learning every bone of the hand.
sceneCN: 这里 anatomy 指「解剖学」（第 1 个义项：研究生物体结构的学科）；句意：解剖学学生第一学期要学完手部每一块骨头。图中可辨识物件：分层人体图、手部骨骼标本、标注签。

pos.zh: 解剖学；身体结构；解剖（行为）；剖析（可数时指某生物或某系统的结构）

forms.label: 复数
forms.form: anatomies（指多具身体结构或多种解剖体系）

derivatives.zh: 原子（同出希腊 temnein「切」，但前缀相反，见 similar）

senses.title: The Science of Structure
senses.titleCN: 解剖学：研究身体结构的学科
senses.definition: the scientific study of the structure of living bodies
senses.definitionCN: 研究生物体结构的科学
senses.example: Anatomy students spend the first term learning every bone of the hand.
senses.exampleCN: 解剖学学生第一学期要学完手部每一块骨头。
senses.why: Greek ana- meant 'up, throughout' and temnein meant 'to cut'. Anatomē was a cutting-up, and the name of the act became the name of the science that performs it.
senses.whyCN: 希腊前缀 ana- 意为「向上、遍及」，temnein 意为「切」。anatomē 就是「切开」，这个动作的名称后来变成了从事该动作的学科名称。

senses.title: Body Structure Itself
senses.titleCN: 身体结构：部件如何安排
senses.definition: the actual structure of a body, its parts and their arrangement
senses.definitionCN: 身体实际的结构、各部分及其排列
senses.example: The dolphin's anatomy shows that its flipper is a modified arm.
senses.exampleCN: 海豚的身体结构表明，它的鳍肢是改造过的手臂。
senses.why: The same noun names the object as well as the study. When a biologist says 'the anatomy of the dolphin', the cutting has become a description of what was found.
senses.whyCN: 同一个名词既指学科也指对象；当生物学家说 the anatomy of the dolphin 时，「切」已经变成了对所见之物的描述。

senses.title: The Act of Dissection
senses.titleCN: 解剖：切开并分离的动作
senses.definition: the act or practice of cutting a body apart to study it
senses.definitionCN: 为研究而把身体切开的动作或做法
senses.example: The anatomy of the specimen took the whole afternoon.
senses.exampleCN: 对这份标本的解剖花了一整个下午。
senses.why: This is the oldest sense: the physical cutting. Modern laboratories may use imaging instead, but the word still remembers the knife.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的义项：实际的切割。现代实验室可能改用成像技术，但这个词仍记得那把刀。

senses.title: Detailed Analysis
senses.titleCN: 剖析：把一个整体拆开来看
senses.definition: a detailed examination of the parts of a thing or idea
senses.definitionCN: 对事物或观念的各个部分所作的细致检查
senses.example: The book is an anatomy of how rumours spread.
senses.exampleCN: 这本书是对谣言如何传播的一次剖析。
senses.why: The metaphor is exact: to understand a whole, take it apart part by part. Analysts therefore borrow the anatomist's word for structures that are not biological.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻非常贴切：要理解一个整体，就把它一部分一部分拆开。因此分析者借解剖学家的词，用于并非生物的结构。

senses.title: The Human Body
senses.titleCN: 人体：整个身体（口语）
senses.definition: the human body, especially in informal or humorous use
senses.definitionCN: 人的身体，尤用于口语或戏谑
senses.example: He fell and bruised his entire anatomy.
senses.exampleCN: 他摔了一跤，全身都碰伤了。
senses.why: Because anatomy studies the body, the noun can stand for the body itself. The tone is usually light, as if the speaker were looking at the body from outside.
senses.whyCN: 因为解剖学研究身体，这个名词可以代指身体本身；语气通常轻松，仿佛说话者从外部打量这具身体。

senses.title: Plant and Animal Structure
senses.titleCN: 动植物结构：非人体的解剖
senses.definition: the structure of plants or animals studied as a field
senses.definitionCN: 作为研究领域的植物或动物结构
senses.example: Plant anatomy explains why stems bend toward light.
senses.exampleCN: 植物解剖学解释了茎为何向光弯曲。
senses.why: The science is not limited to people. Comparative anatomy compares species, and plant anatomy studies tissues; the same cutting-up logic applies.
senses.whyCN: 这门科学并不限于人。比较解剖学比较各物种，植物解剖学研究组织；「切开来看」的逻辑是一样的。

senses.title: Structure of an Institution
senses.titleCN: 机构的结构：组织如何构成
senses.definition: the internal structure and working parts of an organization or system
senses.definitionCN: 组织或系统的内部结构与运作部件
senses.example: The report examined the anatomy of the health service.
senses.exampleCN: 该报告考察了医疗服务体系的结构。
senses.why: Institutions have parts that can be mapped like organs. The word implies that the parts are interdependent, so a change in one shows up elsewhere.
senses.whyCN: 机构有可以像器官一样被描绘的部件；这个词暗示各部件相互依赖，因此改一处就会在别处显现。

senses.title: The Anatomy Course
senses.titleCN: 解剖学课程：作为科目的解剖
senses.definition: the subject or course taught under this name
senses.definitionCN: 以解剖学为名讲授的科目或课程
senses.example: She passed anatomy but failed physiology.
senses.exampleCN: 她解剖学通过了，生理学却没过。
senses.why: In medical schools the science becomes a subject with exams. Names of disciplines often work this way: biology is both a field and a class at nine o'clock.
senses.whyCN: 在医学院，这门科学变成有考试的科目。学科名称常如此运作：biology 既是研究领域，也是九点钟的那堂课。

intro.en: Anatomy comes from Greek anatomē 'a cutting up', from ana- 'up, throughout' and temnein 'to cut'. Latin borrowed it as anatomia, and English took it in the sixteenth century; the exact date is approximate.
intro.cn: anatomy 出自希腊 anatomē「切开」，由 ana-「向上、遍及」与 temnein「切」构成。拉丁语借作 anatomia，英语于十六世纪引入；确切年代为约数。

items.en: Temnein meant 'to cut'. From it came tomos 'a cut' and the adjective -tomos, which survives in English compounds such as appendectomy and lobotomy.
items.cn: temnein 意为「切」，由此产生 tomos「切口」与形容词 -tomos；后者在英语复合词中留存，如 appendectomy（阑尾切除术）、lobotomy（脑叶切断术）。

items.en: The same root produced atomos, 'uncuttable', from a- 'not' plus tomos. Democritus used it for the smallest indivisible piece of matter. Anatomy and atom are therefore opposites built from one verb: one cuts up, the other cannot be cut.
items.cn: 同一词根产生 atomos「不可切的」，由 a-「不」加 tomos 构成；德谟克利特用它指不可再分的最小物质。因此 anatomy 与 atom 是由同一个动词造出的反义对：一个切开，一个不可切。

items.en: Anatomē meant 'a cutting up, dissection'. Greek medicine used it for the procedure of opening a body to learn its parts, not for the parts themselves.
items.cn: anatomē 意为「切开、解剖」。希腊医学用它指打开身体以了解其部件的操作，而不是指部件本身。

items.en: Latin anatomia kept both the act and the science. Medieval and Renaissance anatomists added the sense 'the structure so revealed', which English inherited.
items.cn: 拉丁 anatomia 同时保留行为与学科两义；中世纪与文艺复兴时期的解剖学家又添上「由此揭示的结构」这一含义，英语继承了它。

items.en: From the seventeenth century English extended anatomy to the parts of anything, from a poem to a government. The metaphor survives because every whole can be taken apart.
items.cn: 自十七世纪起，英语把 anatomy 扩展到任何事物的部件，从一首诗到一个政府。这个比喻之所以存活，是因为任何整体都可以拆开。

note.en: The first group separates members of the Greek cutting family that look alike. The second holds near-synonyms for study, body and analysis.
note.cn: 第一组区分希腊「切」词族中形近的成员；第二组是表示研究、身体与分析的近义词。

entries.definition: The smallest unit of an element, named by Greek atomos 'uncuttable'. It is the exact opposite prefix to anatomy, which is about cutting up.
entries.definitionCN: 元素的最小单位，名称来自希腊 atomos「不可切的」；它的前缀恰与 anatomy「切开」相反。

entries.definition: Relating to anatomy or to body structure. It modifies nouns such as structure, position and model.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，指与解剖学或身体结构有关的；修饰 structure、position、model 等名词。

entries.definition: A person who studies or practises anatomy. It names the human agent, not the field.
entries.definitionCN: 研究或从事解剖的人；命名的是人，而非领域。

entries.definition: The act of cutting something apart for study. It is the procedure, while anatomy can also be the science or the structure.
entries.definitionCN: 为研究而切开某物的行为；它是操作过程，而 anatomy 还可指学科或结构。

entries.definition: The study of how body parts work. Anatomy asks what the parts are; physiology asks what they do.
entries.definitionCN: 研究身体部件如何运作的学科；anatomy 问部件是什么，physiology 问它们做什么。

entries.definition: The study of form, especially in biology and linguistics. It is broader than anatomy and does not imply dissection.
entries.definitionCN: 研究形式的学科，尤用于生物学与语言学；比 anatomy 更宽，且不暗示解剖。

entries.definition: The way parts are put together. It is the neutral word; anatomy adds the biological or systematic flavour.
entries.definitionCN: 各部分的组合方式；是中性词，而 anatomy 增添了生物学或系统性的色彩。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: ana- 'up, throughout' + temnein 'cut' + -y: the cutting-up that reveals structure.
normal.cn: ana-「向上、遍及」+ temnein「切」+ -y：揭示结构的切开。

normal.en: The family runs anatomical, anatomically, anatomist, anatomize, and the -tomy words such as appendectomy.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 anatomical、anatomically、anatomist、anatomize，以及 appendectomy 一类 -tomy 词。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the use: human anatomy, comparative anatomy, plant anatomy, gross anatomy.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出用法：人体解剖学、比较解剖学、植物解剖学、大体解剖学。

normal.en: atom is the same root with the opposite prefix: 'not cuttable' against 'cut up'.
normal.cn: atom 是同一词根加相反前缀：不可切，对比切开。

normal.en: anatomy asks what the parts are; physiology asks what they do.
normal.cn: anatomy 问部件是什么，physiology 问部件做什么。

abstract.en: Picture a watch opened on a table, every wheel laid out in order.
abstract.cn: 想象一只表在桌上被打开，每个齿轮都按顺序摆好。

abstract.en: Picture a map of a city printed as layers: roads, pipes, then power lines.
abstract.cn: 想象一张城市地图分层印出：先是道路，再是管道，然后是电线。

abstract.en: Picture a sentence taken apart word by word to see how it holds together.
abstract.cn: 想象一个句子被逐词拆开，以看清它如何组合。

examples.en: Human anatomy has changed little since the Renaissance.
examples.cn: 自文艺复兴以来，人体解剖学变化不大。

examples.en: The anatomy of a frog is often taught before that of a mammal.
examples.cn: 教学上常先讲青蛙的解剖结构，再讲哺乳动物。

examples.en: Her paper offers an anatomy of the failure rather than a remedy.
examples.cn: 她的论文对这次失败作了剖析，而没有给出补救办法。

dict_mnemonic.text: ana（向上、分开）+ tomy（切）→ 分开切开来研究 → 解剖学；身体结构

root: 希腊 ana-「向上、遍及」+ temnein「切」→ anatomē「切开、解剖」→ 拉丁 anatomia → 英语 anatomy；同根 atom 意为「不可切的」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one act of cutting: the science, the structure revealed, the cutting itself, metaphorical analysis, the body in speech, plant and animal bodies, institutional structure and the school subject.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都沿着「切开」这一动作展开：学科、被揭示的结构、切割本身、比喻性的剖析、口语中的身体、动植物身体、机构结构与学校科目。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a body opened layer by layer, each part labelled.
core.cn: 核心意象：一具被逐层打开、每个部件都带标签的身体。

branches.en: THE ACT AND THE SCIENCE: the physical cutting and the discipline that grew from it.
branches.cn: 动作与学科：实际的切割，以及由它生长出来的学科。

branches.en: WHAT THE CUT REVEALS: human, animal and plant bodies are described part by part.
branches.cn: 切开后所见：人、动物与植物的身体被逐部件描述。

branches.en: THE METAPHOR: books, rumours and institutions can be taken apart the same way.
branches.cn: 比喻延伸：书籍、谣言与机构也能以同样方式拆解。

branches.en: THE BODY IN SPEECH: informal use lets the noun stand for the whole body.
branches.cn: 口语中的身体：非正式用法让该名词代指整个身体。

branches.en: THE SUBJECT: in medical schools the science becomes a course with examinations.
branches.cn: 科目：在医学院，这门科学变成有考试的课程。

intro.en: Anatomy is a Greek compound: a prefix of opening, the verb 'to cut', and a noun ending. English also uses the combining form -tomy for surgical cuttings.
intro.cn: anatomy 是希腊语复合词：表示打开的动词前缀、动词「切」，以及名词词尾。英语还用构词成分 -tomy 表示外科切开。

latinIntro.en: Latin anatomia came from Greek anatomē. The Latinized form supplies anatomy, anatomical, anatomist and anatomize; the Greek root tom- supplies appendectomy, tonsillectomy and lobotomy.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 anatomia 来自希腊 anatomē；拉丁化形式衍生 anatomy、anatomical、anatomist、anatomize；希腊词根 tom- 衍生 appendectomy、tonsillectomy、lobotomy。

items.meaning: a cutting up; the structure revealed
items.example: The anatomy of the insect was drawn in detail.
items.exampleCN: 这只昆虫的解剖结构被详细绘制。

items.example: The anatomical model comes apart in twelve pieces.
items.exampleCN: 这个解剖模型可拆成十二块。

items.example: The two joints are anatomically identical.
items.exampleCN: 这两个关节在结构上完全相同。

items.example: The anatomist named the muscle in 1840.
items.exampleCN: 这位解剖学家在 1840 年给该肌肉命名。

items.meaning: to dissect or analyse in detail
items.example: He anatomized the argument line by line.
items.exampleCN: 他逐行剖析了这场论证。

items.example: An atom of carbon has six protons.
items.exampleCN: 一个碳原子有六个质子。

items.structure: tomos (a cut, a slice) + English form
items.meaning: a large book, a 'slice' of writing
items.example: The library owns a rare tome on beetles.
items.exampleCN: 图书馆藏有一部罕见的甲虫专著。

items.meaning: a cutting short; a perfect summary
items.example: The small town is the epitome of quiet.
items.exampleCN: 这个小镇是宁静的缩影。

latinEntries.meaning: dissection; the science of the body

latinEntries.structure: atomus, -i (f. or m., Greek loan in Latin)

definition_zh: 解剖学的；身体结构的；结构上的
definition_en: relating to anatomy or to the structure of a body
core_image: 一张人体挂图上每块肌肉都被编号，线条标出它们之间的位置关系
scene: The anatomical model comes apart in twelve layers, from skin to bone.
sceneCN: 这里 anatomical 指「解剖用的」（第 4 个义项：用于展示或研究身体结构的标本与模型）；句意：这个解剖模型可以拆成十二层，从皮肤到骨骼。图中可辨识物件：分层人体模型、编号标签、骨骼支架。

pos.zh: 解剖学的；身体结构的；结构上的（由 anatomy 加 -ical 构成，常修饰 model、structure、position 等）

senses.title: Of the Science
senses.titleCN: 解剖学的：属于这门学科
senses.definition: belonging to the science of anatomy
senses.definitionCN: 属于解剖学这门学科的
senses.example: The anatomical literature on the wrist is enormous.
senses.exampleCN: 关于腕部的解剖学文献浩如烟海。
senses.why: The adjective attaches the noun to the discipline. In this sense it sits beside histological, physiological and embryological as labels of research fields.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词把名词挂到学科上；在这一义项里，它与 histological、physiological、embryological 并列，都是研究领域的标签。

senses.title: Of Body Structure
senses.titleCN: 身体结构的：讲部件怎么长
senses.definition: relating to the actual structure of a body
senses.definitionCN: 与身体实际结构有关的
senses.example: The anatomical difference between the two species is small.
senses.exampleCN: 这两个物种在身体结构上的差异很小。
senses.why: Here the reference is to parts and their arrangement, not to books about them. A difference is anatomical when it lies in structure rather than in behaviour or chemistry.
senses.whyCN: 这里指的是部件及其排列，而不是关于它们的书籍。当差异存在于结构而非行为或化学时，就说它是 anatomical 的差异。

senses.title: Structural, by Metaphor
senses.titleCN: 结构上的：用于非生物对象
senses.definition: relating to the internal structure of a non-biological thing
senses.definitionCN: 与非生物事物的内部结构有关
senses.example: The anatomical weaknesses of the treaty were obvious.
senses.exampleCN: 该条约在结构上的弱点显而易见。
senses.why: The metaphor treats an institution as a body with joints. It is looser than the biological sense and often signals that a failure lies in design, not in execution.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻把机构当作有骨架的身体；它比生物学义更宽松，常暗示问题出在设计而非执行。

senses.title: For Display or Study
senses.titleCN: 解剖用的：模型与标本
senses.definition: made to show or study body structure
senses.definitionCN: 为展示或研究身体结构而制作的
senses.example: The anatomical model comes apart in twelve layers, from skin to bone.
senses.exampleCN: 这个解剖模型可以拆成十二层，从皮肤到骨骼。
senses.why: Objects as well as ideas can be anatomical: a model, a chart, a plate. The word then labels the purpose of the object, not a branch of knowledge.
senses.whyCN: 物体也能是 anatomical 的：模型、挂图、图版。此时这个词标出的是该物件的用途，而不是知识分支。

senses.title: Standard Reference Position
senses.titleCN: 解剖学姿势的：标准化方位
senses.definition: relating to the standard position used to describe body parts
senses.definitionCN: 与描述身体部件时所用的标准姿势有关
senses.example: In the anatomical position the palms face forward.
senses.exampleCN: 在解剖学姿势中，手掌朝前。
senses.why: Description needs a fixed frame, or 'left' and 'right' mean nothing. The adjective marks that frame, which is a convention rather than a fact of the body.
senses.whyCN: 描述需要一个固定参照，否则「左」「右」毫无意义；这个形容词标出的正是那一参照，它是约定而非身体的事实。

senses.title: Recognizable in Structure
senses.titleCN: 解剖上可辨识的：结构上找得到
senses.definition: identifiable by its structure when examined
senses.definitionCN: 检查时能凭结构辨认出来的
senses.example: The tumour was anatomically distinct from the surrounding tissue.
senses.exampleCN: 该肿瘤在结构上与周围组织明显不同。
senses.why: Surgeons and radiologists ask whether a thing can be told apart by its parts. Anatomically distinct means the difference is visible in structure, before any chemical test.
senses.whyCN: 外科医生与放射科医生要问：某物能否凭其部件被区分开来。anatomically distinct 意为差异在结构上就可见，无需等到化学检验。

senses.title: Of the Anatomy Course
senses.titleCN: 解剖课的：课程与教学
senses.definition: belonging to the teaching of anatomy
senses.definitionCN: 属于解剖学教学的
senses.example: The anatomical drawings were hung in the dissection room.
senses.exampleCN: 解剖图挂在解剖室里。
senses.why: Teaching produces its own vocabulary and objects. In this sense the adjective points to the classroom and its materials rather than to research.
senses.whyCN: 教学会产出自己的词汇与物件；在这一义项里，这个形容词指向课堂及其教材，而不是科研。

senses.title: Analytic, Part by Part
senses.titleCN: 结构分析的：逐部件拆解
senses.definition: treating a subject by separating its parts
senses.definitionCN: 把对象按部件分开处理
senses.example: The critic offered an anatomical reading of the novel.
senses.exampleCN: 这位批评家对小说作了结构解剖式的解读。
senses.why: This is the adjective of the metaphorical noun: an analysis that names each part and its function. It is more formal than 'structural' and more vivid than 'detailed'.
senses.whyCN: 这是比喻义名词的形容词形式：一种逐一点明每个部件及其作用的分析。它比 structural 更正式，比 detailed 更生动。

intro.en: Anatomical is anatomy plus -ical. Anatomy comes from Greek anatomē 'a cutting up', from ana- 'up, throughout' and temnein 'to cut'. The English adjective is dated only approximately.
intro.cn: anatomical 是 anatomy 加 -ical。anatomy 出自希腊 anatomē「切开」，由 ana-「向上、遍及」与 temnein「切」构成。英语形容词的年代仅为约数。

items.en: Temnein 'to cut' gave the noun tomos 'a cut piece' and the suffix -tomos. English keeps that suffix in surgical names such as appendectomy and lobotomy.
items.cn: temnein「切」给出名词 tomos「切下的一片」与后缀 -tomos；英语在外科名称中保留该后缀，如 appendectomy、lobotomy。

items.en: Anatomē meant the act of cutting up a body. Greek medicine used the word for dissection, and the study of parts grew around that practice.
items.cn: anatomē 指把身体切开的动作；希腊医学用这个词表示解剖，而关于部件的研究正是围绕这一实践发展起来的。

items.en: Latin anatomia carried both the procedure and the knowledge gained. Medieval Latin writers also used it for a written summary of body parts.
items.cn: 拉丁 anatomia 兼指操作过程与所获知识；中世纪拉丁作者也用它指关于身体部件的书面概述。

items.en: English anatomy appears in the sixteenth century, and the adjective anatomical followed in the same period or shortly after. The exact first citation of the adjective is uncertain.
items.cn: 英语 anatomy 于十六世纪出现，形容词 anatomical 在同一时期或稍后跟上。该形容词的确切首见书证不确定。

items.en: Medicine fixed phrases such as anatomical position, anatomical variation and gross anatomical features. Each borrows the adjective to mark a standard frame or a level of observation.
items.cn: 医学固定了 anatomical position（解剖学姿势）、anatomical variation（解剖变异）、gross anatomical features（大体解剖特征）等说法；每个都借这个形容词标出标准参照或观察层次。

note.en: The first group separates the adjective from its noun and from its adverb. The second holds near-synonyms that describe structure at different levels.
note.cn: 第一组区分该形容词与其名词、副词；第二组是描述不同层次结构的近义词。

entries.definition: The field, the structure or the act of dissection. It is what the adjective describes, so the two never occupy the same slot in a sentence.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，指学科、结构或解剖行为；它是该形容词所描述的对象，因此两者在句中不会占据同一位置。

entries.definition: Means 'in terms of body structure'. It modifies verbs and adjectives, as in anatomically correct or anatomically distinct.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，意为「在身体结构方面」；修饰动词与形容词，如 anatomically correct、anatomically distinct。

entries.definition: A person who studies anatomy. It never replaces the adjective before a noun.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，指研究解剖学的人；它不能替代名词前的形容词。

entries.definition: Relating to structure of any kind, biological or not. It is the broader and safer word where no body is involved.
entries.definitionCN: 与任何结构有关，无论是否生物；在不涉及身体时，它更宽泛也更稳妥。

entries.definition: Relating to form and shape, especially in biology and linguistics. It stresses outward form rather than internal arrangement.
entries.definitionCN: 与形式和外形有关，尤用于生物学与语言学；强调外部形态，而非内部排列。

entries.definition: Relating to the microscopic study of tissues. It is a level below gross anatomy, so it is not a synonym.
entries.definitionCN: 与组织的显微研究有关；它比大体解剖低一个层次，因此并非同义词。

entries.definition: Relating to how the body works. It contrasts with anatomical, which concerns what the parts are and where they sit.
entries.definitionCN: 与身体如何运作有关；它与 anatomical 相对，后者关心部件是什么、位于何处。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: anatomy + -ical: belonging to the cutting-up science or to the structure it reveals.
normal.cn: anatomy + -ical：属于「切开之学」，或属于它揭示的结构。

normal.en: The family runs anatomy, anatomical, anatomically, anatomist, anatomize.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 anatomy、anatomical、anatomically、anatomist、anatomize。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the use: anatomical structure, anatomical position, anatomical model, anatomical variation.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出用法：解剖结构、解剖学姿势、解剖模型、解剖变异。

normal.en: anatomical is about parts; physiological is about functions.
normal.cn: anatomical 讲部件，physiological 讲功能。

normal.en: atom carries the same root with a negative prefix: not cuttable, against cut up.
normal.cn: atom 是同一词根加否定前缀：不可切，与切开相对。

abstract.en: Picture a numbered diagram where every line points to one small part.
abstract.cn: 想象一张编号示意图，每条引线都指向一个小部件。

abstract.en: Picture a machine manual that begins by naming every screw before explaining what it does.
abstract.cn: 想象一本机器手册，先给每颗螺丝命名，再解释它的作用。

abstract.en: Picture two animals that look alike until you compare their skeletons.
abstract.cn: 想象两只动物外表相似，直到比较骨架才发现不同。

examples.en: The two species differ in anatomical detail but not in behaviour.
examples.cn: 这两个物种在解剖细节上不同，行为上却没有差别。

examples.en: The surgeon studied the anatomical charts before the operation.
examples.cn: 手术前外科医生仔细看了解剖图。

examples.en: An anatomically modern skeleton was found in the cave.
examples.cn: 洞穴中发现了一具结构上属于现代人的骨架。

dict_mnemonic.text: anatomy（解剖）+ ical（……的）→ 解剖学的、身体结构的

root: 希腊 ana-「向上、遍及」+ temnein「切」→ anatomē「切开」→ 拉丁 anatomia → 英语 anatomy → anatomical。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses attach the adjective to different things: a science, a body's parts, a non-biological structure, a teaching model, a standard position, a visible difference, a course and a method of analysis.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项把这个形容词挂到不同对象上：一门学科、身体的部件、非生物结构、教学模型、标准姿势、可见差异、课程与分析方式。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a labelled chart where every line points to one part of a body.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张带标签的图，每条引线都指向身体的一个部件。

branches.en: THE DISCIPLINE AND ITS TEACHING: the adjective marks research literature and classroom materials alike.
branches.cn: 学科及其教学：这个形容词既可标出研究文献，也可标出课堂教材。

branches.en: STRUCTURE MADE VISIBLE: parts and their arrangement, including differences that can be seen before any test.
branches.cn: 可见的结构：部件及其排列，包括无需检验就能看出的差异。

branches.en: THE METAPHOR: institutions and texts can be treated as bodies to be taken apart.
branches.cn: 比喻：机构与文本都可被当作身体来拆解。

branches.en: THE OBJECT: a model or chart is anatomical because of the use it serves.
branches.cn: 物件：模型或挂图之所以是 anatomical 的，是因为它服务的用途。

branches.en: THE CONVENTION: a standard position makes left and right describable at all.
branches.cn: 约定：标准姿势才使「左」「右」变得可以描述。

intro.en: Anatomical is a Greek compound with an English adjective ending: a prefix of opening, the verb 'to cut', the noun -y, and the adjective suffix -ical.
intro.cn: anatomical 是希腊复合词加英语形容词词尾：表示打开的前缀、动词「切」、名词词尾 -y，以及形容词后缀 -ical。

latinIntro.en: Latin anatomia supplies anatomy, anatomical, anatomically, anatomist and anatomize. The Greek root tom- also yields atom, tome, epitome and the surgical -ectomy names.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 anatomia 衍生 anatomy、anatomical、anatomically、anatomist、anatomize；希腊词根 tom- 还给出 atom、tome、epitome 以及外科的 -ectomy 类名称。

items.example: The anatomist corrected the older drawing.
items.exampleCN: 这位解剖学家修正了那幅旧图。

items.example: She anatomized the contract clause by clause.
items.exampleCN: 她把合同逐条剖析了一遍。

items.example: The word atom once meant 'uncuttable'.
items.exampleCN: atom 一词原意是「不可切的」。

items.example: A single tome filled the shelf.
items.exampleCN: 一卷书就占满了书架。

items.meaning: a cutting short; a perfect example
items.example: The village is the epitome of calm.
items.exampleCN: 这个村庄是宁静的典型。

definition_zh: 生物；有机体；生物体；（社会或组织的）有机整体
definition_en: an individual living thing, or a whole whose parts work together like those of a living body
core_image: 一个由许多器官协同工作的完整生命体，每个部件都为整体服务
scene: A single organism can contain more cells than there are people in the city.
sceneCN: 这里 organism 指「生物」（第 1 个义项：独立存活的个体生命）；句意：一个生物体内的细胞数可能超过这座城市的人口。图中可辨识物件：示意的细胞群、器官剖面、放大镜。

pos.zh: 生物；有机体；生物体；（比喻）有机整体、组织体

senses.title: An Individual Living Thing
senses.titleCN: 生物：独立存活的个体
senses.definition: a single living thing, such as an animal, plant or bacterium
senses.definitionCN: 单个活物，如动物、植物或细菌
senses.example: A single organism can contain more cells than there are people in the city.
senses.exampleCN: 一个生物体内的细胞数可能超过这座城市的人口。
senses.why: Greek organon meant 'tool, instrument'. An organism is a body whose parts work as instruments for the whole, which is why the word stresses organized cooperation rather than mere life.
senses.whyCN: 希腊 organon 意为「工具、器具」；organism 是各部件作为整体之工具而协同工作的身体，因此这个词强调有组织的协作，而不只是「活着」。

senses.title: Microscopic Life
senses.titleCN: 微生物：肉眼难见的个体
senses.definition: a microscopic living thing, especially a bacterium or fungus
senses.definitionCN: 微小的活物，尤指细菌或真菌
senses.example: The water contained several harmful organisms.
senses.exampleCN: 水中含有几种有害微生物。
senses.why: In hygiene and medicine the word usually points to things too small to see. The size is not part of the definition, but the context supplies it.
senses.whyCN: 在卫生与医学语境里，这个词通常指小到看不见的东西；大小并不属于定义，而是由语境补上的。

senses.title: A Social Whole
senses.titleCN: 有机整体：社会或组织的比喻
senses.definition: a society or organization treated as a body whose parts depend on one another
senses.definitionCN: 被看作相互依存之身体的社会或组织
senses.example: Some nineteenth-century writers called society a living organism.
senses.exampleCN: 一些十九世纪的作家把社会称为活的有机体。
senses.why: The metaphor claims that institutions are not assembled machines but growing bodies. It has been used both to justify reform and to argue that parts cannot be replaced at will.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻主张制度不是拼装的机器，而是生长出来的身体；它既被用来支持改革，也被用来论证各部分不能随意替换。

senses.title: Engineered Life
senses.titleCN: 改造过的生物：转基因个体
senses.definition: a living thing whose genetic material has been deliberately altered
senses.definitionCN: 遗传物质被人为改动的活物
senses.example: Regulations cover any genetically modified organism sold as food.
senses.exampleCN: 法规涵盖任何作为食品出售的转基因生物。
senses.why: Modern biotechnology made the word a legal category. The organism is still an individual living thing; only its genes have been edited, which is why the modifier carries the weight.
senses.whyCN: 现代生物技术把这个词变成法律类别；该生物仍是独立活物，只是基因被编辑过，因此分量落在修饰语上。

senses.title: Model Organism
senses.titleCN: 模式生物：用于研究的代表
senses.definition: a species studied in the laboratory to understand general biological processes
senses.definitionCN: 在实验室中研究、以理解一般生物过程的物种
senses.example: The fruit fly became the model organism for genetics.
senses.exampleCN: 果蝇成了遗传学的模式生物。
senses.why: Research needs a stand-in that is easy to keep and well understood. The word marks the individual, while the phrase marks its representative role.
senses.whyCN: 研究需要一个易饲养、已被充分理解的替身；这个词标出的是个体，而短语标出的是它的代表角色。

senses.title: An Ecological Unit
senses.titleCN: 生态个体：生态学中的计数单位
senses.definition: an individual counted as a unit in an ecological study
senses.definitionCN: 生态研究中作为一个单位来计数的个体
senses.example: The survey counted every organism larger than a millimetre.
senses.exampleCN: 该调查统计了每一个大于一毫米的生物个体。
senses.why: Ecology counts individuals to estimate populations. Here the word is almost a unit of measurement, defined by the size cut-off the researcher chooses.
senses.whyCN: 生态学通过数个体来估计种群；此时这个词几乎是一个计量单位，其边界由研究者选定的尺寸下限决定。

senses.title: An Organized Whole
senses.titleCN: 有机整体：哲学意义上的整体
senses.definition: a whole whose parts are mutually dependent and cannot be understood alone
senses.definitionCN: 各部分相互依赖、不能孤立理解的整体
senses.example: For the philosopher, the mind is an organism, not a machine.
senses.exampleCN: 在这位哲学家看来，心灵是有机整体，而不是机器。
senses.why: Philosophy uses the word against mechanism. If parts only make sense in the whole, explanation must begin with the whole, not with the smallest piece.
senses.whyCN: 哲学用这个词来反对机械论：如果部件只有在整体中才有意义，解释就必须从整体开始，而不是从最小零件开始。

senses.title: A Working Body
senses.titleCN: 运作中的组织体：机构如身体
senses.definition: an organization understood through the cooperation of its parts
senses.definitionCN: 通过各部分协作来理解的机构
senses.example: The department behaves like an organism with its own metabolism.
senses.exampleCN: 这个部门像一个有自己的代谢方式的有机体那样运作。
senses.why: Management writing borrows the biological image to talk about flow, feedback and adaptation. The claim is that removing one part changes the health of the rest.
senses.whyCN: 管理写作借生物学意象来谈流动、反馈与适应；其主张是：拿掉一个部件会改变其余部分的健康。

intro.en: Organism is a modern formation on Greek organon 'tool, instrument, organ', from ergon 'work'. It was coined in the nineteenth century; the exact coiner and first date are uncertain.
intro.cn: organism 是建立在希腊 organon「工具、器具、器官」之上的近代构词，而 organon 出自 ergon「工作」。该词于十九世纪被造出；确切的造词者与首见年代不确定。

items.en: Ergon meant 'work, deed'. Its Indo-European root also gives English work and the Greek adjective energetikos, source of energy.
items.cn: ergon 意为「工作、行动」，其印欧词根也给出英语 work，以及希腊形容词 energetikos——energy 的来源。

items.en: Organon meant 'a tool or instrument', and by extension an organ of the body, since an organ is the body's instrument for a task. Aristotle's logical works were called the Organon, the tool of reasoning.
items.cn: organon 意为「工具、器具」，引申指身体器官，因为器官就是身体完成某项任务的工具。亚里士多德的逻辑著作被称为 Organon，即推理的工具。

items.en: Latin organum kept the senses of instrument and, later, musical instrument and body organ. English organ and organize descend from this line.
items.cn: 拉丁 organum 保留「器具」义，后来又指乐器与身体器官；英语 organ 与 organize 都出自这条线索。

items.en: Organism was formed in the nineteenth century to name a living body as an organized whole. The exact coiner is uncertain; the word spread with biology and with the philosophy of organized wholes.
items.cn: organism 于十九世纪被造出，用来指作为有组织整体的活体。确切的造词者不确定；该词随生物学以及「有组织整体」的哲学而传播开来。

items.en: Social thinkers soon applied organism to societies and institutions. The metaphor was attractive because it explained interdependence, but it was also criticized for making change seem like mere growth.
items.cn: 社会思想家很快把 organism 用于社会与机构。这个比喻之所以有吸引力，是因为它能解释相互依存；但它也因让变革显得只是「生长」而受到批评。

note.en: The first group separates the noun from its adjective relatives and from organization. The second holds near-synonyms that name life at different scales.
note.cn: 第一组区分该名词与其形容词亲属以及 organization；第二组是不同尺度上指称生命的近义词。

entries.definition: Means 'of living things' or 'grown without chemicals'. It describes a quality, while organism names the living individual.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，意为「生物的」或「不用化学方式种植的」；它描述性质，而 organism 命名的是活的个体。

entries.definition: A structured group such as a company, or the act of arranging. It shares the organ root but names arrangement, not life.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，指公司一类有结构的人群，或安排的动作；它同出 organ 词根，但命名的是安排，而不是生命。

entries.definition: A body part with a specific function, or a musical instrument. It is the instrument that the organism as a whole uses.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，指有特定功能的身体部件，或指乐器；它是整个 organism 所使用的「工具」。

entries.definition: A living being, especially an animal. It is warmer and less technical than organism.
entries.definitionCN: 活物，尤指动物；比 organism 更有温度，技术性更弱。

entries.definition: A living entity, or existence itself. It is broader and vaguer, often used where organism would sound clinical.
entries.definitionCN: 活的存在者，或存在本身；更宽泛、更模糊，在 organism 显得过于临床的地方常用它。

entries.definition: A microscopic living thing. It is narrower than organism, which covers elephants as well as bacteria.
entries.definitionCN: 微小的活物；比 organism 狭窄，因为后者同样包括大象与细菌。

entries.definition: Any kind of living thing, often used when imagining life elsewhere. It stresses kind rather than individual.
entries.definitionCN: 任何种类的活物，常用于设想别处的生命；强调种类而非个体。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: organon 'tool' + -ism: a body whose organs are tools for the whole.
normal.cn: organon「工具」+ -ism：器官作为整体工具的身体。

normal.en: The family runs organ, organic, organism, organismal, organismic, organize, organization, organelle.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 organ、organic、organism、organismal、organismic、organize、organization、organelle。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the use: living organism, model organism, single-celled organism, genetically modified organism.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出用法：生物、模式生物、单细胞生物、转基因生物。

normal.en: organism is the living thing; organization is the arranged group.
normal.cn: organism 是活的东西，organization 是安排成的群体。

normal.en: organic describes a quality; organism names the individual.
normal.cn: organic 描述性质，organism 命名个体。

abstract.en: Picture a workshop where every tool has its place and every worker serves the same finished object.
abstract.cn: 想象一间作坊，每件工具都有位置，每个工人服务于同一件成品。

abstract.en: Picture a city that repairs its own roads without anyone giving the order.
abstract.cn: 想象一座自己修补道路、无需谁下命令的城市。

abstract.en: Picture a watch that grows new wheels instead of replacing them.
abstract.cn: 想象一只表会自己长出新的齿轮，而不是更换齿轮。

examples.en: No organism can survive without water for long.
examples.cn: 没有生物能在缺水的情况下长期存活。

examples.en: The pond supports thousands of microscopic organisms.
examples.cn: 这个池塘养育着数以千计的微小生物。

examples.en: The model organism is chosen because its genome is small.
examples.cn: 选择该模式生物，是因为它的基因组很小。

dict_mnemonic.text: organ（器官）+ ism（体系、状态）→ 由器官协同构成的整体 → 生物、有机体

root: 希腊 ergon「工作」→ organon「工具、器官」→ 拉丁 organum → 英语 organ → 十九世纪加 -ism 构成 organism。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all concern an organized living whole: an individual, a microbe, a society, an engineered plant or animal, a laboratory model, an ecological unit, a philosophical whole and a working institution.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都涉及有组织的活的整体：个体、微生物、社会、被改造的动植物、实验室模型、生态单位、哲学整体与运作中的机构。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: many organs working as one body, each part serving the whole.
core.cn: 核心意象：许多器官作为一个身体协同工作，每个部件都为整体服务。

branches.en: THE INDIVIDUAL UNIT: from a whale to a bacterium, one living thing counted as one.
branches.cn: 个体单位：从鲸到细菌，一个活物算作一个。

branches.en: THE INVISIBLE MAJORITY: hygiene and medicine use the word for life too small to see.
branches.cn: 看不见的多数：卫生与医学用这个词指小到看不见的生命。

branches.en: THE SOCIAL METAPHOR: societies and departments are described as bodies whose parts depend on each other.
branches.cn: 社会比喻：社会与部门被描述为部件相互依存的身体。

branches.en: LIFE UNDER DESIGN: engineered organisms and model organisms exist because humans chose and altered them.
branches.cn: 被设计过的生命：转基因生物与模式生物之所以存在，是因为人选择并改动了它们。

branches.en: THE PHILOSOPHICAL WHOLE: against mechanism, the whole explains the parts rather than the reverse.
branches.cn: 哲学整体：与机械论相对，整体解释部件，而不是反过来。

intro.en: Organism is a Greek-derived root with the English suffix -ism: an instrument-root, a suffix of system or state, and later a biological noun.
intro.cn: organism 是希腊来源的词根加英语后缀 -ism：表示器具的词根、表示体系或状态的后缀，后来成为生物学名词。

latinIntro.en: Greek organon reached Latin as organum and produced organ, organic, organism, organize, organization and organelle. The root ergon also underlies energy.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊 organon 以拉丁 organum 进入拉丁语，衍生 organ、organic、organism、organize、organization、organelle；词根 ergon 也支撑 energy。

items.example: The organism responds to light within seconds.
items.exampleCN: 该生物在数秒内就对光作出反应。

items.meaning: of living things; grown without chemicals
items.meaningCN: 生物的；不用化学方式种植的
items.example: Organic matter in the soil feeds the crop.
items.exampleCN: 土壤中的有机物滋养作物。

items.meaning: at the level of the individual organism
items.example: Organismal responses differ from cellular ones.
items.exampleCN: 个体层面的反应不同于细胞层面的反应。

items.meaning: treating the whole as an organized body
items.example: Organismic biology studies wholes, not only parts.
items.exampleCN: 有机体生物学研究整体，而不只是部件。

items.meaning: a body part with a task
items.meaningCN: 承担某项任务的身体部件
items.example: The liver is the largest internal organ.
items.exampleCN: 肝脏是最大的内部器官。

items.meaning: a small structure inside a cell
items.example: The chloroplast is an organelle.
items.exampleCN: 叶绿体是一种细胞器。

items.meaning: to arrange parts into a working whole
items.meaningCN: 把部件安排成可运作的整体
items.example: She organized the files by year.
items.exampleCN: 她按年份整理了文件。

items.meaning: an arranged group or the act of arranging
items.meaningCN: 安排成的群体或安排的行为
items.example: The organization has forty staff.
items.exampleCN: 该组织有四十名员工。

definition_zh: 生物个体的；个体生物层面的；有机体层面的
definition_en: relating to an individual organism as a level of biological organization
core_image: 一只完整的甲虫被放在培养皿旁，旁边还有放大的细胞与整片森林，三张比例尺并排
scene: Organismal biology asks how an entire animal survives, not just how its cells divide.
sceneCN: 这里 organismal 指「个体生物层面的」（第 2 个义项：以完整生物个体为研究层次）；句意：个体生物学研究的是整只动物如何存活，而不只是细胞如何分裂。图中可辨识物件：完整甲虫、细胞放大图、森林比例尺。

pos.zh: 生物个体的；个体生物层面的；有机体层面的（由 organism 加 -al 构成，多用于 organismal biology 等搭配）

senses.title: Of the Individual
senses.titleCN: 生物个体的：以单个活体为单位
senses.definition: relating to an individual living thing
senses.definitionCN: 与单个活的个体有关的
senses.example: Organismal survival depends on finding enough water.
senses.exampleCN: 生物个体的存活取决于能否找到足够的水。
senses.why: Organism plus -al makes an adjective of the individual. The suffix adds no new idea; it simply attaches the noun to whatever is being described, such as survival or health.
senses.whyCN: organism 加 -al 构成「个体」的形容词。后缀并未增添新观念，只是把这个名词挂到所描述的对象上，例如 survival 或 health。

senses.title: The Whole-Animal Level
senses.titleCN: 个体层面的：整体生物这一层
senses.definition: at the level of the complete organism rather than a cell or molecule
senses.definitionCN: 处于完整生物体这一层，而不是细胞或分子层
senses.example: Organismal biology asks how an entire animal survives, not just how its cells divide.
senses.exampleCN: 个体生物学研究的是整只动物如何存活，而不只是细胞如何分裂。
senses.why: Biology is organized in levels: molecule, cell, tissue, organ, organism, population. The adjective names the rung of that ladder, which is why it appears so often in course titles.
senses.whyCN: 生物学按层次组织：分子、细胞、组织、器官、个体、种群。这个形容词命名的正是梯子上的这一级，因此常出现在课程名称里。

senses.title: A Branch of Biology
senses.titleCN: 学科分支的：个体生物学
senses.definition: belonging to the branch that studies whole organisms
senses.definitionCN: 属于研究完整生物体的分支
senses.example: She teaches organismal biology to first-year students.
senses.exampleCN: 她给一年级学生讲授个体生物学。
senses.why: Once the level has a name, it can become a field. Organismal biology sits between molecular biology below and ecology above, and borrows methods from both.
senses.whyCN: 一旦某个层次有了名字，它就能变成领域。个体生物学位于下方的分子生物学与上方的生态学之间，并借用两者的方法。

senses.title: The Unit of Ecology
senses.titleCN: 生态计数的单位
senses.definition: treating a single living thing as the unit of study or count
senses.definitionCN: 把单个活物当作研究或计数的单位
senses.example: Organismal patterns of dispersal shape the whole meadow.
senses.exampleCN: 个体层面的扩散格局塑造了整片草甸。
senses.why: Ecology moves between individuals and populations. The adjective marks the lower end of that scale, where a single life still counts as one.
senses.whyCN: 生态学在个体与种群之间移动；这个形容词标出该尺度的下端，在那里一条生命仍算作一个单位。

senses.title: Developmental Whole
senses.titleCN: 个体发育的：从合子到成体
senses.definition: relating to the development of a whole organism from a single cell
senses.definitionCN: 与整个生物体从单个细胞发育而来有关
senses.example: Organismal development begins with one fertilized cell.
senses.exampleCN: 个体发育始于一个受精细胞。
senses.why: Development turns one cell into an integrated body. The adjective distinguishes that journey from the molecular events that accompany it.
senses.whyCN: 发育把一个细胞变成一个整合的身体；这个形容词把这段旅程与伴随其发生的分子事件区分开来。

senses.title: Whole-Body Response
senses.titleCN: 整体反应的：全身一起应答
senses.definition: belonging to the response of the whole body rather than one organ
senses.definitionCN: 属于全身而非单个器官的反应
senses.example: The organismal response to cold includes shivering and reduced blood flow.
senses.exampleCN: 对寒冷的整体反应包括发抖与血流减少。
senses.why: An organ can react alone, but many reactions only make sense across the whole body. The adjective gathers those scattered events into one subject.
senses.whyCN: 器官可以单独反应，但许多反应只有放在全身才说得通；这个形容词把这些分散的事件收拢成一个主体。

senses.title: Trait of the Whole
senses.titleCN: 个体性状的：属于整体的特征
senses.definition: describing a trait that belongs to the whole organism
senses.definitionCN: 指属于整个生物体的性状
senses.example: Body size is an organismal trait; enzyme speed is not.
senses.exampleCN: 体型是个体性状，酶的反应速度则不是。
senses.why: Some traits exist only at the whole-body level. The adjective sorts them from traits that belong to tissues or molecules, which matters in comparing species.
senses.whyCN: 有些性状只存在于全身层面；这个形容词把它们与属于组织或分子的性状分开，这在物种比较中很重要。

senses.title: Philosophical Individualism
senses.titleCN: 个体主义的：以个体为解释起点
senses.definition: explaining biological facts primarily through the individual organism
senses.definitionCN: 主要通过生物个体来解释生物学事实
senses.example: An organismal view of selection begins with the fate of individuals.
senses.exampleCN: 以个体为起点的选择观，从个体的命运出发。
senses.why: The adjective can mark a stance in theory: start from the individual, not the gene or the group. It is a level choice that carries consequences for how selection is described.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词可以标出一种理论立场：从个体出发，而不是从基因或群体出发。这是一种层次选择，会影响到如何描述选择。

intro.en: Organismal is organism plus -al. Organism itself is a nineteenth-century formation on Greek organon 'tool, instrument'. The adjective is a later, chiefly scientific coinage whose exact first date is uncertain.
intro.cn: organismal 是 organism 加 -al。organism 本身是十九世纪建立在希腊 organon「工具、器具」之上的构词。该形容词是更晚的、主要用于科学的造词，确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: Organon meant 'tool, instrument', and by extension a body organ, since an organ is the instrument of a function. The word supplied Latin organum.
items.cn: organon 意为「工具、器具」，引申指身体器官，因为器官是完成某项功能的工具；该词给出拉丁 organum。

items.en: Organism was coined to name a living body as an organized whole. The exact coiner is uncertain; the word spread with the rise of biology as a discipline.
items.cn: organism 被造出来，用来指作为有组织整体的活体。确切的造词者不确定；该词随生物学成为一门学科而传播。

items.en: Twentieth-century biology formalized levels from molecule to biosphere. Adjectives such as cellular, organismal and ecological were created to name each rung.
items.cn: 二十世纪生物学把从分子到生物圈的层次正式化；cellular、organismal、ecological 这类形容词被造出来，为每一级命名。

items.en: Organismal appears mainly in scientific writing from the twentieth century, above all in organismal biology. Its first citation is not firmly dated.
items.cn: organismal 主要出现在二十世纪的科学写作中，尤其是 organismal biology；其首见书证没有可靠年代。

items.en: English developed two adjectives. Organismal marks the level of the individual; organismic marks the philosophical claim that the whole organizes its parts. The division became standard in the twentieth century.
items.cn: 英语发展出两个形容词：organismal 标出个体这一层次；organismic 标出「整体组织其部分」的哲学主张。这一分工在二十世纪成为标准。

note.en: The first group separates the two adjectives built on organism, which are close but not interchangeable. The second holds near-synonyms that name different levels.
note.cn: 第一组区分建立在 organism 上的两个形容词，它们相近但不可互换；第二组是命名不同层次的近义词。

entries.definition: Marks the view or study that treats the whole as organizing its parts. It is about holism, while organismal is about the level of the individual.
entries.definitionCN: 标出把整体视为组织其部分的那种观点或研究；它讲的是整体论，而 organismal 讲的是个体这一层次。

entries.definition: Means 'of living things' or 'grown without chemicals'. It describes a property and never names a level of organization.
entries.definitionCN: 意为「生物的」或「不用化学方式种植的」；描述性质，从不命名组织层次。

entries.definition: The living individual itself. The adjective attaches to it, so the two cannot occupy the same grammatical slot.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，指活的个体本身；形容词依附于它，因此两者不能占据同一语法位置。

entries.definition: Relating to the entire body. It is the everyday version of the medical and physiological uses of organismal.
entries.definitionCN: 与整个身体有关的；是 organismal 在医学与生理学用法中的日常说法。

entries.definition: Relating to a single entity as distinct from a group. It is broader, since individuals need not be alive.
entries.definitionCN: 与单个实体有关，区别于群体；更宽泛，因为个体不必是活物。

entries.definition: Relating to cells. It is the neighbouring rung below organismal on the ladder of biological organization.
entries.definitionCN: 与细胞有关的；在生物组织层次的梯子上，是 organismal 下面相邻的一级。

entries.definition: Relating to populations and environments. It is the neighbouring rung above organismal.
entries.definitionCN: 与种群和环境有关的；是 organismal 上面相邻的一级。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: organism + -al: the adjective of the individual living thing.
normal.cn: organism + -al：活的个体这一名词的形容词。

normal.en: The family runs organism, organismal, organismic, organic, organ, organelle.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 organism、organismal、organismic、organic、organ、organelle。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the level: organismal biology, organismal level, organismal development, organismal ecology.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出层次：个体生物学、个体层面、个体发育、个体生态学。

normal.en: The ladder runs molecule, cell, tissue, organ, organismal, ecological, biosphere.
normal.cn: 梯子依次是：分子、细胞、组织、器官、个体、生态、生物圈。

normal.en: organismal is a level word; organismic is a holism word.
normal.cn: organismal 是层次词，organismic 是整体论词。

abstract.en: Picture three photographs side by side: a cell, a whole beetle, and the meadow it lives in.
abstract.cn: 想象三张照片并排：一个细胞、一只完整的甲虫，以及它所在的草甸。

abstract.en: Picture a ladder where each rung is studied by a different department.
abstract.cn: 想象一架梯子，每一级都由不同的系所研究。

abstract.en: Picture a doctor asking how the patient feels, not only what one organ shows.
abstract.cn: 想象一位医生询问病人整体感受，而不只看某个器官的指标。

examples.en: Organismal biology bridges molecular detail and ecological pattern.
examples.cn: 个体生物学连接分子细节与生态格局。

examples.en: The study measured organismal, not cellular, responses to heat.
examples.cn: 该研究测量的是整体层面对热的反应，而非细胞层面。

examples.en: Organismal traits such as body size evolve slowly.
examples.cn: 体型这类个体性状演化得很慢。

dict_mnemonic.text: organism（生物）+ al（……的）→ 生物个体的、个体层面的

root: 希腊 organon「工具、器官」→ 拉丁 organum → 英语 organism（十九世纪）→ organismal。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all locate a subject at the level of the individual living thing: its survival, its biological level, its branch of study, its ecological unit, its development, its whole-body response, its traits and its explanatory stance.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都把对象定位在「单个活物」这一层：它的存活、它在生物学中的层次、相关学科分支、生态单位、发育过程、整体反应、个体性状与解释立场。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a cell, a whole beetle and a meadow shown at three different scales.
core.cn: 核心意象：细胞、完整甲虫与草甸，以三种不同比例尺并排呈现。

branches.en: THE INDIVIDUAL AND ITS BODY: survival and whole-body responses belong to one living thing.
branches.cn: 个体及其身体：存活与整体反应都属于同一个活物。

branches.en: THE LEVEL AND THE FIELD: a rung on the biological ladder becomes a named branch and a course.
branches.cn: 层次与领域：生物学梯子上的一级变成具名分支与课程。

branches.en: THE ECOLOGICAL UNIT: a single life counted as one within a population.
branches.cn: 生态单位：在种群中，一条生命算作一个。

branches.en: DEVELOPMENT AND TRAITS: one cell becomes a body, and some traits exist only at that level.
branches.cn: 发育与性状：一个细胞变成一个身体，而有些性状只存在于这一层次。

branches.en: THE EXPLANATORY STANCE: begin with individuals rather than with genes or groups.
branches.cn: 解释立场：从个体出发，而不是从基因或群体出发。

intro.en: Organismal is a noun of organized life with the adjective suffix -al: an instrument-root, a suffix of state, and a suffix of belonging.
intro.cn: organismal 是「有组织的生命」名词加形容词后缀 -al：器具词根、状态后缀与归属后缀。

latinIntro.en: Greek organon, Latin organum, English organism and organismal form one line. The same root gives organ, organic, organize, organization and organelle.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊 organon、拉丁 organum、英语 organism 与 organismal 构成一条线索；同一词根给出 organ、organic、organize、organization、organelle。

items.example: Organismal heat tolerance varies with body size.
items.exampleCN: 个体耐热性随体型而变。

items.example: The organism lives in the leaf litter.
items.exampleCN: 该生物生活在落叶层中。

items.meaning: of the whole as organizing parts
items.example: Organismic theory treats the whole as primary.
items.exampleCN: 有机体论把整体视为首要。

items.example: Organic remains were found in the clay.
items.exampleCN: 黏土中发现了生物遗骸。

items.example: The gill is a respiratory organ.
items.exampleCN: 鳃是呼吸器官。

items.meaningCN: 细胞内的小型功能结构
items.example: Mitochondria are organelles.
items.exampleCN: 线粒体是细胞器。

items.meaning: to arrange into a working whole
items.example: Cells organize into tissues.
items.exampleCN: 细胞组织成组织。

items.example: The organization of the colony follows a strict order.
items.exampleCN: 该群体的组织遵循严格的秩序。

definition_zh: 有机整体的；有机体论的；整体论的
definition_en: treating a whole as an organized body whose parts are explained by the whole
core_image: 一张网被整体提起，每个结点都被同一股力牵动，无法单独取下
