senses.title: The Whole Organizes Parts
senses.titleCN: 有机整体的：整体组织部分
senses.definition: treating a whole as the unit that organizes its parts
senses.definitionCN: 把整体视为组织其各部分的单位
senses.example: Organismic biology treats the whole animal as the unit that organizes its parts.
senses.exampleCN: 有机体生物学把整只动物当作组织其各部分的单位。
senses.why: Organism plus -ic marks a way of seeing: the body is not a pile of parts but an order in which each part has its place. The suffix points to a quality or a school, not to a level.
senses.whyCN: organism 加 -ic 标出一种观看方式：身体不是零件的堆叠，而是一种每个部件都有其位置的秩序。这个后缀指向一种性质或学派，而不是一个层次。

senses.title: Against Mechanism
senses.titleCN: 与机械论相对的
senses.definition: explaining life by whole-organizing principles rather than by machine-like parts
senses.definitionCN: 以整体组织原则、而非机械式部件来解释生命
senses.example: The organismic view rejects the idea that a body is only a machine.
senses.exampleCN: 有机整体观拒绝「身体只是一台机器」的看法。
senses.why: The word is useful mainly as an opponent of mechanistic. Where mechanism builds up from parts, organismic theory begins with the whole and asks what each part is doing for it.
senses.whyCN: 这个词主要作为 mechanistic 的对立面而有价值：机械论从部件往上搭，有机体论则从整体开始，追问每个部件在为难做事。

senses.title: A Biological School
senses.titleCN: 生物学流派的：研究整体的分支
senses.definition: belonging to the biological tradition that studies whole organisms
senses.definitionCN: 属于研究完整生物体的生物学传统
senses.example: Organismic biologists insisted that development cannot be split into separate causes.
senses.exampleCN: 有机体生物学家坚持认为，发育不能被拆成彼此分离的原因。
senses.why: Schools need names. Organismic biology was coined to contrast with approaches that begin at the molecular level, and it carries a claim about where explanation should start.
senses.whyCN: 学派需要名字。organicmic biology 被造出来，是为了与从分子层面出发的路径相对照，它带有「解释应当从哪里开始」的主张。

senses.title: Psychological Holism
senses.titleCN: 有机体心理学的：把心理视为整体
senses.definition: belonging to the psychological approach that treats the person as an integrated whole
senses.definitionCN: 属于把个人视为整合整体的心理学路径
senses.example: Organismic psychology studies the person as a whole rather than as a list of traits.
senses.exampleCN: 有机体心理学研究整体的人，而不是一串特质的清单。
senses.why: Psychology borrowed the word for the same reason biology did: some phenomena only appear when the whole is considered. A trait list can miss how the traits interact.
senses.whyCN: 心理学借用这个词，理由与生物学相同：有些现象只有考虑整体时才出现。特质清单可能漏掉特质之间的相互作用。

senses.title: Development as a Whole
senses.titleCN: 发育整体的：过程不可切分
senses.definition: describing development as one integrated process rather than a set of independent events
senses.definitionCN: 把发育描述为一个整合过程，而非一组独立事件
senses.example: In the organismic account, each stage prepares the conditions for the next.
senses.exampleCN: 在整体论的叙述中，每个阶段都为下一阶段准备条件。
senses.why: If stages depend on one another, no single cause explains the outcome. The adjective marks that dependence, which is why it appears in debates about embryos and about growth.
senses.whyCN: 如果各阶段相互依赖，就没有单一原因能解释结果。这个形容词标出的正是这种依赖，因此它出现在关于胚胎与生长的争论中。

senses.title: Irreducible to Parts
senses.titleCN: 不可还原为部件的
senses.definition: not fully explainable by the separate properties of parts
senses.definitionCN: 不能完全由各部件各自的性质来解释
senses.example: The flock's motion has an organismic quality that no single bird possesses.
senses.exampleCN: 鸟群的运动有一种任何单只鸟都不具备的整体性质。
senses.why: This is the strongest form of the claim: the whole has properties the parts lack. The word then belongs to philosophy of biology as much as to biology itself.
senses.whyCN: 这是该主张最强的形式：整体具有部件所缺乏的性质。此时这个词既属于生物学，也属于生物学哲学。

senses.title: System-Like Coherence
senses.titleCN: 系统式连贯的
senses.definition: showing the coherence of a system whose parts serve one end
senses.definitionCN: 显出各部件服务于同一目的的系统连贯性
senses.example: The city's transport network has an organismic coherence.
senses.exampleCN: 这座城市的交通网络具有一种有机整体式的连贯性。
senses.why: The metaphor travels beyond biology: any system can look organismic when its parts fit together without a visible designer. The tone is admiring but cautious.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻走出了生物学：任何系统，只要各部分在没有可见设计者的情况下彼此吻合，就显得 organismic。语气是赞赏而谨慎的。

senses.title: Resembling a Living Body
senses.titleCN: 像生物体一样的
senses.definition: resembling a living body in its organization
senses.definitionCN: 在组织方式上像活体
senses.example: The old library grew in an organismic way, wing by wing.
senses.exampleCN: 这座老图书馆以一种像生物生长的方式，一翼一翼地扩展。
senses.why: Here the adjective is descriptive rather than doctrinal: it says a thing looks grown rather than built. The comparison is to a body, not to a theory.
senses.whyCN: 这里的形容词是描述性的，而非立场性的：它说某物看起来是「长出来的」而不是「造出来的」。比较的对象是身体，而不是理论。

intro.en: Organismic is organism plus -ic. Organism was coined in the nineteenth century on Greek organon 'tool, instrument'; organismic is a twentieth-century adjective of schools and theories, and its exact first date is uncertain.
intro.cn: organismic 是 organism 加 -ic。organism 于十九世纪建立在希腊 organon「工具、器具」之上；organismic 是二十世纪用于学派与理论的形容词，确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: Organon meant 'tool, instrument', and by extension a body organ. The idea of the body as a set of instruments for the whole is already present in the Greek word.
items.cn: organon 意为「工具、器具」，引申指身体器官。身体作为一整套为整体服务的工具，这一观念已含在希腊词里。

items.en: Organism named a living body as an organized whole. Writers on society soon borrowed it, so the word carried both a biological and a metaphorical load from early on.
items.cn: organism 指作为有组织整体的活体。讨论社会的作者很快借用了它，因此这个词从一开始就同时承载生物学与比喻的双重分量。

items.en: In the twentieth century, biologists who opposed reduction to genes and molecules called their approach organismic biology. The adjective marked a school rather than a level.
items.cn: 二十世纪，反对还原到基因与分子的生物学家把他们的路径称为 organismic biology；这个形容词标出的是学派，而不是层次。

items.en: Psychology adopted the term for approaches that treat the person as an integrated whole. The exact first uses in each field are not firmly dated.
items.cn: 心理学采用该术语，指把个人视为整合整体的路径。它在各领域的确切首见用法没有可靠年代。

items.en: English settled into a division: organismal for the level of the individual, organismic for the claim that wholes organize parts. The two are close relatives but argue different points.
items.cn: 英语逐渐形成分工：organismal 指个体这一层次，organismic 指「整体组织部分」的主张。两者是近亲，却在论证不同的观点。

note.en: The first group separates organismic from the adjective of level and from its doctrinal opposite. The second holds near-synonyms from biology and philosophy.
note.cn: 第一组区分 organismic 与「层次形容词」及其立场上的对立词；第二组是生物学与哲学中的近义词。

entries.definition: Marks the level of the individual organism, as in organismal biology. It names where a study sits, not what it argues.
entries.definitionCN: 标出个体生物这一层次，如 organismal biology；它命名研究的所在层次，而不命名其主张。

entries.definition: Explaining a whole by the workings of its parts as in a machine. It is the standard opponent of organismic in theoretical debate.
entries.definitionCN: 像解释机器那样，用部件的运作来解释整体；在理论争论中是 organismic 的标准对立词。

entries.definition: Means 'of living things' or 'grown without chemicals'. It describes a property and carries no theory of wholes.
entries.definitionCN: 意为「生物的」或「不用化学方式种植的」；描述性质，不携带任何整体理论。

entries.definition: Treating a whole as more than the sum of its parts. It is broader and used outside biology, while organismic keeps the body image.
entries.definitionCN: 把整体视为大于部分之和；更宽泛，可用于生物学之外，而 organismic 保留了身体意象。

entries.definition: Relating to a system as a whole. It is neutral about whether the whole organizes its parts, which organismic asserts.
entries.definitionCN: 与作为整体的系统有关；对「整体是否组织其部分」保持中性，而 organismic 则明确主张这一点。

entries.definition: Combining parts or fields into one account. It stresses the act of joining rather than the primacy of the whole.
entries.definitionCN: 把部件或领域合并为一种说明；强调合并的动作，而不是整体的优先性。

entries.definition: Relating to organisms and their surroundings. It concerns interactions across levels, not the internal organization of one body.
entries.definitionCN: 与生物及其环境的关系有关；关注跨层次的互动，而不是单个身体的内部组织。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: organism + -ic: the adjective of a school that begins with the whole.
normal.cn: organism + -ic：从整体出发的那个学派的形容词。

normal.en: The family runs organism, organismal, organismic, organic, organ, organization.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 organism、organismal、organismic、organic、organ、organization。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the school: organismic biology, organismic psychology, organismic theory.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出学派：有机体生物学、有机体心理学、有机体论。

normal.en: Its opposite is mechanistic: whole-first against part-first.
normal.cn: 它的对立词是 mechanistic：整体优先对部件优先。

normal.en: organismal is where you study; organismic is what you argue.
normal.cn: organismal 说的是在哪一层研究，organismic 说的是主张什么。

abstract.en: Picture a net lifted by one corner: every knot moves, none can be removed alone.
abstract.cn: 想象一张网被一角提起：每个结点都在动，没有一个能被单独取下。

abstract.en: Picture a choir where no single voice makes the chord.
abstract.cn: 想象一个合唱团，没有任何一个声音单独构成那个和弦。

abstract.en: Picture a house that grew room by room instead of being drawn all at once.
abstract.cn: 想象一座房子是一间间长出来的，而不是一次画好的。

examples.en: Organismic approaches ask what a part does for the whole.
examples.cn: 整体取向的方法追问一个部件为整体做了什么。

examples.en: The debate between organismic and mechanistic views is older than genetics.
examples.cn: 整体论与机械论之间的争论比遗传学更古老。

examples.en: Her organismic reading of the novel treats every chapter as one body.
examples.cn: 她对这部小说的有机整体式解读，把每一章都视为同一个身体。

dict_mnemonic.text: organism（有机体）+ ic（……的）→ 把整体当有机体的 → 有机整体的、整体论的

root: 希腊 organon「工具、器官」→ 拉丁 organum → 英语 organism（十九世纪）→ organismic（二十世纪，用于整体论学派）。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all begin with the whole and work downward: the whole organizes parts, opposes mechanism, names a school, shapes psychology, describes development, resists reduction, shows system coherence and merely resembles a body.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都从整体出发向下推：整体组织部分、反对机械论、命名学派、塑造心理学、描述发育、抵抗还原、显出系统连贯，以及仅仅像一具身体。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a net lifted by one corner, every knot moved by the same pull.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张被一角提起的网，每个结点都被同一股力牵动。

branches.en: WHOLE BEFORE PARTS: the body organizes its members, and mechanism is the standing opponent.
branches.cn: 整体先于部件：身体组织其成员，而机械论是长期的对立面。

branches.en: NAMED SCHOOLS: biology and psychology each adopted the word for a whole-first tradition.
branches.cn: 具名学派：生物学与心理学各自采用这个词，指一种整体优先的传统。

branches.en: DEVELOPMENT AS ONE: stages prepare each other, so no single cause explains the result.
branches.cn: 发育为一：各阶段互为准备，因此没有单一原因能解释结果。

branches.en: NO REDUCTION: the whole may have properties that no part possesses.
branches.cn: 不可还原：整体可能具有任何部件都不具备的性质。

branches.en: THE METAPHOR TRAVELS: networks and buildings can look grown rather than built.
branches.cn: 比喻外溢：网络与建筑可以显得是「长出来的」而非「造出来的」。

intro.en: Organismic is a noun of organized life with the adjective suffix -ic: an instrument-root, a suffix of state, and a suffix of quality or school.
intro.cn: organismic 是「有组织的生命」名词加形容词后缀 -ic：器具词根、状态后缀，以及表示性质或学派的后缀。

latinIntro.en: Greek organon and Latin organum supply organ, organic, organism, organismal and organismic. The -ic ending is the same one that turns system into systemic and theory into theoretic.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊 organon 与拉丁 organum 衍生 organ、organic、organism、organismal、organismic。-ic 结尾与把 system 变成 systemic、把 theory 变成 theoretic 的那个后缀相同。

items.meaningCN: 在方法上以整体组织的
items.example: The organismic view treats the whole as primary.
items.exampleCN: 有机整体观把整体视为首要。

items.example: Each organism has its own balance.
items.exampleCN: 每个生物都有自己的平衡。

items.example: Organismal data were collected first.
items.exampleCN: 先收集了个体层面的数据。

items.example: The soil is rich in organic matter.
items.exampleCN: 土壤富含有机物。

items.example: Each organ serves the whole.
items.exampleCN: 每个器官都为整体服务。

items.example: The organelle has its own membrane.
items.exampleCN: 该细胞器有自己的膜。

items.example: The parts organize themselves into a pattern.
items.exampleCN: 各部分自行组织成一个格局。

items.example: The organization of the tissue is visible under the lens.
items.exampleCN: 组织的结构在镜头下清晰可见。

definition_zh: 生物圈；生命层；全球生命支持系统
definition_en: the zone of Earth, including land, water and air, in which living things exist
core_image: 一颗裹着薄薄绿色生命膜的蓝色星球，那层膜比苹果皮还薄
scene: The biosphere is a thin skin on the planet, yet it controls the air we breathe.
sceneCN: 这里 biosphere 指「生物圈」（第 1 个义项：地球上生命存在的整体区域）；句意：生物圈只是这颗行星上薄薄的一层，却控制着我们呼吸的空气。图中可辨识物件：地球剖面、绿色生命层、大气薄层标注。

pos.zh: 生物圈；生命层；全球生命支持系统（通常作单数，带定冠词 the biosphere；也可指其他行星的生命圈）

forms.label: 相关层级名词

senses.title: The Living Zone of Earth
senses.titleCN: 生物圈：地球上生命存在的整体区域
senses.definition: the zone of Earth where living things exist, including land, water and air
senses.definitionCN: 地球上生命存在的区域，包括陆地、水与空气
senses.example: The biosphere is a thin skin on the planet, yet it controls the air we breathe.
senses.exampleCN: 生物圈只是这颗行星上薄薄的一层，却控制着我们呼吸的空气。
senses.why: Greek bios 'life' plus sphaira 'ball' gives 'the life-ball'. The word treats all living things together as one layer of the planet, not as a list of species.
senses.whyCN: 希腊 bios「生命」加 sphaira「球」构成「生命之球」。这个词把所有生物合起来当作行星的一层，而不是一张物种清单。

senses.title: Life on Another World
senses.titleCN: 其他行星的生命圈
senses.definition: the living layer of any planet, real or imagined
senses.definitionCN: 任何行星上真实或想象的生命层
senses.example: A Mars biosphere, if it ever existed, may survive only underground.
senses.exampleCN: 火星生物圈若曾存在，可能只幸存于地下。
senses.why: Once the word means a layer rather than a place, it can be detached from Earth. Planetary science uses it for the total living system of any world.
senses.whyCN: 一旦这个词指「一层」而不是「一个地方」，它就能与地球脱离；行星科学用它指任何世界的整体生命系统。

senses.title: The Ecological Layer
senses.titleCN: 生态学上的生命层
senses.definition: the living layer studied as part of the Earth system
senses.definitionCN: 作为地球系统一部分来研究的生命层
senses.example: Ecologists model the biosphere as one component of the Earth system.
senses.exampleCN: 生态学家把生物圈建模为地球系统的一个组分。
senses.why: Earth-system science splits the planet into spheres: atmosphere, hydrosphere, lithosphere and biosphere. The word then names one box in a diagram of interacting boxes.
senses.whyCN: 地球系统科学把行星分成若干圈：大气圈、水圈、岩石圈与生物圈；此时这个词命名的是相互作用框图里的一个方框。

senses.title: A Sealed Living System
senses.titleCN: 封闭生物圈：人工封闭生态系统
senses.definition: a closed experimental system that contains living things and recycles its materials
senses.definitionCN: 包含生物并循环其物质的人工封闭系统
senses.example: The sealed biosphere lasted only two years.
senses.exampleCN: 那个封闭生物圈只维持了两年。
senses.why: Experiments such as Biosphere 2 borrowed the name for a sealed miniature world. The test is whether life can keep its own conditions without outside help.
senses.whyCN: 生物圈二号一类实验借用了这个名字，指封闭的微型世界；它检验的是生命能否在没有外界帮助的情况下维持自身条件。

senses.title: Life as a Planetary Component
senses.titleCN: 作为行星组分的生命总体
senses.definition: the total living component of a planet, considered as one system
senses.definitionCN: 一颗行星的全部生命组分，被视为一个系统
senses.example: The biosphere and the atmosphere exchange carbon every second.
senses.exampleCN: 生物圈与大气每时每刻都在交换碳。
senses.why: Here the emphasis is on exchange: life is not only inside the environment but helps make it. This sense underlies the idea that life regulates the planet's chemistry.
senses.whyCN: 这里强调交换：生命不只在环境之中，还参与制造环境。这一义项支撑了「生命调节行星化学」的观点。

senses.title: Total Living Support
senses.titleCN: 全球生命支持系统
senses.definition: the whole system that keeps conditions suitable for life
senses.definitionCN: 维持适宜生命条件的整个系统
senses.example: Protecting the biosphere is not the same as protecting a few species.
senses.exampleCN: 保护生物圈并不等于保护少数几个物种。
senses.why: Policy language uses the word for the life-support system as a whole. The shift is from a place to a function: the biosphere is what keeps conditions livable.
senses.whyCN: 政策语言用这个词指整个生命支持系统；重心从「地点」转向「功能」：生物圈是维持条件宜居的那套东西。

senses.title: A Reserve for Life
senses.titleCN: 生物圈保护区：受保护的样板区
senses.definition: an area designated to protect ecosystems and to study them
senses.definitionCN: 为保护并研究生态系统而划定的区域
senses.example: The valley was named a biosphere reserve in 1998.
senses.exampleCN: 该山谷于 1998 年被列为生物圈保护区。
senses.why: International programmes turned the abstract noun into a label on a map. A biosphere reserve is not the whole biosphere but a local sample of it, managed for both use and study.
senses.whyCN: 国际计划把这个抽象名词变成地图上的标记；生物圈保护区不是整个生物圈，而是它的一个地方样本，兼顾利用与研究。

senses.title: The Object of a Science
senses.titleCN: 作为研究对象的全球生态系
senses.definition: the global ecosystem taken as the object of a scientific field
senses.definitionCN: 作为某一科学领域研究对象的全球生态系统
senses.example: Biosphere science connects biology with climate and chemistry.
senses.exampleCN: 生物圈科学把生物学与气候、化学联系起来。
senses.why: A name for a layer can become the name of a field. The word then appears in course titles and journal names, where it marks a scale rather than a single object.
senses.whyCN: 一个圈层的名称可以变成一个领域的名称；此时该词出现在课程名与期刊名里，标出的是一个尺度，而不是单一对象。

intro.en: Biosphere joins Greek bios 'life' and sphaira 'ball, sphere'. It was coined by the geologist Eduard Suess in 1875 and later popularized by Vladimir Vernadsky.
intro.cn: biosphere 由希腊 bios「生命」与 sphaira「球、球体」组成。该词由地质学家 Eduard Suess 于 1875 年造出，后由 Vladimir Vernadsky 推广。

items.en: Bios meant 'life, mode of life'. It appears in biology, biography, biota and antibiotic, though the compound meanings differ in each.
items.cn: bios 意为「生命、生活方式」，出现在 biology、biography、biota、antibiotic 中，但各复合词的含义并不相同。

items.en: Sphaira meant 'ball, globe'. Latin took it as sphaera, and English gets sphere, spherical and the -sphere of atmosphere and hydrosphere.
items.cn: sphaira 意为「球、球体」。拉丁语借作 sphaera，英语由此得到 sphere、spherical，以及 atmosphere、hydrosphere 中的 -sphere。

items.en: Eduard Suess coined Biosphere in 1875 to name the layer of Earth in which life occurs. His word treated life as a stratum comparable to rock or water, a geological rather than a poetic idea.
items.cn: Eduard Suess 于 1875 年造出 Biosphere，用来指地球上生命出现的那一层。他的词把生命视为可与岩石或水相提并论的层，这是一个地质学观念，而非诗意比喻。

items.en: Vladimir Vernadsky developed the concept in the early twentieth century, arguing that life actively shapes the planet's chemistry. His work made the word common in ecology.
items.cn: Vladimir Vernadsky 在二十世纪初发展了这一概念，主张生命主动塑造行星的化学；他的工作使该词在生态学中通行。

items.en: UNESCO's biosphere reserve programme and Earth-system science gave the word a policy and a modelling life. It now names a layer, a global system and a protected area at once.
items.cn: 联合国教科文组织的生物圈保护区计划与地球系统科学赋予该词政策与建模上的生命；如今它同时指一个圈层、一个全球系统与一片保护区。

note.en: The first group separates the neighboring sphere terms and the smaller ecological units. The second holds near-synonyms that name life at global scale.
note.cn: 第一组区分相邻的圈层术语与更小的生态单位；第二组是命名全球尺度生命的近义词。

entries.definition: A large ecological region defined by climate and vegetation, such as a rainforest. The biosphere is the sum of all biomes.
entries.definitionCN: 由气候与植被界定的大尺度生态区域，如雨林；生物圈是所有生物群系的总和。

entries.definition: A community of organisms together with its physical environment. It can be as small as a pond and need not be global.
entries.definitionCN: 生物群落与其物理环境的整体；可以小到一个池塘，不必是全球尺度。

entries.definition: The place where a particular species lives. It is species-specific, while the biosphere is the total living zone.
entries.definitionCN: 某一特定物种生活的地方；它针对物种，而生物圈是全部生命所在的区域。

entries.definition: The gaseous envelope of a planet. It is one of the spheres that exchange matter with the biosphere.
entries.definitionCN: 行星的气体包层；它是与生物圈交换物质的圈层之一。

entries.definition: The global system of life together with its environment. It overlaps with biosphere but stresses the system rather than the layer.
entries.definitionCN: 全球生命与其环境的整体系统；与 biosphere 重叠，但强调系统而非圈层。

entries.definition: All the living things of a region or of Earth. It names the organisms, not the zone they occupy.
entries.definitionCN: 一个地区或地球上的全部生物；它命名生物本身，而不是它们占据的区域。

entries.definition: The Earth or a realm of activity. It is far vaguer than biosphere, which is a defined layer of the planet.
entries.definitionCN: 地球或某个活动领域；比 biosphere 模糊得多，后者是行星上一个被界定的圈层。

entries.definition: The conditions surrounding an organism. It can exclude the organisms themselves, unlike biosphere.
entries.definitionCN: 围绕生物的条件；与 biosphere 不同，它可以把生物本身排除在外。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: bio- 'life' + sphere 'ball': the layer of life on the ball of Earth.
normal.cn: bio-「生命」+ sphere「球」：地球这个球上的生命之层。

normal.en: The family runs biology, biota, biome, biosphere, biospheric, antibiotic, biography.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 biology、biota、biome、biosphere、biospheric、antibiotic、biography。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the use: biosphere reserve, biosphere integrity, terrestrial biosphere, marine biosphere.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出用法：生物圈保护区、生物圈完整性、陆地生物圈、海洋生物圈。

normal.en: The spheres run atmosphere, hydrosphere, lithosphere and biosphere.
normal.cn: 各圈层为：大气圈、水圈、岩石圈、生物圈。

normal.en: The biosphere is the whole; a biome is one large region inside it.
normal.cn: 生物圈是整体，生物群系是其中一个大的区域。

abstract.en: Picture a blue marble with a green film so thin that a fingernail could scrape it off.
abstract.cn: 想象一颗蓝色弹珠，上面覆着一层薄到指甲就能刮掉的绿膜。

abstract.en: Picture a sealed glass ball where the plants must remake the air for the animals.
abstract.cn: 想象一只密封玻璃球，里面的植物必须为动物重新制造空气。

abstract.en: Picture a planet where the rocks breathe because the living layer taught them to.
abstract.cn: 想象一颗岩石也会呼吸的行星，因为生命层教会了它。

examples.en: Carbon moves between the biosphere and the atmosphere constantly.
examples.cn: 碳在生物圈与大气之间不断移动。

examples.en: The biosphere reserve protects both the forest and the village inside it.
examples.cn: 生物圈保护区既保护森林，也保护其中的村庄。

examples.en: No sealed biosphere has yet supported people for many years.
examples.cn: 至今还没有封闭生物圈能多年维持人的生活。

dict_mnemonic.text: bio（生命）+ sphere（球、圈）→ 生命之球 → 生物圈

root: 希腊 bios「生命」+ sphaira「球、球体」→ 1875 年 Eduard Suess 造 Biosphere → 英语 biosphere。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all treat life as a layer or a system: Earth's living zone, another planet's life, an ecological component, a sealed experiment, a planetary actor, a support system, a protected area and a field of study.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都把生命视为一个圈层或一个系统：地球的生命区、其他行星的生命、生态组分、封闭实验、行星行动者、支持系统、保护区与研究领域。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a blue planet wrapped in a green film thinner than an apple's skin.
core.cn: 核心意象：一颗蓝色行星裹着比苹果皮还薄的绿色膜。

chain: ONE BOX IN THE EARTH SYSTEM

branches.en: THE LAYER: a thin zone of life, treated as one component of the planet.
branches.cn: 圈层：薄薄的生命带，被当作行星的一个组分。

branches.en: OTHER WORLDS: the word detaches from Earth and names any planet's living layer.
branches.cn: 其他世界：该词脱离地球，指任何行星的生命层。

branches.en: THE SEALED MODEL: a miniature biosphere tests whether life can recycle its own conditions.
branches.cn: 封闭模型：微型生物圈检验生命能否循环维持自身条件。

branches.en: LIFE AS ACTOR: the biosphere exchanges matter with air and water and keeps conditions livable.
branches.cn: 生命作为行动者：生物圈与空气、水交换物质，并维持条件宜居。

branches.en: NAMES ON MAPS AND IN JOURNALS: the same word became a protected area and a scientific field.
branches.cn: 地图与期刊上的名字：同一个词变成了保护区与科学领域。

intro.en: Biosphere is a scientific compound of two Greek roots: life and ball. It was made in the nineteenth century and needs no further affix to name its object.
intro.cn: biosphere 是由两个希腊词根构成的科学复合词：生命与球。它于十九世纪造成，命名其对象时不再需要别的词缀。

latinIntro.en: Greek bios gives biology, biota, biosphere and antibiotic; Greek sphaira, through Latin sphaera, gives sphere, spherical, atmosphere and hydrosphere. Biosphere sits where the two families meet.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊 bios 给出 biology、biota、biosphere、antibiotic；希腊 sphaira 经拉丁 sphaera 给出 sphere、spherical、atmosphere、hydrosphere。biosphere 正处在两个词族的交会处。

items.meaning: the living layer of a planet
items.example: The biosphere absorbs a large share of our carbon emissions.
items.exampleCN: 生物圈吸收了我们排放的很大一部分碳。

senses.title: A Climate-Defined Region
senses.titleCN: 气候界定的生物群系
senses.definition: a large region defined by its climate and its characteristic plant and animal communities
senses.definitionCN: 由气候及其典型动植物群落界定的大区域
senses.example: The rainforest biome supports more species than any other region on land.
senses.exampleCN: 雨林生物群系所支持的物种数超过任何其他陆地区域。
senses.why: Biome groups places that share a climate and therefore a way of life. It is a classification of regions, not a single place: every tropical rainforest on Earth belongs to one biome.
senses.whyCN: biome 把共享同一种气候、因而共享同一种生活方式的地区归到一起。它是对区域的分类，而不是某一地点：地球上每一片热带雨林都属于同一个生物群系。

senses.title: A Community in Place
senses.titleCN: 某一地区的生物群落
senses.definition: the community of organisms occupying a particular region
senses.definitionCN: 占据某一特定区域的生物群落
senses.example: The island biome is cut off from the mainland by deep water.
senses.exampleCN: 这座岛的生物群落被深水与大陆隔开。
senses.why: The word can point to the living community of one area rather than to a global class. Geography decides which reading is meant, and 'the island biome' is clearly local.
senses.whyCN: 这个词可以指某一地区的生物群落，而不是全球性的类别；地理语境决定取哪一读法，而 the island biome 显然指局部。

senses.title: The Vegetation Belt
senses.titleCN: 植被带：气候对应的植被类型
senses.definition: a broad belt of vegetation determined by temperature and rainfall
senses.definitionCN: 由温度与降水决定的大片植被带
senses.example: Moving north, the biome changes from forest to tundra.
senses.exampleCN: 向北走，生物群系从森林变为苔原。
senses.why: Early ecologists described biomes mainly by their plants, because vegetation is what a traveller sees. Climate is the cause; the plant belt is the visible sign.
senses.whyCN: 早期生态学家主要按植物来描述生物群系，因为植被是旅行者看得见的东西；气候是原因，植被带是可见的标志。

senses.title: A Setting in a Game
senses.titleCN: 游戏中的生物群系：生成区域
senses.definition: a region type in a game or simulation, with its own terrain, plants and weather
senses.definitionCN: 游戏或模拟中具有特定地形、植被与天气的区域类型
senses.example: The game generates a new biome every few hundred metres.
senses.exampleCN: 游戏每几百米就生成一个新的生物群系。
senses.why: Games borrowed the word because their worlds are also divided by climate and vegetation. Here biome means a procedural region, a direct descendant of the ecological sense.
senses.whyCN: 游戏借用这个词，因为它们的虚拟世界也按气候与植被分区；此时 biome 指程序生成的区域，是生态义项的直接后代。

senses.title: A Unit of Mapping
senses.titleCN: 生态区划单位
senses.definition: a unit used to divide a territory into ecological zones
senses.definitionCN: 把一片地域划分为生态区域的单位
senses.example: Conservation plans are drawn at the biome scale.
senses.exampleCN: 保护规划是在生物群系的尺度上绘制的。
senses.why: Planners need units larger than a site and smaller than a planet. The biome fits that gap, which is why the word appears so often in conservation policy.
senses.whyCN: 规划者需要比单个地点大、比整个行星小的单位；biome 正好填上这个空档，因此在保护政策中频繁出现。

senses.title: The Ocean's Regions
senses.titleCN: 海洋生物群系：水体分区
senses.definition: a large marine region defined by depth, temperature and light
senses.definitionCN: 由深度、温度与光照界定的大尺度海洋区域
senses.example: The deep-sea biome receives no sunlight at all.
senses.exampleCN: 深海生物群系完全照不到阳光。
senses.why: In water the defining variables differ: light and depth replace rainfall. The word still names a large region with a characteristic community, so the concept survives the change of medium.
senses.whyCN: 在水里，界定变量不同：光照与深度取代了降水。这个词仍指具有典型群落的大区域，因此概念在更换介质后依然成立。

senses.title: A Modified Biome
senses.titleCN: 受改造的生物群系
senses.definition: a region whose original community has been substantially altered by human activity
senses.definitionCN: 原有群落被人类活动大幅改变的区域
senses.example: The city is now studied as a novel urban biome.
senses.exampleCN: 这座城市如今被当作新型城市生物群系来研究。
senses.why: Once humans dominate a region, ecologists still need a word for it. Adding an adjective such as urban or novel keeps the biome frame while admitting that the community is new.
senses.whyCN: 当人类主导一个区域，生态学家仍需要一个词来指它；加上 urban 或 novel 一类形容词，既保留 biome 框架，又承认群落是新的。

senses.title: A Classroom Category
senses.titleCN: 教学中的生物群系类型
senses.definition: one of the standard types taught in ecology, such as forest, desert or tundra
senses.definitionCN: 生态学教学中讲授的标准类型，如森林、荒漠或苔原
senses.example: Students learn six major biomes before they learn about food webs.
senses.exampleCN: 学生学习六大生物群系之后，才学食物网。
senses.why: Textbooks standardized the list, and the word became a teaching category. The map is simplified, but it gives beginners a way to compare very different regions.
senses.whyCN: 教科书把清单标准化，这个词于是成为教学类别；地图虽被简化，却给初学者提供了比较差异极大区域的办法。

intro.en: Biome joins Greek bios 'life' with the element -ome. It was coined in 1916 by the American ecologist Frederic Clements, but the origin of the -ome element is uncertain.
intro.cn: biome 把希腊 bios「生命」与构词成分 -ome 结合。该词由美国生态学家 Frederic Clements 于 1916 年造出，但 -ome 这一成分的来源不确定。

items.en: Bios meant 'life'. It supplies the first element of biology, biota, biosphere and biome, and its compounds vary widely in meaning.
items.cn: bios 意为「生命」，提供 biology、biota、biosphere、biome 的第一个成分，而各复合词的含义差别很大。

items.en: The second element -ome is usually traced to the Greek suffix -ōma, which forms nouns for masses or results. How exactly it entered biome is uncertain; some writers connect it with the ending of 'genome' or with a sense of 'group'. This is a case of uncertain root: the element is not certainly identified.
items.cn: -ome 这一成分通常追溯到希腊后缀 -ōma，它构成表示「团块、结果」的名词。它究竟如何进入 biome 并不确定；有作者把它与 genome 的词尾联系起来，也有作者认为它表示「群」。此处属于词根存疑：该成分的身份不能确定。

items.en: Frederic Clements proposed biome in 1916 for the largest unit of a plant community shaped by climate. The date is well documented; the exact wording of his first use is less so.
items.cn: Frederic Clements 于 1916 年提出 biome，指由气候塑造的植物群落的最高单位。年代有可靠记载；他首次使用的确切措辞则不那么确定。

items.en: English ecology adopted biome in the following decades, broadening it from plant communities to whole communities of plants and animals.
items.cn: 此后数十年英语生态学采用 biome，并从植物群落扩展到动植物的整体群落。

items.en: Recent use extends biome to ocean regions, urban areas and game worlds. The core test remains the same: a large region with a characteristic community shaped by its conditions.
items.cn: 晚近用法把 biome 扩展到海洋区域、城市地区与游戏世界；核心检验标准不变：一个由自身条件塑造、具有典型群落的大区域。

note.en: The first group separates biome from the larger and smaller units that surround it. The second holds near-synonyms that name regions or communities.
note.cn: 第一组区分 biome 与环绕其上下的大小单位；第二组是命名区域或群落的近义词。

entries.definition: The total zone of life on a planet, the sum of all biomes. It is global, while a biome is one large region inside it.
entries.definitionCN: 行星上生命存在的整个区域，是所有生物群系的总和；它是全球的，而 biome 是其中一个大的区域。

entries.definition: Organisms plus their physical surroundings, at any scale. A biome contains many ecosystems and is defined mainly by climate.
entries.definitionCN: 生物与其物理环境的整体，可在任何尺度；一个 biome 包含许多生态系统，主要按气候界定。

entries.definition: The place where a species lives. It is tied to one kind of organism, not to a whole region.
entries.definitionCN: 某一物种生活的地方；与某一类生物绑定，而不是整个区域。

entries.definition: The community of microbes living in or on a host. It shares the -ome ending but means a microbial group, not a climate region.
entries.definitionCN: 生活在宿主内部或体表的微生物群落；它与 biome 共享 -ome 词尾，但指微生物群，而非气候区域。

entries.definition: A region defined by its ecosystems and geography. It is close to biome but more often used in mapping and conservation.
entries.definitionCN: 由其生态系统与地理界定的区域；接近 biome，但更常用于制图与保护工作。

entries.definition: An older term for a belt of vegetation and animal life defined by climate. It is largely replaced by biome.
entries.definitionCN: 较旧的术语，指由气候界定的植被与动物带；如今大体已被 biome 取代。

entries.definition: A category based on plant form and cover. It is narrower than biome, which includes animals and climate.
entries.definitionCN: 按植物形态与覆盖划分的类别；比 biome 窄，后者还包括动物与气候。

entries.definition: The organisms living together in a place. It names the living part alone, without the climate that defines a biome.
entries.definitionCN: 共同生活在一处的生物；只命名活的部分，不含界定 biome 的气候。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: bio- 'life' + -ome: a large region of life shaped by climate.
normal.cn: bio-「生命」+ -ome：由气候塑造的大片生命区域。

normal.en: The family runs biology, biota, biosphere, biome, microbiome, antibiotic.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 biology、biota、biosphere、biome、microbiome、antibiotic。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the types: rainforest biome, desert biome, grassland biome, marine biome.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出类型：雨林生物群系、荒漠生物群系、草原生物群系、海洋生物群系。

normal.en: The ladder runs ecosystem, biome, biosphere: small, large, global.
normal.cn: 梯子依次是 ecosystem、biome、biosphere：小、大、全球。

normal.en: microbiome looks like a sibling but means microbes on a host.
normal.cn: microbiome 看似同族，实际指宿主身上的微生物群。

abstract.en: Picture a world map coloured by rainfall, each colour holding its own animals.
abstract.cn: 想象一张按降水上色的世界地图，每种颜色都养着各自的动物。

abstract.en: Picture walking north and watching the trees shrink until none are left.
abstract.cn: 想象一路向北走，看树木越来越矮，直到一棵不剩。

abstract.en: Picture a game world where the ground changes colour at an invisible line.
abstract.cn: 想象一个游戏世界，地面在一条看不见的线上突然换色。

examples.en: The desert biome receives less than 250 millimetres of rain a year.
examples.cn: 荒漠生物群系年降水量不足 250 毫米。

examples.en: Climate change is pushing some biomes toward higher ground.
examples.cn: 气候变化正把一些生物群系推向更高的地方。

examples.en: Each biome has its own set of dominant plants.
examples.cn: 每个生物群系都有自己的一套优势植物。

dict_mnemonic.text: bio（生命）+ ome（群、块）→ 一大片生命群落 → 生物群系

root: 希腊 bios「生命」+ -ome（来源不确定，或与希腊 -ōma「团块」有关）→ 1916 年 Clements 造 biome。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all name a large region of life: a climate class, a local community, a vegetation belt, a game setting, a mapping unit, an ocean region, a human-altered region and a textbook category.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都指一片大的生命区域：气候类别、地方群落、植被带、游戏设定、制图单位、海洋区域、被人类改造的区域与教科书类别。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a world map cut into great coloured regions, each with its own vegetation.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张被切成若干彩色大区的世界地图，每区各有自己的植被。

branches.en: CLIMATE AND VEGETATION: temperature and rainfall produce a visible plant belt, and animals follow.
branches.cn: 气候与植被：温度与降水产生可见的植被带，动物随之而来。

branches.en: THE LOCAL COMMUNITY: the same word can name the living community of one island or valley.
branches.cn: 地方群落：同一个词也可指某座岛或某条谷地的生物群落。

branches.en: REPRODUCTION AND TEACHING: games copy the climate logic, and textbooks fix a short list of types.
branches.cn: 复制与教学：游戏复制气候逻辑，教科书固定一份简短的类型清单。

branches.en: THE PLANNER'S UNIT: large enough to matter, small enough to map, in water as on land.
branches.cn: 规划者的单位：大到有意义，小到可制图，在水里与在陆上都适用。

branches.en: THE HUMAN VERSION: cities and farmland become novel biomes once people dominate them.
branches.cn: 人类版本：当人占据主导，城市与农田成为新型生物群系。

intro.en: Biome is a two-element scientific compound: a Greek root for life and a suffix whose origin is not certainly known. It has no internal affix beyond those two parts.
intro.cn: biome 是由两个成分构成的科学复合词：一个希腊「生命」词根，以及一个来源不能确定的成分。除这两部分外，它没有别的内部词缀。

latinIntro.en: Greek bios gives biology, biota, biosphere and biome. The ending -ome also appears in genome and microbiome, but its meaning varies by word, which is why biome's second element is best described as uncertain.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊 bios 给出 biology、biota、biosphere、biome。词尾 -ome 也出现在 genome 与 microbiome 中，但其含义随词而异，因此 biome 的第二个成分最好描述为来源不确定。

items.meaning: a large climate-defined region of life
items.meaningCN: 由气候界定的大片生命区域
items.example: The boreal biome rings the northern hemisphere.
items.exampleCN: 北方针叶林生物群系环绕北半球。

items.meaning: the whole living layer of a planet
items.example: Biomes together make up the biosphere.
items.exampleCN: 各生物群系合起来构成生物圈。

items.meaning: all living things of a region
items.example: The biome's biota is unusually rich.
items.exampleCN: 该生物群系的生物区系异常丰富。

items.example: Ecology is a branch of biology.
items.exampleCN: 生态学是生物学的一个分支。

items.meaning: the microbes of a host or site
items.meaningCN: 宿主或某处的微生物群
items.example: The gut microbiome affects digestion.
items.exampleCN: 肠道微生物组影响消化。

items.example: A biome contains many ecosystems.
items.exampleCN: 一个生物群系包含许多生态系统。

items.example: Biotic factors include predators and food.
items.exampleCN: 生物因素包括捕食者与食物。

items.example: Antibiotic resistance is a growing problem.
items.exampleCN: 抗生素耐药性是一个日益严重的问题。
